He erupted for 11 catches and 157 yards on 16 targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) exiting in the second quarter, Joe Burrow relied heavily on Higgins, as he paced the team in yardage and targets while tying for the lead in receptions. Unfortunately for the Bengals, Higgins sustained an adductor injury in the final minutes of the game, leaving his status questionable for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tee Higgins and the Bengals travel to Baltimore for a divisional clash in Week 7. He caught two of four targets for 22 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Higgins was able to battle through an adductor injury that kept him limited in practices leading up to the contest, and he has now had a bye week for some added rest. He draws a favorable matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 34.1 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 22nd.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: A.J. Brown won't suit up for at least four weeks for the Patriots, beginning in Week 2 against the Steelers, after landing on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins figure to be New England's top three wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: A.J. Brown will continue shaking off some rust when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle injury, Brown amassed 10 targets in Week 6 but finished with just three catches for 27 yards while struggling with drops. With New England's passing game operating at a high level, featuring 10 touchdown passes in three weeks, Brown should have ample opportunity for a breakout performance against a Chicago secondary that's allowing 9.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers face off against the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He had 14 carries for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards during Pittsburgh's overtime victory in Week 6. With Rico Dowdle (toe) back on the field, Warren's opportunities dipped noticeably despite out-touching Dowdle 16-10. He should still handle a larger volume than Dowdle going forward, but managers should certainly temper expectations as long as both backs are healthy. Warren draws a very favorable matchup against a New Orleans defense that ranks dead last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.
outlooksByWeek.6: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Breece Hall has missed three straight games due to a quad injury as the Jets get set to face the Dolphins in Week 7. Braelon Allen has shined during Hall's absence, and should Hall be deemed healthy, it would appear safe to assume he'd be eased back into action. Miami's defense ranks in the middle of the pack against opposing rushers, allowing 4.0 yards per carry and three rushing scores, but five touchdowns through the air to opposing backs. With questionable volume if he returns to action, it's probably wise to wait one more week before deploying Hall.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback. Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jeremiyah Love's second NFL game for the Cardinals will be a tough Week 2 matchup against Seattle. Love was largely held in check by the Chargers in Week 1, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and catching two passes for nine yards, but he did get into the end zone on a five-yard run. He logged six fewer carries and 20 fewer rushing yards than Tyler Allgeier, which isn't ideal for fantasy managers who drafted the rookie with the expectation that he'd be the lead back right off the bat. Even if Love gets a larger share of the workload against Seattle, he could struggle against a defense that held Patriots No. 1 RB Rhamondre Stevenson to 2.8 YPC in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jeremiyah Love is still looking for his first big breakout game heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash in San Francisco. Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jeremiyah Love appears to have ascended to the clear-cut No. 1 RB in Arizona heading into a Week 4 clash versus the Giants. Love handled a career-high 26 touches (21 carries and five catches) this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, compiling 90 yards on the ground and 19 (along with a TD) through the air. Tyler Allgeier was the only other Cardinals RB to log a carry in the contest, and he got just two totes. There could be room for Love to run against the Giants, who are giving up 5.05 yards per carry to running backs, the third-worst mark in the league through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and his status is uncertain for Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit. The rookie running back logged a full workload Week 4 against the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards and one catch for minus-8 yards. Fantasy managers who roster Love will likely keep a close eye on the Cardinals' injury reports throughout the week to get a sense of his odds of playing in Week 5. If he does suit up, Love will face a Lions defense that allowed Carolina RB Chuba Hubbard to rumble for 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jeremiyah Love will look to rebound in Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Love managed just 22 yards on 12 carries against Detroit this past Sunday, and he finished without a catch for the first time as a pro. The rookie continues to lead the Cardinals' ground attack but has managed a meager 3.7 yards per carry through five weeks. The Rams rank 12th in the NFL by giving up 15.5 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jeremiyah Love enters Week 7 with a questionable tag after missing Arizona's Week 6 game against the Rams with an ankle injury. The rookie has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score through five appearances. His 3.7 yards per carry shows room for improvement, though his involvement in the passing game adds fantasy value. Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, creating an attractive matchup if Love returns. However, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight could complicate his workload even if he's cleared to play.

player.seasonOutlook: Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Parker Washington has recorded just 47 receiving yards on eight targets over Jacksonville's last two games after turning 18 targets into 181 yards over the preceding two games. Washington could have an easier time getting back on track in Week 5 if the Eagles are without top cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee). Philadelphia's secondary still has plenty of talent but hasn't been nearly as effective this year, allowing four touchdown catches to WRs after holding the position to six TDs in the entire 2025 regular season. Washington leads the Jaguars in all receiving categories and remains a fantasy WR2 at worst despite the recent hiccup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Egbuka had his most promising game of the 2026 season in the overtime loss to the Steelers, turning a whopping 16 targets into seven receptions for 48 yards and a score. Tampa Bay's offense has struggled without Baker Mayfield (thumb), averaging just 167 passing yards per game since his injury. Despite this, Egbuka has remained productive and could benefit from the potential return of Mayfield in Week 7. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Golden will look to build off another statement performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Golden brought in six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which could have been more if not for a pair of dropped touchdowns. The second-year wideout has now recorded a 30-501-3 receiving line off a team-high 57 targets, and he's already outpaced all of his 2025 output in just six games this season. He'll take on a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashee Rice picked up a minor hamstring strain and was limited to just six snaps in Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Raiders, but coming out of a Week 5 bye, the issue may not cost him any further time. In his first three games of the season, Rice produced a 13-190-1 line on 15 targets, and his volume could increase with speedster Tyquan Thornton out due to an ankle injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the year. Rice could pop for big numbers in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashee Rice wasn't able to get healthy over Kansas City's Week 5 bye, and the wide receiver sat out a Week 6 win over the Chargers due to knee and hamstring issues. His absence didn't significantly affect the offense as Kenneth Walker dominated against the Chargers. In his three full games this season, Rice has produced a 13-190-1 line on 17 targets. If he's able to return in Week 7, he'll have a tough matchup against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.7: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Titans for an interconference clash in Week 7. He was inactive for Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6 due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. Jaleel McLaughlin (9), Audric Estime (9), and Michael Burton (1) handled the backfield responsibilities, with Estime notching his first TD as a Brown. Judkins is averaging 3.0 yards per carry on 73 attempts, and if he's active for Week 7, he'll face a Tennessee defense allowing 20.3 fantasy points per game (13th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season. Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on all three of his Week 4 field-goal attempts, improving to 7-for-8 this season. Houston's excellent kicker could be busy in Week 5 against the Titans, whose nine made field goals allowed are tied for fifth-most in the NFL. Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season for the Texans and remains a high-end starting fantasy kicker for Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense is trending in the wrong direction. The Giants allowed just 18.3 points per game through Week 3 but have surrendered 28.3 points per game across their last three, including 34 to the Saints in Week 6. Meanwhile, the Texans have won two consecutive games after starting 0-4, and Fairbairn has made all nine of his field-goal attempts over the past three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Kelce remains on pace for a bounce-back season coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. Through four games, the veteran tight end is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022, although it's fair to wonder if he can keep that up given his reduced volume, as he's also on track to fall short of 100 targets for the first time since 2014. With Kenneth Walker having rejuvenated the team's rushing game and Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy both capable of handling underneath and intermediate routes, there isn't a clear niche for Kelce to thrive in. He remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, and that should keep his floor relatively high. Kelce will take on a Chargers defense in Week 6 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Travis Kelce wasn't needed much in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching four of five targets for 53 yards. The veteran tight end has slowed down after a fast start to the season, and through five games he's produced a 20-299-2 line on 27 targets while the offense has leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker. Kelce remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, especially while Rashee Rice is sidelined. Kelce faces a tough matchup in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that's allowed the fewest receiving yards in the league to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Jones could be set to share the backfield in Week 7 as the Vikings play the Colts. Jones logged his best game of the season in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye, rushing the ball 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. The veteran could unfortunately now be in store for a shared role again, as position mate Jordan Mason is primed to return from IR, but the two have proven to be productive together in the past. Indy's defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. He'll face an Eagles defense in Week 5 that's allowing 106 rushing yards per game to RBs and just surrendered a pair of late rushing scores to the Rams' Kyren Williams in a Week 4 loss. Tuten and the Jaguars will have a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff Sunday in Week 5 when they face the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bhayshul Tuten remains Jacksonville's starting RB heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans. He has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in four of five games while occupying that role and has two rushing TDs this season. Houston has been among the league's stingiest defenses against RBs, limiting the position to 89 scrimmage yards per game and allowing only three TDs on 103 carries. Tuten's prominent role in an above-average offense keeps him in the fantasy RB2 range despite the tricky Week 6 matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings.
