He'll face another tough challenge in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Courtland Sutton's struggles continued in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran wideout has yet to catch more than three passes in a game this season or reach 50 receiving yards, leaving him with a paltry 13-123-1 line on 28 targets through six games. With quarterback Bo Nix unable to build any momentum, Sutton and the entire passing game offer little upside. He could at least get into the end zone again in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to WRs this season, 31st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain very involved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Vele has been targeted 30 times (second-most on the team) through New Orleans' first four contests this season, logging 226 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns. With Tyler Shough averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game this season, Vele will likely remain a solid fantasy option as the year progresses, at least until the return of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR). However, Vele is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 7.7 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Vele was quiet in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for just 26 yards. He still ranks second on the Saints in targets (36) and receiving yards (252) through five contests, which is a positive sign for his outlook moving forward. Vele could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's already allowed five touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain New Orleans' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Vele has been relatively quiet over the last two weeks, catching seven of 12 targets for 68 yards. Despite this, he's played over 90% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the last two contests, suggesting more fantasy production is coming soon, especially if New Orleans continues throwing the ball at such a high clip (39.2 pass attempts per game -- fourth-most in the NFL). Vele could struggle against a strong Steelers defense in Week 7 though, as they've allowed just 6.1 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive. Miami has been much more favorable against quarterbacks than Tampa so far this season, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. In his second full start of the year, Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards, but he was unable to find the end zone. The veteran quarterback also now holds a 1:2 TD:INT through his three appearances this season, so he'll need to do more for Minnesota to lock him down as a long-term option. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyler Murray will look to keep the Vikings rolling in Week 7 against the Colts. Murray recorded his best game of the season against the Saints heading into Minnesota's bye, completing 80 percent of passes for 229 yards and a touchdown, with 10 rushes for 51 yards. The veteran quarterback could be a dangerous threat moving forward, especially if he can get it going on the ground once again. He'll face an Indy defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 2 matchup versus Miami on the heels of making two field goals in San Francisco's season-opening victory against the Rams. Pineiro's makes came from 20 and 56 yards out, though he also missed a 52-yarder. The veteran kicker made a career-high six FGs from 50-plus yards out last year, so San Francisco is clearly comfortable relying on his leg from that distance. The 49ers could put up plenty of points in Week 2, as the Dolphins just gave up 27 points to Las Vegas in a Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Eddy Pineiro remains a solid fantasy kicker option heading into the 49ers' Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal Sunday against the Dolphins, but he converted all five of his extra-point tries. San Francisco has averaged 31.0 points per game through two weeks, so Pineiro figures to see frequent opportunities to kick, though that won't always result in field-goal chances. Arizona's opponents have attempted just one FG through two weeks, but the Cardinals gave up a hefty 31 points to Seattle in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Eddy Pineiro will look to get his consistency back on track for San Francisco in Week 4 versus the Broncos. Pineiro missed a pair of extra-point tries Sunday in a win over Arizona, but he also nailed a 57-yard field goal. The veteran kicker hadn't previously struggled with PATs, making all eight over his first two games of the campaign, so his erratic boot may have just been an aberration. Denver has yielded eight field-goal attempts and seven extra-point tries through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Eddy Pineiro's leg could be key for the 49ers in Week 5 versus Seattle in a battle of tough defenses. Pineiro has been mostly asked to kick extra points this season, making 14 of 16 PAT tries while attempting just six field goals (and making four of them). He missed a 54-yard try against Denver this past Sunday, though it was blocked by the Broncos. There may not be many opportunities for Pineiro against the Seahawks, who are giving up the fifth-fewest points (18.3) in the league this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Eddy Pineiro enters a Week 6 tilt against Washington coming off hitting a game-winning field goal for San Francisco this past Sunday. The veteran kicker missed a 52-yard attempt in that contest, but he atoned for that with a 44-yard make that ended up being the deciding score. Pineiro is now 5-for-8 on FG attempts this season, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. He could see plenty of chances against the Commanders, who are allowing the third-most points (29.8) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Eddy Pineiro and the 49ers are back on the road for a meeting with the 2-4 Falcons in Week 7. He converted his only field-goal attempt but went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Pineiro has been underwhelming despite playing for a 49ers team that scores 29.5 points per game, which is the third-most in the league. He's now 6-for-9 (66.7%) on field goals and 19-for-22 (86.4%) on PATs, and he hasn't attempted more than two FGs since the season opener. Pineiro should remain on fantasy waiver wires with more reliable options available at the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Kamara had his best game of the 2026 campaign in a Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for 69 yards and a touchdown on nine touches. Despite this, he logged just 18 offensive snaps, which is fewer both than Kendre Miller (31) and CJ Donaldson (22). Kamara dealt with an injury in the first half, but with Miller receiving 20 carries, it appears as if Kamara's upside is limited, operating primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the Cowboys for a Week 3 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on both PATs during Baltimore's 24-17 loss in Week 2. Loop's first attempt from 49 yards was blocked, but he followed up by making his second attempt from the same distance. He should have plenty of opportunities to score in what's expected to be a high-scoring contest versus Dallas inside the AT&T Stadium dome in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Loop and the Ravens return home to square off against the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was perfect again in Baltimore's dramatic 34-31 victory in Brazil in Week 3, making both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winning kick as time expired, and all four of his extra points. Loop is now 5-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-11 on extra-point tries in 2026. The Ravens are fifth in scoring at 30.7 points per game, so he should continue earning plenty of opportunities for one of the best offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Loop and the Ravens pay a visit to the surging Falcons for a Week 5 interconference clash on Sunday Night Football. The second-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three PATs during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. Loop missed his second field goal of the season but set a new career high with his make from 64 yards out, and he's now 6-for-8 on field goals and a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points. Atlanta has scored the most points in the league over its last two games (80), meaning Loop and the Ravens will have to keep up in a potential high-scoring game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Loop and the Ravens travel to square off against the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory in Week 5. Two of Loop's makes came from 50-plus yards, and he's now 5-for-5 on kicks from that distance this season and 9-for-11 on field goals overall. He's turning into a very reliable fantasy asset for a Ravens team that scores 29.2 points per game, making him a strong play against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Loop and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals for a Week 7 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Through six contests this season, Loop is 10-for-13 (76.9%) on field goals and a perfect 16-for-16 on extra-point tries. He has three outings with 100% accuracy and three with 50% accuracy, making him an inconsistent fantasy option despite kicking for a Ravens offense that scores 26.0 points per game, which ranks seventh so far in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre Tucker was fairly quiet in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching two of four targets for 27 yards. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, project to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Tucker isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre Tucker produced his first ceiling game of 2026 in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. churning out a 5-119-1 line on seven targets. The volatile wideout is showing some early chemistry with new quarterback Kirk Cousins, and no one else has yet shown any indication that they'll be able to challenge him for the top spot on the depth chart, even if Tucker's skill set would be better suited for a WR2 or even WR3 role. Tucker will try to build on last week's effort in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre Tucker remains in the top spot on the Raiders' wide receiver depth chart, but he's a boom-or-bust option. After popping for a big game in Week 2, Tucker fell back to a 4-43-0 line on just four targets in a Week 3 win over the Saints. With Las Vegas off to a 3-0 start, changes in the offensive mix aren't likely, but Tucker simply doesn't have the physical tools to consistently get open and win 1-on-1 matchups in the NFL. Another rare ceiling game is unlikely in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre Tucker handled a season-high eight targets in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, but he turned them into just four catches for 44 yards. The fourth-year wideout has reached 50 receiving yards only once in four games to begin the season, producing a 15-233-1 line on 23 targets. With a healthy Brock Bowers back as Kirk Cousins' No. 1 option, Tucker's chances of another ceiling game have shrunk. He'll face a Patriots secondary in Week 5 that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre Tucker has hauled in at least four passes in four straight games as the Raiders' top wide receiver, although he plays a clear second fiddle to tight end Brock Bowers in the passing game. Tucker has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in three of those games, and his only touchdown came during his Week 2 eruption against the Chargers. The fourth-year wideout will have a ceiling game once in a blue moon, but his weekly floor is low, at least while Kirk Cousins remains under center instead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker will try to get enough volume to take advantage of a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tre Tucker continues to build chemistry with Kirk Cousins. The Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver hauled in two touchdowns in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, and through six games Tucker has produced a 24-371-3 line on 35 targets, putting him on pace for his first 1,000-yard effort. Tight end Brock Bowers remains the top option in the passing game, and Tucker has yet to record more than eight targets in a game in 2026. The prospect of Fernando Mendoza replacing Cousins under center at some point offers additional uncertainty for Tucker. He'll have a hard time delivering another ceiling game in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Paris to take on the Saints in Week 7. He caught two of three targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime in Week 6. Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each played 71% of snaps on offense, but it was the latter who made the bigger impact in this one, as Washington tallied a 4-25-1 line on six targets. Freiermuth will try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that just surrendered six receptions for 99 yards and a TD to Isaiah Likely.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bo Nix didn't show any improvement in Week 5 as the Broncos switched back to Sean Payton as their play-caller, throwing for a season-low 123 yards and producing just one touchdown in a win over the Chargers. The third-year QB has a meager 6:3 TD:INT through five games and is completing fewer than 60.0% of his passes, averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. There's still reason to believe Nix's numbers will improve once Payton gets back in a rhythm, but the Denver offense's ceiling seems limited even if it's operating at peak efficiency. Nix isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks defense that ranks sixth this season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bo Nix continues to struggle, failing to throw a touchdown in Week 6 for the first time this season while compiling a season-low 107 passing yards. The third-year quarterback has produced fewer than 6.0 yards per attempt in four straight games, and the Broncos' switch back to Sean Payton as the play-caller hasn't yet sparked the offense. Nix has just seven total touchdowns (six passing and one rushing) against five turnovers through seven games, but he'll get a chance to build some momentum in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 30 targets from Titans QB Cam Ward over the past four games. Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll loved peppering Robinson with short targets when they were together on the Giants, and Daboll has maintained that philosophy in their new surroundings. Robinson has caught 19 of those 30 targets for 151 yards and two TDs, and his consistent involvement in Tennessee's offense gives him a respectable floor as a solid Week 7 flex option against the Browns, who are giving up 157 yards per game to WRs and have allowed seven TDs to the position through six games. Robinson and QB Cam Ward are the only Titans with multiple TDs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. The 30-year-old was Tampa Bay's second-most productive wideout in the Week 1 loss, hauling in all four of his targets for 40 yards. Godwin likely won't have many big plays after sustaining multiple serious lower-body injuries throughout his career, but he should remain a reliable PPR option and an important part of the Buccaneers' offense moving forward. Additionally, he's in for a great Week 2 matchup, as the Browns defense allowed 13.6 yards per target to WRs in Week 1, the second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Godwin had a quiet Week 3 performance (3-25-0), though he had an 85-yard touchdown reception called back for holding. The veteran wideout has struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's offense, and those struggles could be amplified with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined for the Week 4 contest. However, Godwin is in for a favorable matchup against a Packers defense that's allowed 6.7 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top weapons in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Godwin was targeted a season-high seven times in the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching six of them for just 31 yards. The veteran wideout may actually benefit from Jalon Daniels acting as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback while Baker Mayfield (thumb) is sidelined, as Godwin could act as the rookie's safety blanket. Additionally, Godwin is in for a good Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs through four contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Godwin is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top safety blanket in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Godwin has caught 19 of 22 targets this season, totaling 179 yards. Despite ranking second on the Buccaneers in receptions and third in targets, he's gotten just one red-zone target all season and could struggle finding fantasy relevance without a touchdown. Regardless, Godwin is in for a tough Week 6 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up 220.8 passing yards per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin was targeted a season-high eight times during the Week 6 loss to the Steelers, recording four receptions for 37 yards. The veteran wideout ranks second on Tampa Bay in targets (30), receptions (23) and yards (216) through the first six games and could benefit from the potential return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Week 7. However, Godwin is in for a tough matchup against a Panthers secondary that's allowed just 5.9 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Godwin is on the comeback trail after injuries have limited him to 16 games during the past two seasons. In 2025, he appeared in nine games and reached 11 fantasy points only twice. It seems like a long time ago, Godwin was second among receivers in fantasy points in 2024 when he suffered a severe ankle injury. He wasn't nearly as effective when he was on the field last season, but he's now more than a full year recovered from the injury and has less target competition with Mike Evans no longer on the roster. Entering his age-30 season, Godwin's days as a fantasy WR1 may be over, but with Emeka Egbuka as his only competition to lead the team in targets, he certainly has a path to flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Allgeier heads into a Week 2 clash against Seattle with a big role in Arizona's backfield. Allgeier logged 17 carries for 61 yards in a season-opening win against the Chargers, getting more totes and producing more yards than rookie Jeremiyah Love. It remains to be seen if that will hold true throughout the campaign, but for the time being Allgeier seems set to be heavily involved in the Cardinals' ground game. With that said, both Allgeier and Love could find the sledding tough in Week 2 versus a Seahawks defense that yielded the third-fewest rushing yards per game during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Allgeier seems to have fallen well behind Jeremiyah Love for ball-carrying opportunities heading into Arizona's Week 4 matchup with the Giants. Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Allgeier may be lined up for a big role for Arizona in Week 5 against the Lions. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury, and if he can't suit up Sunday, Allgeier will likely lead the team's backfield. Even with Love healthy for nearly the entire game in Week 4, Allgeier posted good production, recording an 8-42-1 rushing line and two catches for seven yards. The Cardinals' RB group could find success against a Lions defense that is giving up 4.64 yards per carry to running backs, eighth-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's backfield seems to be fading ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Allgeier logged just three carries for seven yards this past Sunday against Detroit while adding nine yards on two catches. The veteran running back has logged three or fewer totes two of the past three weeks and seems to be far behind rookie Jeremiyah Love, who got 12 carries versus the Lions, in the pecking order. With that said, he could get some opportunities as a pass catcher against the Rams, who have given up the fourth-most receiving yards per game (42.6) to running backs through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Allgeier could continue handling a significant share of Arizona's backfield workload in Week 7 against Denver, regardless of whether Jeremiyah Love remains sidelined with an ankle injury or returns after a one-game absence. Allgeier has rushed 53 times for 157 yards and a touchdown through six games, but he's averaging just 3.0 yards per carry, so he needs to be more efficient when he gets the ball. Bam Knight's emergence adds another obstacle to consistent fantasy production. However, Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, so Allgeier should have flex appeal if he has an expanded role for a second consecutive week.

player.seasonOutlook: Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kirk Cousins went down swinging in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, setting season highs with 52 pass attempts and 365 yards while throwing multiple TDs for a fourth straight game to begin the season. While rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza waits in the wings, Cousins' 11 touchdowns are tied for the league lead, and he sits just outside the top 10 in passing yards and completion rate, which should give him plenty of job security. The veteran quarterback will try to keep rolling in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kirk Cousins' production is declining, potentially reducing his time as the Raiders' starting quarterback. After throwing for nine touchdowns during the team's 3-0 start to the season, the veteran has a 3:1 TD:INT over the last two contests, both losses. During a lopsided Week 5 loss to the Patriots, Cousins ceded the final drive to prized rookie Fernando Mendoza, which could be the first step toward Mendoza taking the reins. Cousins' job doesn't seem to be in immediate peril, and he could bounce back in a big way in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kirk Cousins is coming off a productive effort in the Raiders' near-upset of the Bills in Week 6, throwing for over 300 yards for the second time in six games and tossing multiple TDs for the fifth time. The veteran quarterback is on pace for his first 4,000-yard, 30-TD campaign since 2021 with the Vikings, but to reach those numbers he would need to keep first overall pick Fernando Mendoza on the bench, which looks increasingly unlikely after three straight losses for Las Vegas. Cousins will remain under center for now, but he faces another tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that is second in the league in passing yards per game allowed.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).
outlooksByWeek.6: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He threw for 235 yards (22-for-31) with three TDs and no INTs while rushing once for six yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. That's three straight weeks that the 42-year-old has tossed three scores, and he now has a 10:4 TD:INT through five games this season. Rodgers looks to stay hot versus a stingy Buccaneers defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points allowed to QBs (18.4 per game).
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Saints. He threw for 253 yards (33-for-49) with two TDs and one INT while rushing once for minus-one yard during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime. Rodgers led four straight scoring drives to send the game to OT after the Steelers trailed 16-3 to start the fourth quarter. He now owns an 11:4 TD:INT over his last four outings, and he'll face a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dominic Zvada connected on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Giants. Zvada made all four of his PATs during the 28-20 win for the G-Men over the Dallas Cowboys. He did not attempt a field goal for the game. In Week 2, Zvada and company will face a Rams squad that was surprisingly suspect in its season opener. Los Angeles allowed 27 points to the 49ers in a losing effort last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dominic Zvada accounted for the only points for the Giants last game. Zvada connected on both of his field goals in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The injury to Jaxson Dart leaves Jameis Winston under center at quarterback, which could be an ugly development in terms of opportunities for points for Zvada. In Week 3, the Giants will face a Titans squad allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dominic Zvada provided all of the offense last game for the New York Giants. Zvada connected on all four of his field goal attempts in the 12-7 triumph over the Titans. Zvada has yet to miss a field goal through three games, and could see additional opportunities in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals are allowing 27 points per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dominic Zvada continues to shine for the Giants as a rookie. Zvada made all three of his field goals, as well as an extra point, in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Two of Zvada's field goals were from 50-plus yards out. He is perfect to begin his NFL career, with five field goals already from 50-plus yards away. He could be primed for a big output in Week 5 versus a Commanders squad allowing 30.5 points per tilt, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dominic Zvada had an afternoon to forget last game for the Giants. The rookie missed three kicks in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders. Coming into the game, Zvada had not missed a single boot. However, he subsequently missed three field goals from 40-plus yards out. While the conditions were rather poor and the missed attempts were long, Zvada did also hit two other  tries from 50-plus yards away, as well as all three of his extra points. Despite the rough outing, Zvada should remain the kicker in Week 6 versus the Saints. New Orleans is allowing 30.2 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league, so Zvada should get plenty of chances for redemption.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dominic Zvada rebounded from a poor performance with two field goals and an extra point last game for the Giants. Zvada connected on two field goals from inside 50 yards, as well as one PAT, in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. With essentially one bad game to his name, Zvada should continue as the primary placekicker for the G-Men. In Week 7, New York will face a Texans squad allowing 23.8 points per tilt, which is 20th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
