outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Ferguson found the end zone again for the Cowboys last game. Ferguson caught three passes for 23 yards and the touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Ferguson has three touchdowns over his last two contests, all coming within the red zone. However, Ferguson has yet to gain even 45 yards in a single outing, making him a touchdown-dependent option in Week 4 versus the Texans. Houston has yielded five touchdowns through three tilts, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Ferguson had a two-game scoring streak snapped for the Cowboys. Ferguson managed three catches for just 11 yards in the 34-30 win over the Texans. Ferguson has just 12 catches for 83 yards through the first four games of the season, though has scored three times over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jake Ferguson saw a season-high six targets last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which likely contributed to the additional looks for other players, including Ferguson. However, Ferguson managed three catches for just 19 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Ferguson back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Ferguson continues to struggle to find his place in the Dallas offense. Ferguson managed just two catches for 13 yards in the dismal 23-13 loss to the Packers. Ferguson has been held out of the end zone in three-straight games, and has failed to gain even 20 yards receiving in any of those contests. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Terry McLaurin missed last game for the Commanders due to a hamstring injury. McLaurin allegedly pushed hard to play, though, meaning he could very well return to the field in Week 5 versus the Giants. He also could have his starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. New York has been stingy against the pass in 2026 thus far, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. Likewise, the G-Men are tied for the league-lead with six picks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Gainwell has operated as Tampa Bay's top receiving back over the last two weeks, getting more targets (six), receptions (five) and yards (32) than Bucky Irving (two catches on three targets for 10 yards). Despite this, Gainwell will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without scoring a touchdown. He could thrive against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed 200 receiving yards to RBs through five contests, tied for the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Gainwell was given few opportunities in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, accumulating 24 total yards on just three touches. Additionally, Gainwell was on the field for just 15% of Tampa Bay's offensive plays, his lowest mark of the season. It appears as if Gainwell is trending toward receiving less work as the season progresses, but he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed 5.1 yards per carry this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeMario Douglas hasn't emerged in the Patriots' receiving corps ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Despite A.J. Brown's continued absence, Douglas has just four total catches over the last three weeks, tallying 62 yards. An uptick in volume appears unlikely against an exploitable secondary that allows 8.2 yards per target, leaving Douglas as a dart throw as opposed to a reliable lineup option.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeMario Douglas faces an uphill battle to match Week 5's success when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. Douglas shined with two touchdowns and a season-high 65 yards against the Raiders, but he's still hauled in no more than two balls in three of five outings while being held to 38 yards or fewer in his first four games. New England is spreading the ball around in its surging passing attack, so Douglas seems unlikely to retain heavy volume. The Jets have allowed four opposing receivers to register 63 yards or more in the last two weeks, giving Douglas a shot at some upside.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeMario Douglas is emerging as a viable option for the Patriots ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. Over the past two weeks, Douglas has garnered 13 targets, turning them into 11 catches and three touchdowns. Though A.J. Brown is back from an ankle injury, New England could be without Romeo Doubs due to a shoulder ailment, suggesting Douglas' place in the receiving pecking order may be unchanged, giving him a chance to post solid numbers against a secondary that's allowed nine opposing receivers to gain at least 55 yards.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matt Gay missed his first kick of the season in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, pinging the upright on a field goal attempt from 48 yards out. He's still having a strong season, converting all 11 of his PATs and going 11-for-12 on FG attempts, including his only attempt from 50-plus yards. Gay has benefited from a surprisingly potent offense under Kirk Cousins, but the veteran QB may be reverting to his usual level, perhaps opening the door for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take the reins, so it's not necessarily bad news for Gay's long-term outlook. Gay will take on a Bills team in Week 6 that's allowing 28.2 points per game, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matt Gay stayed busy in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, going a perfect 3-for-3 on both field goal attempts and extra points. The veteran kicker has benefited from the team's offensive resurgence under new head coach Klint Kubiak, and Gay sits third in scoring in the NFL behind the Colts' Spencer Shrader and the Bills' Tyler Bass. Gay will face a Rams team in Week 7 that's allowed 23.0 points per game, tied for 17th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker didn't get many chances to hit the scoreboard in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, converting both his extra points but failing to see a field-goal attempt. The team's offense didn't quite look in sync yet under new coordinator Mike McDaniel, and top wideout Ladd McConkey was knocked out of the game early with a rib injury, so scoring drives could be tough to come by for the club in the short term. Dicker will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Raiders team that finished 25th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cameron Dicker has had a shaky start to the season as the Chargers struggle to put points on the board. The fifth-year kicker has seen just five extra points in three games, converting all five, and he's connected on just three of five FG attempts, with all three makes coming in a Week 3 loss to the Bills. That volatility isn't fantasy-friendly, and until the team's skill players begin to get the hang of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, Dicker's volume is likely to remain limited. He probably won't be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Seahawks team allowing just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cameron Dicker's volume increased for a second straight week in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs. While the team's offense continues to struggle, Justin Herbert is at least putting together longer drives, and during those two contests Dicker has gone 6-for-7 on FG tries with all of his attempts coming from inside 50 yards. He likely won't be able to squander many chances in Week 5 against a Broncos team allowing 23.5 points per game, 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cameron Dicker's opportunities continue to be inconsistent due to the struggles of the Chargers' offense. The kicker hasn't attempted more than two PATs in any of the team's first five games, going a perfect 9-for-9, and he's seen one or fewer field goal attempts in three of those five contests. With the offensive line in shambles and Justin Herbert running out of healthy targets, Dicker's volume doesn't seem likely to pick up anytime soon. He'll face a Kansas City squad in Week 6 that's allowing 19.3 points per game, seventh in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence and caught two of five targets for 16 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Pittman tied for second on the team in targets but was unable to make much of an impact, as Aaron Rodgers continued spreading the ball around on offense by hitting nine different receivers. However, he has an opportunity to break out against Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more effective as the Packers play the Jets in Week 2. While Lloyd was the leading rusher for Green Bay in Week 1, he still only totaled 37 yards on 13 rushing attempts. Fellow ball carrier Chris Brooks also recorded seven carries for 29 yards, so the margin between the two doesn't appear to be too large. Lloyd will look to do more with his opportunities against a New York front that should be less menacing than Minnesota's.
outlooksByWeek.3: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more efficient as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Lloyd scored his first career touchdown off a six-yard catch in Week 2, but he also rushed six times for just 20 yards. The inexperienced running back has now averaged just 3.0 YPC off 19 carries this season, which is far from what Green Bay is looking for out of its RB1. Lloyd will also face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a top-10 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make his job even harder.
outlooksByWeek.4: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to turn things around as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Lloyd continued his disappointing season against the Falcons in Week 3, rushing four times for 11 yards and catching two of three passes for seven yards. While the inexperienced running back was hindered by a pass-heavy game script, he's still averaged just three yards per carry across 23 attempts and seen his offensive snap share decrease in each of his first three games. He'll also face a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs this year, making him a very risky play.
outlooksByWeek.5: MarShawn Lloyd remains in the mix of Green Bay's backfield ahead of Week 5 against Chicago. Lloyd remained extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 4, rushing the ball seven times for 13 yards, but he did salvage his performance with five catches for 36 yards. The second-year running back looks to be in direct competition with Kaleb Johnson for carries as of late, but the Packers have utilized Lloyd in different ways even when Johnson has been more effective. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed (4.73) to RBs this season, which could give Lloyd the opening he needs to do more as a rusher.
outlooksByWeek.6: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be Green Bay's primary option in the running game again versus the Cowboys in Week 6. Lloyd put together his best fantasy performance of the year versus the Bears in Week 5, recording 10 carries for 31 yards and two touchdowns along with one catch for six yards. The second-year ball carrier has totaled 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 40 carries and caught 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score across the first five games of the campaign. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: MarShawn Lloyd could be in line for a smaller role as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Lloyd was extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 6 against the Cowboys, rushing eight times for 10 yards and logging three fewer carries than position mate Pierre Strong. Lloyd is also now set to share the backfield with a reinstated Josh Jacobs, which could further limit his opportunities. Detroit has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Due to a variety of injuries, Lloyd has appeared in one game since being selected in the third round of the 2024 draft. Now healthy, he appears to have a hold on No. 2 RB duties in Green Bay, which is notable with Josh Jacobs facing a potential suspension. Lloyd is likely to open the season on the RB2/flex radar and should be on your radar in the middle rounds, though note that he'll fade back to no more than an insurance stash once Jacobs returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keenan Allen has caught 11 of 18 targets for 108 yards and a TD in his last two outings for the Colts, sandwiched around a Week 4 absence due to a groin injury. The 34-year-old wideout has stepped up in the absence of WR Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Allen lacks Pierce's ability to stretch the field, but a steady diet of short targets should put Allen back into the flex mix in Week 6 against a Titans defense that ranks among the 10 most generous units in terms of catches and yards allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Keenan Allen has turned back the clock over his past three appearances for the Colts, securing 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards and a TD over that span while drawing at least nine targets in every game. The 34-year-old wideout should continue to fill a high-volume role in a Colts WR room that lacks appealing alternatives in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Allen is a high-floor fantasy WR3 in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing 10 catches for 133 yards per game to WRs. Minnesota's aggressive blitz packages will likely force the Colts into plenty of the quick and short throws on which Allen thrives.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Thomas has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last two games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has played fewer than 50% of snaps on offense while being outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers. Thomas is too talented to overlook completely, but he's a risky flex option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London. The matchup would become more favorable if Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) sits. Philadelphia is allowing 162 receiving yards per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brian Thomas is coming off a Week 5 goose egg against the Eagles and has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last three games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has a snap share below 50% this season heading into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to defend WRs, allowing 193 yards per game to the position, but Thomas isn't a trustworthy fantasy option despite the favorable matchup given his recent struggles. Unless you are desperate for a bye-week plug-in in a deeper format, Thomas should be left on the bench if not dropped outright.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendre Miller could operate as the Saints' No. 2 running back if Alvin Kamara (knee) remains sidelined for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Miller was surprisingly involved in New Orleans' Week 1 gameplan, tying Travis Etienne for the most carries on the team while finding the end zone. Despite averaging only 3.3 yards per carry, Miller could have a similar role if Kamara remains out for Week 2. It's also a favorable matchup for running backs, as the Ravens defense allowed 5.2 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendre Miller is expected to split carries with Alvin Kamara in the Saints' Week 4 matchup  against the Falcons, with Travis Etienne (hamstring) out. Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendre Miller is likely to remain one of the Saints' top rushers while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is out during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Miller received the second-most carries (six) on New Orleans in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons but was largely ineffective, averaging just 1.5 yards per carry. Even if Miller continues splitting work with Alvin Kamara, he likely won't have much fantasy value, as the Saints' offense is averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game. Additionally, Miller is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 307 rushing yards all season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kendre Miller is expected to remain a large part of the Saints' rushing attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Miller operated as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, receiving more carries (six) and targets (three) while playing more snaps (13) than Alvin Kamara (three carries and two targets on 12 snaps). While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller appears to have assumed the role as the Saints' top rusher. He could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 21.3 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kendre Miller appears to have emerged as the Saints' top running back ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller has taken over as New Orleans' primary rusher, logging 22 touches and 70 total yards in the Week 6 win over the Giants. Additionally, Miller played a season-high 46% of the Saints' offensive snaps, which is partially due to Alvin Kamara's injury in the first half, but still remains a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Miller could struggle in Week 7, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 4.0 yards per carry this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.6: Dameon Pierce was the last running back standing for the Eagles last game. Will Shipley started the game and found the end zone early for the Eagles, but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. Pierce could start against the Panthers, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Saquon Barkley's place last game for the Eagles.  Pierce also caught four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley cannot suit up in Week 7 due to his balky hamstring, Pierce would be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his PATs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the team's current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Bates logged his best game of the season in Week 4 against the Panthers, nailing all four of his field-goal attempts and converting two XPAs. The second-year kicker has now gone a perfect 21-for-21 on boots (seven field goals, 14 extra points) this season. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Bates will look to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, nailing eight field-goal attempts and converting all 20 of his XPAs across five games. While the field-goal usage hasn't quite been there, the touchdown-scoring ability of Detroit's offense has kept Bates on the field. He'll face a Green Bay squad that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (4.2) to kickers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Washington's volume continues to be steady for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He hauled in five of QB Malik WIllis' nine completions in Week 4, his fourth-straight week with at least five targets while increasing his yardage in each of the last three outings. Cincinnati's secondary hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 63 yards, and while Washington's workload shouldn't be questioned, his potential remains capped by Miami's low-scoring offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Washington brings a steady workload but limited yardage potential into the Dolphins' Week 7 matchup with the Jets. Washington has commanded at least five targets in all five games, three times reaching eight or more, but has topped out at 67 yards, operating mainly on short, slot routes while Miami struggles to find a vertical passing game. The Jets are allowing just 7.3 yards per target; Washington too is averaging 7.3 yards per target, setting him up for a rather predictable Week 7 outing where he'll need a heavy target share to offer anything more than bye-week replacement scoring.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Herbert struggled in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards and one touchdown with one interception, while adding 29 rushing yards on five carries. Injuries along the offensive line were once again an issue for the club; the interior of the line, with rookie Jake Slaughter at center, wasn't able to hold up, and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel didn't seem to have many answers. Ladd McConkey also suffered a rib injury in the game, which could make things even more difficult for Herbert if the top wideout misses any time. Herbert will look to rebound in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season with Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator. Through two games, he's completed less than 60% of his passes with a 2:3 TD:INT ratio and barely over 200 passing yards per game. Ladd McConkey was his only reliable target in the Chargers' opener, but the third-year wideout was limited by a rib injury in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and no one else stepped up. As in years past, Herbert's protection has also been decimated by injuries. An offensive line that was already missing starting center Tyler Biadasz was down to a third-string left guard against Las Vegas in Week 2, and the team also lost its two best blocking tight ends, Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, over the course of that contest. Herbert could be in for another long day in Week 3 against a Bills defense that has seven sacks through two games, tied for fourth in the league, but which has been vulnerable through the air when the opposing QB has found some time.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The veteran quarterback has yet to throw multiple touchdowns in a game this season, while his 59.1% completion rate would be a career-worst mark. Herbert is also dealing with his usual protection issues and has been sacked eight times in three contests, a pace that would see him get brought down more than 40 times for a third straight year. His top target, Ladd McConkey, should be healthier as he puts a rib injury further behind him, but as yet none of his other pass catchers have made any kind of impact. Herbert's rough year could get worse in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 28-year-old quarterback posted season lows with 189 passing yards and 6.1 yards per attempt in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. Through four games, he has a career-low 59.7% completion rate and a weak 4:6 TD:INT. An ineffective running game, along with injuries to the offensive line and his wide receiver corps, have contributed to the team's 0-4 start, but Herbert has been the focal point of the offense's woes. He'll try to turn things around in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain, and which ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Justin Herbert and the Chargers remain winless after a Week 5 loss to the Broncos, as their season spirals down the drain. Injuries have once again gutted the offensive line, with left tackle Rashawn Slater joining center Tyler Biadasz on IR, but offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel also doesn't seem to have any answers. Herbert has posted a career-low 59.4% completion rate and 6.6 yards per attempt through five games with a woeful 5:7 TD:INT, and now his top four wide receivers, along with tight end David Njoku, are all injured. Herbert doesn't seem likely to turn things around in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Herbert enters his seventh NFL season following a solid 2025 campaign in which he ranked just inside the top 10 quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns. Herbert added serious value with his legs, ranking fifth at the position in carries and second in rushing yards (career highs in both). He finished 10th among quarterbacks in fantasy points, but that's a bit misleading, as his inconsistent production led to five top-five weeks but no other finishes better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and 15th in fantasy points per game in each of the past four seasons, though it's fair to expect a leap forward in 2026 with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater healthy and a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel. Herbert is safest as a QB2, but there's upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Makai Lemon caught three passes for 19 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon was third on the team in targets with six, though the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Lemon's upside as well.  In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of them.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathon Brooks is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Brooks received just four carries in the Week 1 loss, which is fewer than Chuba Hubbard (10) and AJ Dillon (five). However, all of Dillon's work came when the Panthers were down substantially in the fourth quarter. Brooks showed flashes of brilliance when on the field, most notably on a 48-yard catch and run. He could continue to take work from Hubbard as the season continues. However, he's in for a tough Week 2 matchup, with Atlanta allowing just 2.8 yards per rush attempt in Week 1, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. Brooks will likely to find fantasy relevance if active in Week 3, with Cleveland's defense allowing just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season.
