Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches with Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he quickly earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role. Consider him in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.
outlooksByWeek.7: Omar Cooper brings momentum into the Jets' Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle issue, Cooper flashed with 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. The Jets remain a low-volume passing attack, and Miami has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, but Cooper provides a big-play option, averaging 19.0 yards per catch in limited action. He could offer a high-upside bye-week fill-in.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Robinson is expected to continue operating as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 win over the Packers, rushing 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has managed to be extremely efficient when given opportunities, averaging 4.6 yards per touch. He's also in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's given up 4.8 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Robinson is expected to remain involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson had his best game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, accumulating 67 yards on 15 touches while scoring three touchdowns. The Alabama product has now logged double-digit carries in three straight games, suggesting that he's established himself as a valuable portion of this Falcons offense. Expect Robinson to remain Atlanta's No. 2 running back behind Bijan Robinson in a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Baltimore defense that's given up just 3.8 yards per carry to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson was ineffective in the Week 5 overtime loss, accumulating just 16 yards on seven carries (2.3 yards per carry). Through five contests this season, Robinson has averaged 42 rushing yards per game, with most of his value coming from touchdowns (four on the season). He could struggle in Week 6 against a Bears defense that's given up just 409 rushing yards to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson was held to just three touches during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, mostly because of the Falcons large deficit early in the game. On the season, Robinson has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns while catching five of six targets for an additional 30 yards. He could struggle finding the end zone in Week 7, however, as San Francisco's defense has given up just three total touchdowns to RBs through five games.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam Darnold suffered a soft-tissue glute injury in Seattle's season-opening win and isn't likely to play in Week 2 against Arizona. As a result, Drew Lock is in line to guide the Seahawks' offense. Darnold isn't expected to miss significant time and could be back as soon as Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam Darnold has a chance to return from a glute injury for Seattle's Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. It remains to be seen if the veteran QB will be able to suit up, but he reportedly has been ahead of schedule in his recovery. With Darnold out against Arizona in Week 2, Drew Lock took over and led the Seahawks to a win. Whichever signal-caller starts under center in Week 3 could feast upon a Washington defense that has allowed a 137.0 passer rating this season, the worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam Darnold seems to be past the glute injury that cost him some early-season action heading into Seattle's Week 4 tilt against the Chargers. Darnold returned from a one-week absence to throw for 379 yards and four touchdowns (albeit with two interceptions) in a Week 3 win against Washington. The veteran QB continued to look often to star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who logged a massive 10-128-2 receiving line on 14 targets. The Chargers have given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, 11th-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam Darnold will look to lead Seattle to victory in a key NFC West clash versus San Francisco in Week 5. Darnold threw for a modest 168 yards and was picked off once against the Chargers in Week 4, but he tossed two touchdowns and guided his team to a win. After playing only five snaps over the first two weeks due to a glute injury, Darnold looks to be back to full health and has posted a 6:3 TD:INT over the Seahawks' past two games. He could face a stiff challenge against the 49ers, who have yielded only three passing TDs through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Sam Darnold will look to bounce back from a rough performance when Seattle visits Denver in Week 6. Darnold was picked off twice this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, and he threw for a modest 195 yards with one touchdown. He now has an uninspiring 7:5 TD:INT through four games after recording the third-most pickoffs (14) among NFL quarterbacks during the regular season last year. The Broncos don't figure to offer much relief, as they've yielded the fifth-best passer rating (79.4) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sam Darnold and the Seahawks host the Chiefs for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He completed 27 of 51 pass attempts for 278 yards with no TDs and two INTs while rushing twice for 19 yards. Darnold has now thrown four interceptions over his last two outings while taking five sacks in each, giving him seven INTs in five games this season. It could be another rough night for Darnold in Week 7 against Kansas City's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (16.3) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Darnold's first season with the Super Bowl champion Seahawks couldn't have gone much better from a real-life standpoint, but it simply didn't translate to much fantasy success. Despite finishing fifth in the NFL in passing yards for the second season in a row, Darnold finished 27th in fantasy points per game. He was very boom or bust, delivering seven top-10 weeks but also nine finishes outside the top 20. Turnovers (15 INTs were second most in the NFL) and a lack of rushing were the culprits. The 29-year-old will have a new playcaller in Brian Fleury, but otherwise it's roughly the status quo offensively. Darnold is no more than a fringe QB2 with a limited ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Dell (knee) is expected to have his practice window opened ahead of the Texans' Week 5 road game against the Titans. The 2023 third-round pick hasn't played since sustaining a significant knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell is currently on injured reserve and will likely take some time to ramp up. He's unlikely to return in Week 5 against Tennessee, but forward-looking fantasy managers should take notice of Dell's impending return, as he averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to his injury.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day return window opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans and has rejoined his teammates at practice but remains on injured reserve ahead of the team's Week 6 trip to London to face the Jaguars. Considering the Texans just traded for WR Marvin Harrison, Dell seems unlikely to be a major contributor in Week 6, even if he is activated from IR. Dell isn't viable in Week 6 but could be worth stashing if you have an open bench or IR slot, as Houston's 2023 third-round pick averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to sustaining a major knee injury late in the 2024 season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day window to return from IR opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, and he has a realistic chance of being activated ahead of the Week 7 home game against the Giants after sitting out against the Titans in Week 5 and the Jaguars in Week 6. Even if Dell suits up in Week 7, he's likely to be brought along slowly in a Texans WR room that also has Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for playing time. Dell is a viable bench stash, but he isn't a recommended starting option against the Giants.

player.seasonOutlook: Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Schultz was second on the Texans in targets behind Nico Collins during the season opener, which matched Schultz's usage last season. After being thrown to eight times in Week 1 against a Bills defense that allowed the fewest yards in the NFL to TEs last season, Schultz is poised for a hefty Week 2 workload against a Bengals defense that surrendered the most yards to his position in 2025. Schultz's role and matchup make him a top-10 fantasy TE for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Schultz paced the Texans with 12 catches for 140 yards on 14 targets in the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati, working as C.J. Stroud's top target in the absence of WR Nico Collins (hamstring). The veteran TE is the favorite to lead the team in targets if Collins sits in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most yards and TDs in the NFL this season. Indianapolis just allowed nine catches for 101 yards and a TD to Chiefs TE Travis Kelce in Week 2. Schultz is locked in as a fantasy TE1 for Week 3 if Collins sits and has a strong argument to stay in that range even if Collins suits up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Schultz is coming off a disappointing 30-yard outing in Week 3 against the Colts, but he'll remain a fantasy TE1 in Week 4 against the Cowboys if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game. Schultz had 12 catches for 140 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 85 receiving yards per game since Collins got hurt. The Cowboys have struggled to defend TEs, allowing three TDs while forcing only two incompletions on 19 passes to the position. If Collins returns, Schultz will maintain fantasy starter-level upside but with a lower floor due to dropping a spot in the pass-catching hierarchy.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Schultz has recorded just 39 yards in two games since his 140-yard outburst for the Texans in Week 2. He's back to working as a supporting piece in Houston's passing game now that Nico Collins has recovered from a hamstring injury. The 30-year-old TE's inconsistent workloads keep him from being a reliable fantasy starter, and Schultz will be tough to trust in Week 5 against a Titans defense that's holding his position to 27 receiving yards per game, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Schultz leads the Texans with 24 catches heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Jaguars in London, though half of those receptions came in Week 2 against the Bengals. Jacksonville has been among the five stingiest defenses against TEs, limiting the position to 3.6 catches for 34 yards per game. The Jaguars have allowed two TDs to the position, but Schultz has scored only five times in 39 regular-season games since the start of the 2024 season and is still searching for his first TD of the season. Despite Schultz's respectable target volume, he's best left on the bench in single-TE formats in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dalton Schultz has exceeded 35 receiving yards just once through Houston's first six games of the season and has yet to score a TD heading into a Week 7 home game against the Giants. He's a secondary option in a Houston passing game that has gotten more production out of its WRs in recent weeks, and Schultz's lack of red-zone involvement compared to other middling TE options makes him an unappealing fantasy play. The Giants have limited TEs to two TDs this season, so Schultz is best left on the bench or waivers since his TD drought is unlikely to end in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Schultz has been one of the league's most consistent tight ends over the past six years, but with the exception of one season, he hasn't been overly useful in fantasy. Schultz was fantasy's No. 3 tight end in scoring while he was in Dallas in 2021, but he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight campaigns (that includes exactly 10th in three of the past four seasons). In 2025, Schultz ranked sixth or better at the position in targets, catches and yards, but he found the end zone only three times and has now cleared five touchdowns once in his career (eight in 2021). Schultz is a reliable target for QB C.J. Stroud, but with Houston's depth at wide receiver, he simply doesn't offer much upside. Consider him a low-ceiling TE2.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keon Coleman doesn't appear to have a meaningful role in the Bills' offense entering Week 2 against the Lions. Despite playing 52% of the team's offensive snaps, Coleman drew only one target, which resulted in a one-yard catch. Always a candidate for an end-zone jump ball, Coleman is no better than fourth in the target pecking order, suggesting he's unlikely to contribute despite an inviting matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keon Coleman will look to build on a mild breakout when the Bills face the Chargers in Week 3. He hauled in six passes last week, his highest total since Week 1 of 2025, as the Bills lost DJ Moore (shoulder) early in Week 2. The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Patriots. Dealing with a Week 3 ankle injury, Coleman caught a 37-yard pass on two targets, a significant decrease in volume with DJ Moore healthy. Moore dominates targets and Buffalo is a run-first offense. Facing a defense that's allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target, there may not be enough opportunities for Coleman to contribute.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains unsettled ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. DJ Moore exited Week 4 after aggravating a shoulder injury that forced a similar result in Week 2, and Coleman again shined. In the two games with Moore leaving early, Coleman has 12 catches on 13 targets for 179 yards and a touchdown. With Moore playing four quarters, Coleman has two catches for 38 yards. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards leaves Coleman as a fantasy risk regardless of Moore's status.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keon Coleman brings inconsistent volume in the Bills' passing game into a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Coleman saw just two targets in Week 5 despite the absence of DJ Moore, marking the third time in five outings he's drawn that limited amount of volume. Buffalo remains a run-first offense and while Coleman has shown red zone and downfield ability, the lack of consistent volume leads to volatility against a Las Vegas secondary that's allowing the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts, though has been more vulnerable over the middle of late than to boundary receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: So far, so bust for Coleman, who has struggled to make an impact after being selected 33rd overall in the 2024 draft. After flashing in a situational deep-threat role as a rookie (15.0 aDOT), Coleman saw more high percentage looks in 2025 (11.2 aDOT). That led to a much better catch rate (from 51% to 66%), but a big dip in yardage (19.2 YPR to 10.9). Coleman has yet to emerge as a reliable, full-time starter and was even a healthy scratch at times last season. Perhaps the 23-year-old will make a Year 3 leap with Joe Brady now running the show, but he'll have his hands full overtaking DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart. Coleman is only worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashid Shaheed should continue to operate in a versatile role for Seattle in a big Week 5 battle against San Francisco. Though Shaheed had just one catch for 20 yards versus the Chargers in Week 4, he added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while also returning kickoffs and punts. The 49ers have a similarly versatile player in Deebo Samuel, and the pair of Swiss-army-knife wideouts could be keys in what figures to be a battle of tough defenses. San Francisco has allowed just 17.0 fantasy points per game to WRs this season, sixth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashid Shaheed has been a relatively quiet contributor to Seattle's passing game heading into a Week 6 tilt in Denver. Shaheed has caught three or fewer passes in all of the Seahawks' games so far this season and has yet to record a receiving touchdown, though he does have rushing score on his ledger. The speedy wideout has a big role as an electric kick returner, but Shaheed may struggle to produce as a pass catcher as long as Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to eat up targets. The Broncos are giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (16.3) to wideouts this season, but they could be without both starting cornerbacks -- Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) -- in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashid Shaheed and the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 when the Chiefs pay a visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught five of eight targets for 66 yards while rushing once for two yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6. Shaheed also compiled 77 yards on three kickoff returns and another 39 yards on three punt returns, but he fumbled twice while only losing one. He finished second on the Seahawks in yardage, tied with Cooper Kupp for second in receptions, and was third in targets. Shaheed will look to build on that performance versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches on offense to be worth considering in fantasy against Denver's stout defense in Week 2. He had one target and one carry in Jacksonville's season opener, which he turned into 11 scrimmage yards across four snaps on offense while playing primarily on defense. Hunter played both wide receiver and cornerback at Colorado before being drafted second overall by the Jaguars in 2025. With WRs Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers ahead of him, the versatile Hunter is currently more useful to the Jaguars on defense, much to the chagrin of his fantasy managers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Hunter didn't have a target or carry in Week 2 and has played only a handful of snaps on offense for the Jaguars this season. He's off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, outside of IDP formats that reward Hunter's contributions as a cornerback. Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers should continue to lead Jacksonville's wide receiver room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense in either of Jacksonville's last two games heading into a Week 4 trip to Cincinnati. The 2025 second overall pick has been playing almost exclusively on defense, so Hunter's off the fantasy radar in formats that don't count individual defensive statistics. He's trending up as a cornerback after intercepting Drake Maye in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots.
outlooksByWeek.5: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense for the Jaguars since Week 1. He played every defensive snap in Week 4 and is focusing primarily on playing cornerback rather than wide receiver. Hunter is a fantasy non-factor except in formats that reward his defensive contributions. Jacksonville will face the Eagles in Week 5 in London, where Hunter showcased his upside on offense last season with eight catches for 101 yards and a TD against the Rams. Don't expect a repeat performance anytime soon, if ever.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Hunter got his first offensive touch since Week 1 during the Jaguars' Week 5 win over the Eagles, but he's being used as a full-time defensive player while barely seeing the field on offense. Barring a rash of injuries at wide receiver, the Jaguars will likely remain content using Hunter primarily at cornerback. He has enough talent to warrant a bench stash if you have space on the roster, but he isn't an appealing fantasy option in Week 6 against the Texans unless your league counts defensive contributions.

player.seasonOutlook: Full-time focus on defense should unlock rewarding production from a unique talent. Not only can Hunter mirror receivers, he frequently turns his head to track the ball, leading to big plays in coverage.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Mayer was busy in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, turning a season-high 10 targets into eight catches for 82 yards. The additional volume came after wide receiver Jalen Nailor left the game with a concussion, forcing Kirk Cousins to lean even more heavily on his tight end duo of Mayer and Brock Bowers to move the chains. Even with a healthy Bowers back in action the last two weeks, Mayer has delivered an 11-114-1 line on 13 targets. However, he'll struggle to maintain that pace in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Mayer's volume took a significant step backward in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After turning 10 targets into an 8-82-0 line in Week 4, Mayer got only one look from Kirk Cousins in New England, turning it into a two-yard gain. Brock Bowers is the unquestioned top option in the team's passing game, but a lack of established wide receivers has created an opening for Mayer to be more than just injury insurance. Through five games, he's delivered a 21-171-1 line on 25 targets, putting him on pace for career-best numbers in 2026. Mayer will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Mayer took advantage of the extra defensive attention the Bills paid to Brock Bowers in Week 6, catching seven of nine targets for a season-high 95 yards. While Bowers remains the top option in the Raiders' passing attack, Mayer is on pace for a career-best year of his own, producing a 28-266-1 line on 34 targets through six games. He is eight receptions and 63 yards away from establishing new personal bests. Mayer will likely struggle to reach those marks in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quentin Johnston wasn't able to get much going in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching just two of his six targets for 17 yards. The entire passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel wasn't yet in rhythm aside from Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey isn't able to play in Week 2, Johnston could be the biggest beneficiary when it comes to additional volume from Justin Herbert. Johnston will face a Raiders secondary in Week 2 that was tied for 21st in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quentin Johnston has struggled through the Chargers' first two games, catching just three of 11 targets for 24 yards. The fourth-year wideout had emerged as a deep option over the prior two seasons, but new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme is built on quick passes and yards after the catch, giving little time for Johnston's typical downfield routes to develop. Tre' Harris and rookie speedster Brenan Thompson both seem better suited to that style of passing game, and Johnston runs a real risk of becoming an afterthought as the season progresses. He does at least get a potentially favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quentin Johnston could be in danger of losing his spot as the Chargers' No. 2 wide receiver. The 2023 first-round pick leads the team with 17 targets through three games, but that volume has resulted in just a 6-64-0 line, and Johnston has been unable to take advantage of Ladd McConkey's limitations due to a rib injury. Second-year WR Tre' Harris did in Week 3, suggesting he could be about to move past Johnston in the pecking order. Johnston will have a hard time building any momentum in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quentin Johnston saw only two targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but he was able to turn one of them into a 44-yard gain for his only catch. The season-low volume was especially disappointing given that Ladd McConkey left the game early with a foot injury. The passing game as a whole is struggling, and Johnston could end up getting passed on the depth chart by Tre' Harris if he doesn't begin to make a more consistent impact. Johnston will try to earn more look from Justin Herbert in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quentin Johnston was unable to play through a chest injury in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, missing his first game of the season. The fourth-year wideout has just a 7-108-0 line on 19 targets in four contests, and the team's offensive struggles under coordinator Mike McDaniel have dragged down essentially every skill player on the roster. If Johnston returns in Week 6, it will be for a brutal matchup against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Four weeks into the 2025 season, it appeared Johnston was on the verge of a breakout campaign. The 2023 first-round pick found the end zone four times and scored 14-plus fantasy points in each game during the span. The return to earth was abrupt, as Johnston went on to average 9.2 PPG in his final 10 games. The 25-year-old has posted consistent receiving lines in each of the last two seasons (55-724-8 and 51-735-8), but neither resulted in a top-30 fantasy campaign. The Chargers offense should be better in 2026 with a healthy line and Mike McDaniel calling plays, but Johnston is unlikely to see a big boost in usage with the likes of Ladd McConkey and sophomores Tre Harris and Omarion Hampton also in the fold. Johnston is no more than a boom/bust flex in deeper leagues.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.2: Dontayvion Wicks made his presence felt in his Eagles debut in Week 1. Wicks reeled in two passes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the 24-22 win over Washington. Only Dallas Goedert had more receiving yards than Wicks for the game. Wicks also notched four targets in his premiere for the Birds. In Week 2, Wicks will face a dismal Titans defense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing scores a season ago, which was tied for 23rd in the NFL
outlooksByWeek.3: Dontayvion Wicks continues to cement himself as the No. 2 wideout in the Eagles offense. Wicks caught five passes for 74 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Wicks was second on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury, and with Dallas Goedert also banged up, Wicks could be one of the chief beneficiaries.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dontayvion Wicks had his first subpar game of the season for the Eagles. Wicks had five targets but caught just two passes for 32 yards in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Wicks had a crucial drop en route to being held under 73 yards receiving for the first time in 2026. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dontayvion Wicks was expected to operate as the No. 1 wideout for the Eagles last game due to the injury to DeVonta Smith. Unfortunately, Philadelphia's offense was stymied, and Wicks managed three catches for just 18 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Smith appears unlikely to play in Week 5 versus the Jags, so Wicks should continue to play a prominent role in the offense. However, it was Darius Cooper who scored twice last game, and rookie Makai Lemon outpaced Wicks in both targets as well as receiving yards. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dontayvion Wicks led all Eagles wideouts in targets last game. Wicks was targeted eight times en route to five catches for 63 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Wicks, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dontayvion Wicks caught two passes for 24 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon had just four targets overall, as the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap the upside for Wicks as well. However, in Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyjae Spears had five touches to Tony Pollard's eight in Tennessee's season-opening loss. Heading into a Week 2 home game against the Eagles, the Titans once again look like one of the NFL's worst offenses. Given Spears' role as a supporting piece in Tennessee's low-octane offense, he's tough to trust as anything more than a low-end deep-league flex play. Spears has exceeded 50 scrimmage yards three times in 14 appearances since the start of last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyjae Spears is likely to see a handful of touches as usual for the Titans behind Tony Pollard in Week 3, but that projected usage is enough for Spears to earn flex consideration in deeper formats against a Giants defense that has struggled to defend RBs. The Giants just allowed at least 92 scrimmage yards apiece to the Rams' backfield duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but the Rams boast one of the league's most talented offenses and led the league with 30.5 points per game last season, while the Titans are averaging 15.0 PPG after scoring 16.7 PPG last season. Spears can make big plays happen in space, as he showed in compiling 70 yards on nine touches in last week's loss to the Eagles, though he had just 24 yards on five touches in the season-opening loss to the Jets.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyjae Spears was limited to three touches for the Titans in Week 3 while playing through an ankle injury. Even if he heals up ahead of a Week 4 trip to Baltimore, Spears is unlikely to crack double-digits in touches while filling his customary change-of-pace role behind Tony Pollard. The Ravens have been middling against the run but have limited RBs to just 12 receiving yards per game, so Spears is unlikely to earn much Week 4 fantasy lineup consideration outside of super-deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyjae Spears has been limited to three touches in each of Tennessee's Week 3 and Week 4 games while playing through an ankle injury. Typically, his total is in the high single digits, but Spears' injury concerns, coupled with Tennessee's struggles on offense (13.8 points per game), make the change-of-pace RB a fantasy non-factor ahead of a Week 5 home game against the Texans, who are allowing just 3.5 yards per carry. Tony Pollard should continue to get the majority of opportunities in Tennessee's backfield.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyjae Spears had a season-high 11 touches, including nine catches, in Tennessee's Week 5 loss to the Texans. His contributions as a receiver give Spears some deep-league flex appeal for Week 6 against a Colts defense that's allowing a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to running backs. Tony Pollard remains the top backfield option in a low-octane Titans offense that's scoring a league-low 11.6 points per game, while Spears has only one game with more than 28 scrimmage yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyjae Spears exceeded three touches in only one of the Titans' last four games while playing through ankle and knee injuries. He can be an effective pass-catcher out of the backfield when at full strength while spelling starter Tony Pollard, but Spears hasn't provided much production while banged up. Another quiet performance from Spears is likely forthcoming in Week 7 against a Browns defense that has allowed just one TD to running backs all season, so he isn't a recommended fantasy play, even in deeper formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenyon Sadiq could have an emerging role for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Sadiq notched four touches in his NFL debut, including a three-yard rushing score, out-gaining starter Mason Taylor handsomely in a run-heavy game for the Jets. They'll likely need to throw more to keep up with Green Bay's offense in Week 2, and the Packers allowed a touchdown to a tight end last week. The floor is volatile, but Sadiq offers high ceiling potential for those in need at tight end.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenyon Sadiq could struggle to build on a breakout performance in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. After recording just six targets in his first two games, Sadiq shined in Week 3, catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, despite playing just 56% of the offensive snaps in Mason Taylor's absence. The Bears have not allowed an opposing tight end to top 30 yards this season, with teams finding more success targeting their corners, so a repeat performance may be challenging.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenyon Sadiq faces an unsettled role in the Jets' limited passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. After a Week 3 breakthrough performance, Sadiq failed to record a catch on four targets in Week 4 and now has 21 or fewer yards in three of his first four games. The Browns haven't allowed an opposing tight end to top 51 yards while surrendering just 6.7 yards per target, not boding well for Sadiq in Week 5. A potential Mason Taylor return would further dampen Sadiq's potential.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenyon Sadiq will need to clear the league's concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. After a breakout Week 3 performance, Sadiq has just two catches for three yards (seven targets) over the last two games. New England struggled against Brock Bowers in Week 5 but had previously not allowed more than 32 yards or a touchdown to opposing tight ends. With Geno Smith not throwing a plethora of passes, Sadiq has minimal fantasy allure. Mason Taylor would elevate if Sadiq sits.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenyon Sadiq's role in the Jets' passing game has ground to a halt ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. After spiking in Week 3 with seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, Sadiq has only three catches for 15 yards over the last three weeks while sharing looks with Mason Taylor. Miami is allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, and Sadiq remains long on potential, suggesting a dart throw as a bye-week replacement is possible, but the floor is minimal.

player.seasonOutlook: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield is set for a difficult Week 3 matchup when the Buccaneers take on the Vikings, whose defense has allowed 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Mayfield has really struggled during Tampa Bay's first two contests, accounting for just two touchdowns while turning the ball over four times. He's thrown for just 184.5 passing yards per game while completing 71 percent of his passes. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 3 matchup, with Minnesota's defense giving up just 12.5 points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will operate as the Buccaneers' signal caller if active for the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield has been sidelined for Tampa Bay's last three contests, but head coach Todd Bowles told reporters he's "supposed to practice" Wednesday, suggesting he could return Sunday. Before the injury, Mayfield struggled in his first three games, throwing for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also losing three fumbles. However, he could bounce back against a Panthers defense that's allowed 22.0 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase McLaughlin is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Packers but made both of his point-after attempts. On the season, he's converted on all nine of his field-goal tries, including three from beyond 50 yards. McLaughlin could get fewer kicking chances with Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), but the Cowboys remain a favorable matchup, allowing 8.5 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chase McLaughlin will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. McLaughlin impressed during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, converting on his lone field-goal try and all three point-after attempts. He remains perfect on the season, making all 20 of his kicks this season (10 field goals and 10 extra points). He could have plenty of scoring chances against a Steelers defense that's given up 9.8 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin had an impressive showing in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Buccaneers, converting on all four of his field-goal tries, including three from 40-plus yards. The veteran kicker is perfect on the season, making 14 field goals and 11 extra points. He'll likely have multiple scoring opportunities in Week 7, as the Panthers defense has allowed 7.4 kicking points per game this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will aim to stay perfect as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Santos was on the field a lot in Week 1 against the Panthers, but most of his 11 points came from his eight PATs. The veteran kicker could continue to benefit from a high-scoring offense, and he'll look to continue against a Minnesota squad that allowed three field goals and an extra point to Trey Smack this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cairo Santos will aim to do more as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Santos made his first field-goal attempt against the Vikings in Week 2, but his second chance for a tie was blocked in the fourth quarter. The veteran kicker's potential for the rest of the season remains up in the air following the injury to Caleb Williams, but an inexperienced Tyson Bagent could get the field-goal team on the field more often rather than finding the end zone. Philly has allowed 6.0 fantasy points per game to kickers this year, a top-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cairo Santos will aim to stay solid as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Santos nailed both of his field-goal attempts and went three-for-three on PATs in Week 3 against the Eagles. The veteran kicker has now made all but one of his field-goal tries and all 10 XPAs in the first three games of the season. He'll face a Jets squad that's allowed a top-ten 6.3 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cairo Santos will look to deliver on high volume again as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Bagent converted a season-high three field goals against the Jets in Week 3, and he also nailed both of his XPAs. The veteran kicker has now gone 7-for-8 on field-goal attempts while making all 13 of his extra-point tries across four weeks this season. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers so far.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cairo Santos will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Santos missed his only field-goal attempt and converted an XPA in a Week 6 blowout loss to the Packers. The veteran kicker has now converted seven of nine field-goal kicks and all 14 of his extra-point tries across five games this season. He'll face an Atlanta squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cairo Santos will aim to get back on track as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Santos nailed all four of his XPAs in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, but he went one-for-two on field-goal attempts. The veteran kicker has now missed a kick in back-to-back games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total. Noel can't be trusted as a starter heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals, but the 2025 third-round draft pick could be worth stashing, especially in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylin Noel is a deep-league dart throw for Week 4 against the Cowboys, especially if top Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for a third consecutive game. Noel is tied for fifth on the team with nine targets through three games, but he leads all of Houston's WRs with 11.2 yards per target. Given the Texans' lack of production from the position in Collins' absence, it would be sensible to give Noel more opportunities. Whether they materialize is another matter, and Noel's limited usage so far this season suggests he'll be tough to trust in Week 4, even against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 387 scrimmage yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylin Noel turned three targets into 85 yards for the Texans in their Week 4 loss to Dallas, and the 2025 third-round pick continues to make the most of his opportunities. Heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans, Noel has caught eight of 12 targets for 186 yards while leading the league with 23.3 yards per reception. Noel's big-play potential makes him worth a flier in deeper formats against a Titans secondary that has been prone to breakdowns, but he hasn't garnered consistent enough volume from C.J. Stroud to be started comfortably in any matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylin Noel continues to make the most of his opportunities for the Texans. The 2025 third-round pick has caught every pass thrown his way in four of five games this season, leads the team with 17.5 yards per catch and just scored his first TD of the campaign while tying his season high with five targets in the Week 5 win over Tennessee. Noel's arrow is pointing up ahead of a Week 6 matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing a league-high 204 receiving yards per game to WRs, though his floor remains low due to modest volume, as he has earned just 17 targets through five games. He's a boom-or-bust Week 6 flex option for managers in deeper leagues or in search of a bye-week plug-in.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylin Noel has made the most of his opportunities all season, and Houston's 2025 third-round pick has started to earn a larger role in recent weeks. He takes a two-game touchdown streak into Week 7 against the Giants. Noel has caught all 12 of his targets for 233 yards over the past three games after posting five catches for 101 yards on nine targets through Week 3. Nico Collins remains the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game, and the role of trade acquisition Marvin Harrison should grow moving forward, but Noel's recent success makes him a viable Week 7 flex play against a Giants secondary that has allowed seven receiving TDs to WRs in six games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxson Dart was electric in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for an additional 54 yards in the stunning 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Dart threw just five incompletions and showed excellent rapport with new tight end Isaiah Likely. Dart was accurate, decisive and poised in what amounted to an extremely promising start to the season for the G-Men. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Los Angeles Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in their opener, allowing 379 scrimmage yards, which ranks them in the bottom third of the NFL. The Rams were torched on the ground in particular to the tune of 174 yards. While Myles Garrett will be sidelined due to a knee injury, the Rams will get Aaron Donald back from retirement when they host the Giants on Monday Night Football.

player.seasonOutlook: Dart is a strong 2026 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie campaign in which he delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for fifth most) despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. Dart was solid as a passer but elite as a rusher, finishing in the top five at the position in rushing attempts, yards, TDs and carries inside the 5-yard line. Dart's aggressive playing style raises concerns about his durability, but it also provides the 23-year-old with elite fantasy upside. With a new coaching staff led by John Harbaugh and a new playcaller in Matt Nagy, as well as an improved supporting cast that includes a healthy Malik Nabers and newcomers Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney, Dart is best valued as a midrange QB1 with a high ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.6: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday in Week 6 as the Bears play the Falcons. Johnson got solid opportunities in Chicago's Week 5 blowout loss to Green Bay, with Kyle Monangai out with a toe injury, rushing the ball five times for six yards and reeling in five of seven targets for 34 yards. Johnson's receiving upside could keep him relevant again if Monangai remains sidelined. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 21st in receiving yards allowed to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday again in Week 7 as the Bears play the Patriots. Johnson capitalized on his usage once again with Kyle Monangai (toe) sidelined in Week 6, rushing 13 times for 51 yards and a touchdown and catching two passes for 34 yards. He's now totaled 125 yards and a touchdown on 27 touches in the last two games with Monangai out. If this stays the case, Johnson will be playable against a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Higbee has become a key target for Rams QB Matthew Stafford ahead of a Week 6 battle against Arizona. Higbee recorded a season-high 83 receiving yards on five catches while drawing six targets Monday versus Buffalo. After beginning the campaign with just two catches for 12 yards over his first two contests, Higbee has posted no less than five receptions and 62 yards each of the past three weeks. He could find more success against the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-worst 9.81 yards per target to tight ends on the season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Higbee has emerged as the Rams' most productive receiving tight end, catching 24 passes for 246 yards and a touchdown through six games. Even though he delivered a subpar showing in Week 6 against the Cardinals, finishing with four catches for 22 yards, he's clearly ahead of Colby Parkinson in the pecking order in the passing game. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the time being, Higbee should be one of the players in line for an uptick in targets and touches. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable on paper, as Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kaelon Black will likely again get a handful of carries again for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Black has logged between four and seven carries each of his past four games after getting 14 totes in Week 1 against the Rams. The rookie hasn't been particularly efficient with his opportunities, managing just 2.4 yards per carry over the past two weeks and 3.7 overall this season. Things may not get easier against the Commanders, who have yielded the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kaelon Black and the 49ers visit the Falcons for a Week 7 showdown. He had eight carries for 34 yards and caught his lone target for three yards in San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Christian McCaffrey tallied 25 touches to the rookie's nine, leaving no doubt about who the leader is in the 49ers' backfield. Black will look to make more of an impact with his limited touches versus Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.7: J.J. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt by the Giants last game. Though McCarthy's efforts fell short, he threw for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of starter Jameis Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Reed will look to make more of his opportunities as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Reed struggled even with seven targets in a loss to the Vikings, logging just three catches for 20 yards. The fourth-year playmaker could start to slip into a WR3 role if he continues to play similarly, but luckily there appears to be plenty of targets to go around in the short term. Reed will face a New York defense that ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Reed's status is up in the air as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Reed was carted off the field after injuring his back on the first drive of Week 2, which in itself makes it unlikely that he'll be rushed back for a TNF matchup. The fourth-year playmaker's absence would give Matthew Golden even more looks, with Skyy Moore and Bo Melton slotting in as supplementary options for Jordan Love. If Reed somehow does play, he'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
