outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Reed is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Packers take on the Falcons. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he hasn't seen the field since. The fourth-year wide receiver also has no current return timeline. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Reed will not play in Week 5 as the Packers play the Bears. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Mevis is coming off a quiet season opener as the Rams prepare to face the Giants in Week 2. Los Angeles' offense was held by the 49ers to just seven points last Thursday, and Mevis didn't get the opportunity to attempt any field goals. The Rams figure to be much more prolific on that side of the ball most weeks, so Mevis should be more active moving forward, though last year he attempted 39 PATs to just 13 field goals. The Giants' defense put up a good performance in a Week 1 win over Dallas, with star kicker Brandon Aubrey getting no field-goal tries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Mevis is still searching for his first field-goal conversion heading into the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Mevis didn't try a FG in Week 1, and he missed his only attempt -- a 43-yarder -- on Monday Night Football. Mevis did make all four of his extra-point tries and figures to kick a lot of those given the Rams' explosive offense. Kickers have gone 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts against the Broncos so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Mevis is coming off a career-best four FGs ahead of the Rams' matchup versus Philadelphia in Week 4. After going 0-for-1 in field-goal tries over the first two weeks of the campaign, Mevis was asked to attempt four FGs versus Denver in Week 3 and made every try, including a 48-yarder. With that said, the Rams' explosive offense doesn't frequently end drives with field-goal attempts, so Mevis may struggle to see such volume moving forward. Opponents have been successful on five of six field-goal attempts versus the Eagles so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harrison Mevis heads into the Rams' Week 5 matchup against Buffalo with a modest four field goals on the season. Four of those came in Week 3 against Denver, and Mevis missed a 48-yard try this past Sunday against Philadelphia. The second-year pro is a perfect 10-for-10 on point-after tries this year and has made all 49 of his PAT attempts in his career. Buffalo has yielded just six FG tries through four weeks, with kickers making five of those attempts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harrison Mevis' job may be on the line heading into the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Cardinals. Mevis missed both of his field-goal attempts in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, including a 50-yarder in the first quarter and a blocked 48-yarder in overtime that could have won the game. He's now just 5-for-9 on FG tries this season, including 3-for-6 from 40-to-49 yards out. Should Mevis still be kicking for the Rams in Week 6, he may be limited mostly to extra points versus a Cardinals defense that has yielded 18 PAT tries to just six FG attempts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson will look to stay perfect when the Bengals visit the Texans in Week 2. He nailed all four of his field-goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, and made all three PATs during Cincinnati's 33-27 win in the season opener. McPherson should remain a top fantasy kicker as a member of one of the NFL's elite offenses. Houston gave up 36 points and 409 total yards in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Steelers for an AFC North divisional matchup in Week 3. He remained perfect on the season after connecting on both of his field-goal attempts and both PATs during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. McPherson drilled both of his field goals from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 6-for-6 on the season, with four of his makes coming beyond 50 yards. He'll continue to earn plenty of scoring opportunities on an elite offense, even despite Pittsburgh's strong defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Evan McPherson and the Bengals host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He stayed perfect on the year after drilling both field-goal attempts and all three PATs during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. McPherson is now 8-for-8 on FGAs and extra-point tries, including five kicks from at least 50 yards out. He'll aim to stay hot against one of the league's best defenses, as Jacksonville allows just 12.0 points per game, which ranks first. Still, McPherson should continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities for a Bengals squad averaging 26.7 PPG (12th).
outlooksByWeek.5: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Dolphins for a Week 5 road tilt. He made his only field-goal attempt from 29 yards out and connected on both of his PATs during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. McPherson remained perfect on his kicks through four outings, but he'll hope to get more involved against a Miami defense that ranks 21st in the league, allowing 25.3 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to face the Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He made his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. McPherson was forced to do his damage with extra points, as the victory marked his second straight outing with only one FGA. He'll look to make more of an impact against a Baltimore defense allowing 22.0 points per game, which ranks 15th.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacoby Brissett will look to help Arizona pull off another upset against Seattle in Week 2. Brissett was great in a season-opening win over the Chargers, throwing for 277 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His passing score went to tight end Trey McBride, who should continue to be his top weapon as one of the league's top players at the position. The Seahawks present a tough challenge, however, as they are expected to have one of the league's top defenses and picked Drake Maye off three times in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his best game of season heading into Arizona's Week 4 clash with the Giants. Brissett threw for a season-high 280 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco while adding a TD as a rusher. His three total scores were more than the two (both through the air) he compiled over the first two weeks of the campaign. The Giants have been middle-of-the-pack statistically against the pass so far but will be without star edge rusher Brian Burns, who is out for the campaign due to a torn ACL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacoby Brissett will aim to clean up his mistakes when Arizona hosts Detroit in Week 5. Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants in Week 4 after getting picked off just once through his first three games of the season. The veteran quarterback has still been pretty productive with 818 passing yards, six touchdowns and 43 rushing yards (with one touchdown) overall this season. He next draws a juicy matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points per game (32.7) to quarterbacks on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his first three-TD performance of the campaign heading into Arizona's Week 6 clash against the Rams. Two of Brissett's scores in this past Sunday's blowout loss to Detroit came after the outcome was already decided, but they count the same in the world of fantasy football. The veteran quarterbacks also threw for a season-high 292 yards and rushed for a season-best 19 yards, though he did throw his fifth interception of the campaign. Brissett could find the sledding tougher against the Rams, who have given up just 5.65 yards per attempt this season, second-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jacoby Brissett will look to build on Arizona's Week 6 victory over the Rams when the Cardinals host the Broncos in Week 7. The veteran quarterback has completed 156 of 234 passes for 1,328 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions through six games, averaging 221.3 passing yards per contest. However, his 5.7 yards per attempt are the best example of the struggles Arizona's offense endures to generate explosive passing plays, and Denver represents another challenging opponent. The Broncos have allowed just 14.9 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the 12th-best mark in the NFL, limiting Brissett's appeal despite his established passing volume. He's best viewed as a lower-end QB2 in superflex formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Fitzgerald is in for a favorable Week 2 matchup when the Panthers face the Falcons, who gave up 8.0 kicking points in a Week 1 loss. Fitzgerald made five of his six kicks last week, drilling his only field-goal attempt while going four-for-five on point-after tries. He's expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 2, as he averaged 11.0 kicking points per game in two games against Atlanta in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Fitzgerald has started the season strong, converting on all three of his field-goal tries and eight of nine point-after attempts. Additionally, he could continue to benefit from the Panthers' offensive success, as the team currently ranks second in points per game (35.5). Fitzgerald is in for a great Week 3 matchup as well, with Cleveland allowing 11.5 kicking points per game through two contests this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to continue building on an impressive performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Fitzgerald was perfect in Carolina's Week 3 loss, converting on all four of his field-goal tries. On the season, he's made all seven field-goal attempts and eight of nine point-after tries. Fitzgerald expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 4, as Detroit's defense has allowed 31.7 points per game this season, despite giving up just 5.0 kicking points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to bounce back from a poor performance in Carolina's Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite an upset win over the Lions in Week 4, Fitzgerald made just two of four point-after attempts. On the season, the second-year pro has made all nine field goals but has struggled on extra points, converting on just 10 of 13 tries. He's in for a tougher Week 6 matchup as well, with Philadelphia's defense allowing just 6.8 kicking pints per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Fitzgerald will likely have plenty of scoring opportunities in Carolina's Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Fitzgerald has struggled over the last two contests, making just three of six point-after attempts. On the season, Fitzgerald is a perfect 11-for-11 on field-goal tries but just 11 of 15 on extra-point attempts. He's in for a very favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's given up 10.0 kicking points per game this season.

player.seasonOutlook: A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Washington's volume was limited in his NFL debut, but he was productive, gaining 41 rushing yards on seven carries in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins. The quality of his opposition needs to be taken into account, but it was still a strong showing from the 2026 fourth-round pick. Lead back Ashton Jeanty had a huge game, proving he was fully recovered from a preseason ankle injury, but if he has trouble staying on the field, Washington appears very capable of stepping into a larger role. He'll face a tough matchup in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't logged big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Washington failed to produce another big play in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, managing only 18 rushing yards on nine carries while catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground, but Washington hasn't yet shown enough consistency to be any kind of threat to his workload on early downs. The rookie is averaging 5.0 yards on his first 24 NFL carries, though, well clear of Jeanty's 3.4 mark, so volume could begin to tilt his way a little more if that trend continues. Washington will try to break free in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Washington logged a season-low two touches in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, turning one carry and one reception into just 10 scrimmage yards. Ashton Jeanty continues to get a bell-cow workload despite his struggles on the ground, and Washington's 5.0 yards per carry on the season might encourage coach Klint Kubiak to give him more work on early downs. The rookie has flashed his big-play potential, but until he gets more consistent volume, his main value will be as injury insurance behind Jeanty. Washington may not need many touches to contribute in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Washington is coming off an intriguing showing in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, as he turned nine carries into a team-high 43 yards. The rookie remains behind Ashton Jeanty on the running back depth chart, but Washington has been the more effective option on the ground, averaging 4.9 yards per carry on his limited volume while Jeanty has struggled to a 3.2 mark. Washington has posted double-digit touches in two of the last three games as his usage creeps up, but he's unlikely to make a splash in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Kirk and the 49ers hope to improve to 7-0 when they visit Atlanta in Week 7. The veteran receiver has been on the reserve/PUP list to begin 2026 due to a calf injury and has yet to suit up for San Francisco. The 49ers opened Kirk's practice window on Oct. 15 and there were reports of him possibly being activated for Week 6, but that was indeed not the case. With Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to miss the road clash against the Falcons, San Francisco could really use Kirk's presence on the field.

player.seasonOutlook: Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.7: Bam Knight got an extended opportunity in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) in Week 6 against the Rams and made the most of the situation, notching 15 carries for 80 yards and outplaying Tyler Allgeier, who mustered just 38 rushing yards on 18 rushing attempts. It remains to be seen whether Love will be an option in the backfield in Week 7, as much of that will depend on whether Love is cleared to play, but he's a player worth keeping close tabs on in the event Love isn't 100 percent ready. The matchup is favorable on paper, as the Broncos have given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing tailbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 4 as Detroit faces Carolina. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the meantime.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 5 when Detroit travels to Arizona. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 7 as Detroit plays the Packers. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kalif Raymond could continue to be a consistent option as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Raymond benefited from a high-scoring Week 1 win, reeling in eight of nine targets for 84 yards. The veteran wide receiver was also on the field for 60 percent of offensive snaps, so it appears at least a WR3 role is cemented moving forward. He'll face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points (55.2) to his position this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).
outlooksByWeek.4: Kalif Raymond will look to continue his tear as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Raymond remained a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 3 against the Eagles, pulling in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Lion transfer has now garnered five or more targets in each game this season, and eclipsed 80 yards in two of three. He'll face a Jets secondary that's been tougher on WRs this season, allowing a top-five 337 receiving yards to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kalif Raymond will seek to reestablish himself as a consistent option in Chicago's passing game against the Packers in Week 5. After totaling 19 catches for 214 yards and one touchdown across the Bears' first three games of the season, Raymond recorded just two catches for six yards versus the Jets in Week 4 with Tyson Bagent under center. The veteran pass catcher will have Bagent throwing to him once again this Sunday, but he will also face a Green Bay defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kalif Raymond will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond has now caught five passes for just 12 yards in the past two weeks. Chicago has had struggles at the quarterback position in this stretch, but the veteran still appears behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR pecking order. Raymond will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to his position this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kalif Raymond remains a secondary option in Chicago's passing game in Week 7 against the Patriots. Raymond was unable to capitalize on Caleb Williams' return in Week 6, recording just two catches for 18 yards. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond is now situated behind Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Colston Loveland in the target hierarchy. He'll take on a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger issue that's cost him the last three weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. He had emerged as a field stretcher for the Jets, but it's an offense that prefers to run and heavily target Garrett Wilson. New England has allowed five touchdown catches by opposing receivers in as many games, and Mitchell would likely require that end-zone success to be considered a starting option. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick will continue to get additional snaps if Mitchell remains sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.7: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger injury that cost him four games if he's to help the Jets against the Dolphins in Week 7. Mitchell looked firm in his role opposite Garrett Wilson prior to injury, but it's fair to question his immediate role should he be active in Week 7. Facing a Dolphins' secondary that's surprisingly allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers despite a desirable 8.2 yards per target doesn't profile as a re-emergent spot, especially with Omar Cooper healthy and surging.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darius Cooper scored twice last game for the Eagles. Cooper finished the contests with seven targets, parlaying those looks into three catches for 33 yards and the pair of scores. If Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and/or Saquon Barkley are sidelined in Week 5 versus the Jags, Cooper could see an uptick in usage again.  Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darius Cooper continues to flash his big-play ability for the Eagles. Cooper snagged his fourth touchdown of the season last game versus the Jaguars en route to leading the Eagles in receiving yards. Four of Cooper's seven receptions have gone for touchdowns in 2026. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has also likely boosted the opportunities for Cooper, who has 10 targets in his last two contests alone. This trend could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darius Cooper caught just one pass for nine yards last game for the Eagles. Cooper had just two targets overall, as the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Cooper's upside as well. However, in Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing six times for 40 yards during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. Watson was sacked eight times for 53 yards and fumbled three times, although he recovered two of them. After leading the Browns to a three-game win streak behind strong performances, Watson struggled with pressure and the rainy conditions in the Week 5 defeat. He'll aim to bounce back versus Baltimore's 12th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to square off against the Titans in Week 7. He completed 16 of 26 pass attempts for 164 yards and rushed eight times for 29 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. Watson is not much of a fantasy-friendly quarterback, but he has the Browns at 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. Next up is a stingy Tennessee defense that ranks 10th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey Smack will look to stay solid as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Smack converted all three of his field-goal attempts against the Vikings in Week 1, but he did go 1-for-2 on XPAs. Still, the perfect field-goal percentage outshines his one miss. Smack will face a Jets defense that allowed a bottom-five fantasy points (4.0) total to Titans kicker Joey Slye this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey Smack will aim to stay perfect as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Smack went perfect in Week 2 against the Jets, nailing two PATs and two field-goal tries, including a game-winner. The rookie kicker has now gone a perfect five-for-five on field goals and made all but one of his four extra-point attempts. He'll take on an Atlanta team that's allowed 9.0 fantasy points per game to kickers on the year, a bottom-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey Smack will have a favorable matchup as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smack went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he also had his sole field-goal attempt blocked. The rookie kicker will seek to get back on track versus a Bucs squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (12.3) to kickers this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey Smack will look to be consistent for the Packers once again in Week 5 against the Bears. Smack nailed a 58-yard field goal and both of his extra-point tries against the Buccaneers in Week 4. The rookie kicker has now gone 6-for-7 on field-goal kicks this season, with three of them from 50-plus yards. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trey Smack will aim to get back on track as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Smack's accuracy was not on point against the Bears in Week 5, as he went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-3 on XPAs. While the rookie kicker's struggles didn't matter in an eventual blowout win, he'll need to get better when high-importance kicks come up more later in the year. Smack will face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack (8.0 points allowed per game) versus fantasy kickers this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Trey Smack will look to build off a solid performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. After a disappointing performance even in a blowout victory against the Bears, Smack nailed all three of his field-goal tries and went two-for-two on XPAs in a Week 6 win over Dallas. The rookie kicker has now converted 10 of 13 field-goal kicks and gone 11-for-13 on extra-point attempts this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. notched a 3-25-0 line on three targets, finishing second on the team in yardage. Gesicki is hard to trust with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) healthy, especially versus a Baltimore defense tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keaton Mitchell could be moving into a bigger role in the Chargers' backfield. While the offense as a whole is struggling, the former Raven logged a season-high eight carries in Week 3 and turned them into 52 rushing yards. He also made his first trip to the end zone in 2026, getting a one-yard shovel pass from Justin Herbert on a jet sweep. Omarion Hampton is struggling to adapt to new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and that's opening the door for Mitchell to push his way into a timeshare in the backfield. However, neither back is likely to make a splash in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keaton Mitchell's role in the Chargers' backfield continues to grow. The former Raven handled a season-high 15 touches in a Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, turning them into 63 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton produced 53 yards and a rushing TD on 11 touches, and Kimani Vidal added 36 yards and a receiving score on seven touches. That split points toward offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel moving into a full-blown backfield committee, and while Mitchell's volume has been trending up, he hasn't done much yet to make a case for the No. 1 spot on the depth chart. He'll look to make his own trip to the end zone in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keaton Mitchell is coming off a disappointing Week 5 performance against the Broncos, as he turned nine touches into a modest 29 scrimmage yards. He was outgained by both Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal as the Chargers' backfield devolves into a full committee, but none of the three have made a strong case to seize the clear No. 1 role. Mitchell flashed big-play potential during his time with the Ravens, but working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line won't generate many holes. He'll try to produce in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyrone Tracy was the third-string running back in the season opener for the Giants while Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1, though that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly. Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Tracy does suit up in Week 2, he will act mostly as depth against a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyrone Tracy was the most productive back last game for the Giants, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown. However, he managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches overall. Meanwhile, Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches, Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries and Cam Skattebo did not even register a touch following last week's costly fumble. It will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. In Week 7, the Giants will also face a stingy Texans run defense. Houston is allowing only 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Tracy is set to compete with Devin Singletary for opportunities in a Giants backfield led by second-year back Cam Skattebo. Tracy has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two NFL seasons, but that doesn't tell the full story. Tracy got there as a fifth-round rookie in 2024 by impressing and taking New York's starting gig by Week 5. Last season, he quickly lost lead-back duties to Skattebo, but played a much larger role once Skattebo went down for the season with an injury (9.0 touches per game during Weeks 1-9, but 18.6 per game from Weeks 10-18). Tracy has no standalone fantasy value, but he's effective as a rusher and receiver. That makes the 26-year-old a solid backup who would be worth adding if Skattebo misses additional time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Jones is unlikely to post gaudy passing numbers in the Colts' run-first offense, and he doesn't appear interested in using his legs as much after tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of last season. His fantasy appeal is limited to multi-QB or superflex formats, and Jones is a low-end option even in those leagues for a Week 2 matchup against a Chiefs defense that held Bo Nix to 131 passing yards in Week 1. Jones had just 166 passing yards with a 1:1 TD:INT and one carry for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Ravens.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Jones is averaging 188 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston gave up two touchdown passes apiece to star QBs Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, but Jones will be hard-pressed to post his first multi-TD performance of the season considering the Texans boast one of the league's best defenses, having allowed the fewest yards in the NFL last season. The Colts will continue to rely primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and Indianapolis has an underwhelming group of pass catchers that's expected to be without last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel) for several weeks. Jones has been a non-factor as a rusher since returning from a torn Achilles, with just 14 rushing yards this season. His mediocre passing stats make him an unappealing Week 3 fantasy option, even in multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.4: Daniel Jones led the Colts to their first win since Week 10 of the 2025 season in Week 3 against the Texans, but he has just three touchdown passes and five turnovers heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Jones, who underwent surgery to repair a torn Achilles in December, hasn't been much of a factor with his legs, rushing for just 19 yards and has yet to score a rushing TD after notching five last season. Washington has allowed a league-high 11 passing TDs, so while Jones will be tough to trust as a starter in one-QB formats with the Colts missing last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel; IR), he's a viable option in superflex or multi-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Daniel Jones is averaging 189 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. Jones threw for a season-high 342 yards against the Steelers last season but had five turnovers in that game. His passing production is likely to be much more muted in this rematch while throwing to a depleted Colts receiving corps that remains without Alec Pierce (heel; IR) and played without Keenan Allen (groin) in the Week 4 win over the Commanders in London. Pittsburgh's defense has limited QBs to a 5:4 TD:INT, while Jones has an even worse 3:4 TD:INT this season. Even superflex and multi-QB league managers are better off looking elsewhere.
outlooksByWeek.6: Daniel Jones has just a 3:4 TD:INT and hasn't rushed for more than 10 yards in a game heading into the Colts' Week 6 home game against the Titans. Indianapolis' offense relies primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and that formula is unlikely to change since the Colts will likely have the luxury of playing from ahead in Week 6 against a Titans team that has been outscored 109-58 this season but allowed only five passing TDs. Between Jones' own limitations as a passer and his team's lack of receiving talent, he remains an unappetizing Week 6 fantasy option, even in superflex and multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Daniel Jones and the Colts are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the previously winless Titans, and things get significantly more difficult on the road in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game. Jones played his part in the loss to Tennessee with a season-worst two interceptions, and he has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game while posting a 4:6 TD:INT through six outings. He's averaging just 215 passing yards and nine rushing yards per game. Even in superflex and multi-QB formats, the struggling QB isn't an advisable fantasy option.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones re-signed with the Colts during the offseason and will return as the team's starter. The 2019 No. 6 draft pick made a big leap in 2025 -- his first season with Indianapolis -- finishing no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt. Despite the strong play, Jones was inconsistent as a fantasy option, averaging 18.8 fantasy points during 12 full games and posting three top-five weeks but no additional finishes better than ninth. Jones was effective through the air and scored five rushing TDs, but he didn't run the ball as much as in years past and might do even less of that in 2026 after tearing an Achilles in Week 14. He's likely to be ready for Week 1, but effectiveness is a concern, so he's best viewed as a midrange QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emmett Johnson has seen little work to begin his career as the No. 2 running back for Kansas City behind bell cow Kenneth Walker. Johnson is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but the fifth-round rookie has teased his big-play potential as a pass catcher, catching all five of his targets for 74 yards. As long as Walker remains healthy, Johnson will remain little more than an upside bench stash. He could get some garbage-time touches in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emmett Johnson remains stuck in a low-volume role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Johnson hasn't logged double-digit touches since Week 1, and his three targets in a Week 6 win over the Chargers were a season-high. The rookie running back will likely need an injury to Walker to contribute. Johnson will look for his first NFL touchdown in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Geno Smith may be called upon more often in Week 2 when the Jets face the Packers. He wasn't asked to do much last week as the club played with a rare lead for the majority of the game, relying on the run-something unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Green Bay's secondary is vulnerable, allowing three touchdowns to Carson Wentz to start the year. With more volume, Smith can ascend to the second tier of quarterbacks in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Geno Smith is facing an uphill battle if he hopes to match his Week 3 success when the Jets face the Bears in Week 4. Smith is coming off a sterling outing where he threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, completing 84% of his passes against the Lions. While the Bears' secondary is vulnerable in individual matchups, their overall body of work has been stout. Chicago hasn't allowed more than 153 yards over the last two weeks, with no touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite Breece Hall's likely absence, the Bears are more suspect against the run, potentially setting Smith up for a game-management approach.
outlooksByWeek.5: Geno Smith hopes for more opportunities in the Jets' Week 5 game against a vulnerable Browns secondary. After completing 31 passes in Week 3, Smith went just 8-for-15 in Week 4 against the Bears. Despite the lack of volume, he has a 5:0 TD:INT ratio and a 7.7 yards-per-attempt average, his highest mark since playing just two games in 2016. Cleveland has allowed nine touchdown passes in four games and at least 291 yards in each of the last two weeks, putting Smith in a spot to exceed his season norms.
outlooksByWeek.6: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle for fantasy success when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Smith has been held to 182 yards or fewer in consecutive weeks and has multiple touchdown passes just once through five games. While the Patriots' secondary is banged up, they've still allowed just a 6:3 TD:INT ratio through five games while holding three quarterbacks to no more than 187 yards. The Jets hope to remain run-first, limiting Smith's opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.7: Geno Smith will look to buck his seasonal trends in an inviting Week 7 matchup when the Jets face the Dolphins. Smith has opened the year with one or zero touchdown passes in five of his six games, but Miami's defense has allowed 11 touchdown throws in five contests. Smith likely needs those timely scoring plays as Miami is allowing just 226 passing yards per game, with teams preferring to exploit its run defense, setting him up as a risky bye-week replacement option.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Penix will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Penix has been great through two starts in 2026, throwing for 479 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He's helped rejuvenate Atlanta's offense, as the team has scored a whopping 40 points per game since his return. Despite this, Penix is in for a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 18.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Penix (ribs) will lead the Falcons' passing attack if active during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Penix was productive for the third consecutive game before exiting with a rib injury in the overtime loss to the Ravens, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. Through three weeks, Penix is averaging 239.7 passing yards and a touchdown per game. He's in for a favorable matchup if ready for Week 6, as the Bears' defense just allowed Jordan Love to throw for 367 yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense during the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Penix was productive despite a loss in Week 6, throwing for 225 yards and three touchdowns while also completing two two-point conversions. Since returning from injury, Penix has led the Falcons' offense to 31.5 points per game, the second-most in the NFL during that span. However, he could struggle against a tough 49ers defense that's given up just 16.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through five contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.3: Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson is a potential breakout candidate in his second NFL season. As expected, the 2025 second-rounder played a situational role behind the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen as a rookie. He didn't get much run, but when he did, he was used as a vertical threat to the extreme. His 17.5 aDOT is highest by any tight end (minimum 10 targets) in at least a decade. The Rams are returning the same tight end room plus second-round pick Max Klare, so while consistent production could prove elusive, Ferguson very well could emerge as the No. 3 pass catcher behind Puka Nacua and 33-year-old Davante Adams in the Rams' elite offense. The 23-year-old, who also saw five end zone targets as a rookie, is worth a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference matchup in Week 2. The rookie third-round pick is doubtful to suit up with a fractured wrist sustained in the opener. Head coach Jesse Minter advised that Lane is seeking second and third medical opinions before establishing a timeline for his return. His health is something to monitor, but for now, his absence could make way for Devontez Walker (groin) and Elijah Sarratt (coach's decision).
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens return home to face off against the division-rival Bengals in Week 7. He impressed in his first game back from a four-week stint on injured reserve with a wrist injury suffered in Week 1, catching four of five targets for 40 yards during Baltimore's Week 6 defeat. Lane tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing third in yardage, setting career highs across the board. With Rashod Bateman (shoulder) exiting the loss in the first half, Lane could see a boost in opportunities if the former is unable to suit up in Week 7. However, he'll be facing Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (29.3) to WRs, so it's best to proceed with caution.

player.seasonOutlook: Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume pass offense. Lane's primary value is as dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. Despite leading Baltimore's receivers with 53 offensive snaps, he logged just one target and did not record a reception. With Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane out with a fractured wrist suffered in the opener, Bateman's opportunities to contribute could increase. Regardless of who's active, he'll aim to bounce back against New Orleans' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (37.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 3 matchup against the Cowboys. In the absence of top wideout Zay Flowers (hamstring), Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. He'll likely slide back to a supporting role if Flowers is able to suit up this Sunday. However, if he's unable to do so, Bateman will have the chance to replicate his solid outing versus a Dallas defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens return home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Baltimore's 34-31 win in Week 3, finishing second on the team in yardage. However, with Zay Flowers (hamstring) returning from a one-game absence, Bateman saw his involvement dip heavily after posting a 7-88-1 line in Week 2's loss. Flowers paced the Ravens in receptions, targets, and yardage, and as long as he remains healthy, managers can expect Bateman to see similar results against Tennessee's 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens square off against the 2-2 Falcons on the road in Week 5. He caught both of his targets for 46 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Bateman tied with five other Ravens in targets while finishing second on the team in yardage, but Zay Flowers (8-118-1) and Mark Andrews (5-27-1) did most of the damage on offense. He'll try to make more of a contribution versus an Atlanta defense that's tied for 27th in fantasy points allowed (38.4) per game to WRs, although that could be challenging given Lamar Jackson's (ankle) uncertain status for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught five of six targets for 62 yards during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. Bateman led the team in receiving yards and was second in receptions while tying for second in targets. Tyler Huntley, who started for Lamar Jackson (ankle), attempted 32 passes and relied heavily on the wideout, as all five of Bateman's catches resulted in first downs for the Ravens. He'll aim to make a similar difference against a Browns defense allowing 36.4 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 24th.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals in Week 7. He failed to catch his only target before exiting in the second quarter of Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Bateman sat out the entire second half while dealing with the nagging shoulder issue, allowing rookie Jakobi Lane to rack up a 4-40-0 receiving line on five targets. Even if Bateman is able to suit up against Cincinnati in Week 7, he should remain on fantasy benches due to his inconsistent involvement in the offense, regardless of the Ravens' quarterback situation.

player.seasonOutlook: Bateman is entering his sixth season in Baltimore following an injury-plagued 2025 campaign in which he was limited to a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games. After scoring nine touchdowns on only 45 receptions in 2024, Bateman had "regression" written all over him entering last season, but it was worse than expected.
