The 2021 first-round pick saw his target share fall from 15.4% to a career-low 11.4% and his only double-digit fantasy effort came in Week 3. The 26-year-old remains second on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers, but even in a new scheme and with a healthy Lamar Jackson under center, he's unlikely to produce his first top-35 fantasy campaign. Bateman isn't the most appealing late-round draft pick.

Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Rodriguez had just six carries to Bhayshul Tuten's 15 in Jacksonville's season opener. Considering Rodriguez contributes almost nothing as a pass-catcher, with just six receptions in 36 career games, he'll be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent deep-league dart throw for fantasy purposes as long as Tuten is healthy. Rodriguez is unlikely to find the end zone in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing TDs (eight) to RBs last season, though Denver gave up two total TDs to Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first three games with the Jaguars heading into a Week 4 road tilt at Cincinnati. He scored his first TD of the season in the Week 3 rout of the Patriots, but Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent deep-league option as long as Bhayshul Tuten is available. The Bengals have allowed the most receiving yards in the league to RBs, but Rodriguez almost certainly won't capitalize on that weakness, as he has yet to earn a target this year and has just six career catches in 38 games.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Rodriguez has a consistent role as the Jaguars' No. 2 RB behind Bhayshul Tuten, but Rodriguez's usage level is too low to warrant lineup consideration in most formats. Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first four games with the Jaguars. He's riding a two-game TD streak but has been a complete non-factor in the passing game with zero targets while averaging a mediocre 4.2 yards per carry. Jacksonville faces an Eagles defense in Week 5 that ranks among the 10 most generous to RBs on the ground, allowing 106 rushing yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Rodriguez has exceeded six rushing attempts in only one of five games with the Jaguars and has just one catch all season. With starting RB Bhayshul Tuten healthy heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans, Rodriguez doesn't look like a usable fantasy option in most formats against a stout Houston front seven that's limiting RBs to 3.5 yards per carry. Rodriguez remains a viable bench stash for managers hedging against a Tuten injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

outlooksByWeek.2: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to face the Texans for a Week 2 tilt. He was highly efficient with his touches in the season-opening win, tallying five carries for 20 yards while catching all three targets for 30 yards. Perine was the only other running back to record a carry, so his status as the No. 2 RB is not in question. Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, but it surrendered 409 total yards of offense in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Samaje Perine and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He rushed three times for nine yards and caught one of three targets for five yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss. Lead back Chase Brown handled 13 carries, so Perine is firmly established as the No. 2 option and primary passing-down option out of the backfield. Jacksonville's defense ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (17.2) to RBs, and it has surrendered just one rushing TD to the position through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Samaje Perine and the Bengals are on the road to take on the Dolphins in Week 5. He tallied three carries for seven yards and failed to bring in his only target during Cincinnati's Week 4 defeat. Perine's offensive snaps and involvement continue to fluctuate as the clear back behind Chase Brown, even despite his team playing from behind more recently. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) allowed to RBs, but Perine should remain on fantasy benches.
outlooksByWeek.7: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the 4-2 Ravens in Week 7. He rushed 14 times for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. Perine out-carried starter Chase Brown (13) and was much more efficient, as Brown managed just 39 yards on the ground. If Brown continues to struggle, Perine could have a larger role than initially anticipated at the beginning of the campaign. However, it might be wise to wait until we know more about the backfield hierarchy following the matchup against Baltimore's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2. They'll face the fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.1) to WRs. Jeudy brought in two of four targets for 26 yards in Cleveland's season-opening blowout loss, but he didn't see any looks in the second half. He tied rookie Denzel Boston for second in targets and third in receptions, while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the way with four catches and five targets. As long as the Browns' QB play remains shaky, there's no reason to consider Jeudy in any fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3, whose defense allowed just 145 yards through the air in Week 2. He failed to corral his lone target during Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2, giving him a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through two games. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 123 yards and one TD while catching 11 of 13 targets, and they look to be the leaders in the WR room. It will be difficult to start any of them until the Browns' offense consistently proves it can sustain any fantasy-relevant players.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns play host to their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He did not record a target in Cleveland's 21-18 Week 3 victory after failing to catch his only target in Week 2's win. Jeudy now owns a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through three games, and it's clear he's fallen down the offensive pecking order behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion and TE Harold Fannin Jr. He should remain on waiver wires against Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns travel to take on the Jets in Week 5. He hauled in all three of his targets for 36 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4, setting new season highs in receptions and yardage. Jeudy had a solid bounce-back effort after failing to record a target in Week 3, but he remains behind Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and Harold Fannin Jr. in the offensive pecking order. Jeudy belongs on fantasy benches against a Jets defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points allowed (28.5) per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Ravens for a divisional clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 19 yards during Cleveland's Week 5 defeat. Jeudy became more involved after KC Concepcion (concussion) exited in the first quarter, and there's a chance the rookie will be unable to clear the NFL's five-step protocol before their matchup with Baltimore. If that is indeed the case, Jeudy will slide into the No. 2 receiver role behind Denzel Boston against a Ravens defense allowing 36.2 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 23rd.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns travel to take on the Titans in Week 7. He caught all four of his targets for 69 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. After compiling a 6-55-0 line on 11 targets over his last four outings, Jeudy led the team in yardage and tied for first in receptions, surpassing the 40-yard mark for the first time all season. However, despite a favorable matchup versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs, he should remain on fantasy waiver wires as a member of an inconsistent offense.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeudy's up-and-down career continues, as he has now finished outside the top 50 receivers in fantasy PPG four times in six seasons and inside the top 25 twice in the last four years. Jeudy has handled a target share in the 19-23% range all six seasons, but he hasn't found the end zone very often (17 TDs in 91 games) and has struggled with drops (32). Horrific efficiency (48% catch rate, 5.7 YPT) was a big issue last season and led to a career-low 7.1 fantasy PPG. Life might not be much better in 2026 with Cleveland's quarterback situation still unsolved and a lot more target competition (rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston join Harold Fannin Jr.). On the other hand, Jeudy, 27, is still in his prime and it has only been one season since he ranked sixth in the league with 1,229 receiving yards. He has some bounce-back potential, but Jeudy is safest as a bench player.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving tight end during the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite signing with the Panthers in early August, Waller ranks first amongst the team's tight end corps in targets (19), receptions (13), yards (148) and touchdowns (two) through four games. Waller could receive fewer opportunities in Week 6, however, with Jalen Coker (quadriceps) expected to return from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a difficult matchup against an Eagles defense that's allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' primary pass-catching tight end in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite going with a catch in Carolina's Week 6 win over the Eagles, Waller still leads the TE corps in targets (18) and yards (148) through five contests. However, Waller will likely see less opportunities to score with Jalen Coker back from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that's already allowed four receiving touchdowns to TEs this year.

outlooksByWeek.3: Konata Mumpfield's role in the Rams' Week 3 matchup against Denver could depend on the status of Puka Nacua (hip). With Nacua sidelined Monday versus Denver, Mumpfield drew the start, but he finished with just one catch on two targets for 12 yards. Meanwhile, Davante Adams posted a massive 10-195-2 line, with no other Los Angeles wideout reeling in more than one catch. The Broncos won't be an easy matchup in Week 3, as they've held opposing WRs to an average of just 13.2 fantasy points per game this season, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Konata Mumpfield is coming off the biggest performance of his young career ahead of the Rams' Week 4 matchup in Philadelphia. Mumpfield established new professional high marks with four catches for 93 yards against Denver in Week 3, with one of his receptions going for a 48-yard touchdown. The second-year wideout logged a healthy eight targets in the loss, but important context is that Puka Nacua sat out due to a hip injury. Should Nacua be able to return in Week 4, it's reasonable to expect Mumpfield to see considerably less opportunities. Still, the Eagles have been vulnerable against wideouts and just allowed Chicago's WR duo of Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond to combine for 13 catches, 151 yards and two TDs on Monday Night Football.
outlooksByWeek.5: Konata Mumpfield is dealing with a shoulder injury heading into the Rams' Week 5 battle versus Buffalo. Mumpfield suffered a bruised rotator cuff in in Week 4 against Philadelphia, though he was able to return to action after getting hurt. That bodes well for his chances of playing in Week 5, though even if he does suit up he's unlikely to be a big part of the offense with both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams healthy. His path to production may be touchdown-dependent, and the Bills have given up six receiving TDs to wideouts -- tied for second-most in the NFL -- through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Konata Mumpfield enters Week 7 with an opportunity to expand his role in the Rams' passing attack after Davante Adams suffered a significant hamstring injury that will sideline him for multiple weeks. Mumpfield has caught eight passes for 127 yards and a touchdown through six games, averaging an impressive 15.9 yards per reception despite limited opportunities. His ability to generate explosive plays could make him a useful complement to Puka Nacua, but his fantasy upside will be boom-or-bust, as he's likely to operate as a touchdown-dependent option with other names ahead of him in the pecking order. At least the Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable, as Las Vegas has allowed the 10th-most receiving yards and fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury to help the Dolphins against the Bengals in Week 5. He missed the last two weeks, and his role in this low-volume passing offense is questionable; he drew seven targets in Week 1 and only three in Week 2. The Bengals defense is much improved and ranks 14th in points allowed to opposing wideouts, with no receiver topping 63 yards against them. While Douglas can stretch the field, availability and usage remain question marks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Douglas hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week healthy and help their struggling passing game in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury and was used at varying rates when healthy: seven targets in his debut followed by just three the following week. While his 94 yards in Week 1 show potential, uncertain availability and opportunity likely keep him off the radar for lineup consideration against a slightly above-average Jets' secondary that's surrendering 7.3 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chad Ryland enters Arizona's Week 2 matchup against Seattle as the NFL's co-leader in field-goal makes. Ryland converted four of five FG attempts in a Week 1 win against the Chargers, matching his 2025 season-high mark for field goals in a game. However, the veteran kicker had just 25 FG makes last year, so it may not be wise to expect such volume on a weekly basis. The Seahawks don't figure to provide Ryland with as many scoring opportunities, as they led the NFL with just 17.2 PPG allowed during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chad Ryland will hope for Arizona's offense to find more success in Week 3 against San Francisco. The Cardinals managed just seven points Sunday in a loss to Seattle, and Ryland's only scoring opportunity was a successful extra point on that score. He was much more active in Week 1, when he made four of five FG attempts and both PAT tries. The 49ers have given up an average of only 10.0 points through two games, so Ryland may see limited opportunities again in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chad Ryland heads into Arizona's Week 4 matchup versus the Giants having gotten off to a strong start to the campaign. Ryland made all three FG tries and all three point-after attempts this past Sunday against San Francisco, with his longest kick coming from 49 yards. Though he's yet to convert from 50-plus yards out this season, Ryland has been solid in going 7-for-8 on FG tries and 6-for-6 on PATs. However, his opportunities may be limited against the Giants, who have somewhat remarkably not given up a field-goal conversion through three contests this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chad Ryland showed off his leg in Week 4 and will look to do so again when the Cardinals square off against the Lions in Week 5. Though Ryland had only one field-goal attempt against the Giants this past Sunday, he impressed with a 60-yarder just before halftime. Ryland has now made eight of nine field-goal tries this season while nailing all nine of his point-after attempts. He could get plenty of opportunities against the Lions, who have given up a league-worst 31.8 points per game through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chad Ryland is coming off back-to-back quiet weeks with Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams on tap. Ryland has gone just 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts over his past two games, though he's made all six of his extra-point tries during that span. The veteran kicker does have two games with at least three FG makes on the campaign, so it's been pretty feast or famine in terms of his opportunities so far. Opponents are 9-for-11 on field-goal tries against the Rams so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chad Ryland enters Arizona's Week 7 matchup against Denver following one of the most productive kicking performances of the season. He converted all six field-goal attempts against the Rams, including a game-winning 43-yarder as time expired, accounting for all 18 of the Cardinals' points. Ryland has benefited from an Arizona offense that frequently struggles to finish drives, creating additional field-goal opportunities despite inconsistent touchdown production. However, Denver has allowed just 7.5 fantasy points per game to opposing kickers this season, making the matchup less attractive than his recent performance suggests, but he's a player to keep close tabs on either way. Ryland remains a viable streaming option, but he should continue to be a matchup-based alternative, and fantasy managers shouldn't expect six field goals on a steady basis.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals in Week 2. Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in a season-opening win against New England, though he would have had a bigger performance if not for a 24-yard touchdown grab that was nullified by a penalty. Of note, Drew Lock is expected to start behind center for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with a glute injury and is unlikely to suit up. The Cardinals aren't expected to field a top secondary this year, but they did a good job of holding Justin Herbert and the Chargers' offense in check in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cooper Kupp will look to rebound from a quiet performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Against the Chargers this past Sunday, Kupp caught just one of two targets for 13 yards. It was his lowest offensive output of the season, though he's been pretty quiet overall with two or fewer receptions in three of four contests so far. The 49ers are yielding just 123.5 receiving yards per game to wideouts, seventh-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cooper Kupp has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver on tap. Kupp has produced a modest 11 catches for 129 yards and a touchdown through five weeks, and he's posted just three catches for 28 yards in his past two games. He's regularly logging a healthy offensive snap share, but there hasn't been much room for any of Seattle's complementary wideouts to shine behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is averaging 10.0 targets per game. Kupp may need a big play or two to break out, but the Broncos are yielding just 7.65 yards per WR target, 12th-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks host the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. Kupp finished behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16) for second on the team in targets, as his 10 looks from QB Sam Darnold were a season high for the 33-year-old. He'll try to relieve some of the pressure Smith-Njigba will face versus a Kansas City defense that allows 21.2 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks first.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Patriots in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. He caught three of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory versus Atlanta. Wilson tied for second on the team in targets and was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps. Despite the solid start, it's best he remains on benches or waiver wires until he can prove to be a consistent fantasy contributor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Roman Wilson and the Steelers welcome the division rival Bengals to town for a Week 3 matchup. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, Wilson stepped into the No. 2 receiver role behind DK Metcalf. He finished the 20-3 loss with a team-high five catches for 28 yards on six targets. Rookie Germie Bernard was one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite receivers, however, turning eight targets into four catches and a team-leading 35 yards. Pittman's status is cloudy at best for Week 3, but Wilson and the Steelers face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs, so he's best left on benches for now.
outlooksByWeek.4: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 4. He caught three of six targets for 60 yards and his first touchdown of the season during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Wilson led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished second behind Darnell Washington in yardage. He has a favorable matchup versus Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs, but it's still difficult to trust him with so many mouths to feed in the Steelers' offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Roman Wilson and the Steelers take on the Colts at home in Week 5. He caught three of six targets for 74 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Wilson tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage, and he now has a TD catch in two consecutive contests. He's been a reliable option for Aaron Rodgers, as he's generated six targets in all four outings this season en route to a 14-188-2 line. Wilson's next opportunity comes against the Colts' 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Roman Wilson and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He failed to catch his only target prior to exiting Pittsburgh's 34-22 win in Week 5 with a finger injury. Wilson has already been ruled out for the trip to Tampa Bay, meaning Germie Bernard should see a boost in playing time and opportunities in his absence.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers in Week 2. Unfortunately for the second-year pro, he's expected to miss "significant time" with a left knee injury sustained in Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The severity of his injury is still being evaluated, but there's a high chance of him being placed on IR once more information comes out.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. The second-year running back, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury since September 15, could potentially return to practice ahead of their matchup with Baltimore. Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there's a "possibility" Cleveland opens the 21-day practice window for Sampson this week. If he's able to get back on the field, it couldn't come at a better time for the Browns, as they're currently dealing with injuries to Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained in Week 5's loss. It would be wise to monitor the practice reps for the entire backfield as they prepare for Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson is back for Year 2 in Cleveland after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he struggled on a small sample of work as a rusher (his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs), but was a contributor in the passing game (23rd among RBs with 33 receptions). Sampson was a young rookie (he doesn't turn 22 until September), so there's still some room for growth, and he's positioned for a larger role behind Quinshon Judkins with Jerome Ford no longer on the roster. Expect Sampson to see some change-of-pace carries and a moderate pass-catching role in 2026. He'll land on the flex radar only if Judkins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ted Hurst will look to build on his solid NFL debut in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Hurst played 75 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps and caught all three of his targets for 36 yards, taking advantage of increased opportunities with Jalen McMillan (knee) sidelined. Hurst could continue being a valuable asset to Tampa Bay's offense if McMillan continues to miss time, which he very well could in Week 2. The matchup against the Browns is also great, with that defense allowing a whopping 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Despite the return of Jalen McMillan in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, Hurst played a career-high 45 offensive snaps -- 38 more than McMillan. Additionally, Hurst led the team with seven targets, though it led to just two receptions. Regardless, it appears as if Hurst will remain an important piece of the Buccaneers' offense as the season progresses. The rookie wideout will likely struggle but could find success against a Minnesota secondary that's allowed 12.6 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ted Hurst is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Hurst has proved to be a valuable part of Tampa Bay's offense just three games into his rookie campaign, catching six of 14 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. With Jalen McMillan (knee) going down in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, Hurst's role could continue to expand as the season progresses. He will likely see fewer opportunities in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined, but the matchup remains favorable, as the Packers' defense allowed 14.2 yards per completion in a Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top wideouts in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Hurst finished with the third-most receiving yards on the Buccaneers during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching two of three targets for 25 yards. He will likely get fewer scoring opportunities with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined but should remain involved in the team's offensive game plan. Hurst could find success against a struggling Dallas secondary that's allowed 11.7 yards per reception on the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ted Hurts will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Hurst went without a target for the first time in his NFL career during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys. On the season, the rookie wideout has caught eight of 16 targets for 128 yards and a touchdown, averaging 16.0 yards per reception. He could find success against a solid Steelers secondary in Week 6 that's allowed 10.8 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ted Hurst will look to build on a solid Week 6 performance when the Buccaneers' travel to Carolina in Week 7. Hurst was Tampa Bay's second-leading receiver in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, catching three of six targets for 40 yards. While he remains firmly behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin in the Buccaneers' receiving corps, it appears as if he's established himself as the team's No. 3 wideout, at least while Jalen McMillan (knee) remains sidelined. Hurst could also benefit from the possible return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback in Week  7, but he'll likely struggle against a Carolina secondary that's allowed just 9.7 yards per completion this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurst was selected by the Buccaneers in the third round of April's draft. Granted he played at a small school, but Hurst ranked third in this rookie class target share (26%) and first in air yard share (45%) during his FBS career. A tall, vertical receiver, Hurst posted solid collegiate efficiency despite inconsistent QB play (only 68% of his 235 FBS targets were catchable, which is easily lowest among qualified WRs in this class). His 135-inch broad jump was best among wide receivers at the combine. Hurst will get some run at 'X' receiver as a rookie, but he's a longshot for consistent rookie-season fantasy production with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan in the fold.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jameis Winston will take the reins of the Giants offense in Week 3 versus the Titans. Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury and may not return this year. Winston's performance in relief of Dart last game left much to be desired, as he completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. Against Tennessee, at least Winston will have a week to prepare and face a lower-tier defense. The Titans are giving up 233.5 passing yards per game in 2026, which is 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameis Winston led the Giants to an ugly victory last game against the Titans. Winston was underwhelming to say the least, though, as he passed for under 120 yards for the second-straight outing. On a positive note, he did not throw an interception, and the Giants won the contest. However, the G-Men just traded for JJ McCarthy from the Vikings, which could put some pressure on Winston to perform. Nevertheless, Winston should remain the starter for now, and the Giants have another very winnable game in Week 4 versus the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns last game for the Giants. It was the full Jameis Winston experience, though, as the veteran also threw two interceptions. However, he finished 18-of-29 for 250 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Miraculously, the G-Men currently sit in first place in the NFC East. In Week 5, Jameis and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns for the second-consecutive week for the Giants. He also threw for over 300 yards for the first time this season in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders.  Winston did not throw a pick, though he did lose a fumble. While JJ McCarthy took a few snaps, the starting job will remain Winston's heading into a Week 6 clash with the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameis Winston was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy last game for the Giants. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt, throwing for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the Falcons for a Week 5 showdown. He rushed once for three yards and caught two of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Derrick Henry out-carried Hill 23-1, even with Lamar Jackson missing the entire second half with an ankle injury. It appears that regardless of who's under center, the Ravens' backfield belongs to Henry. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against an Atlanta defense allowing just 17.9 points per game to RBs, which ranks ninth.
outlooksByWeek.6: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He rushed four times for 73 yards and caught two of four targets for five yards during Baltimore's Week 5 overtime win. Derrick Henry out-carried him 24-4, although Hill led the way with a game-long 47-yard run. However, as long as Henry is the lead back and the Ravens don't fall into a massive deficit, Hill's involvement in the offense will remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.7: Justice Hill and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He did not record a carry but brought in all three of his targets for nine yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Derrick Henry accounted for 17 of the 18 rushing attempts out of the Ravens' backfield, a trend that should continue as long as he remains healthy. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against a Cincinnati defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendrick Bourne had a promising performance for Arizona in Week 1 and will look to be productive again versus the Seahawks in Week 2. Bourne led Cardinals wideouts with eight catches and 75 yards in a season-opening victory versus the Chargers, with only stud tight end Trey McBride outpacing his eight targets. The veteran Bourne looked to have great rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett, so it will be interesting to see how the target distribution shakes out in Week 2 and beyond. He won't have an easy matchup against Seattle, who limited New England to 178 yards through the air in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendrick Bourne is coming off two quiet weeks heading into Arizona's Week 4 tilt versus the Giants. After posting an 8-75-0 receiving line in the season opener against the Chargers, the veteran wideout has managed a modest four catches on six targets for 33 yards combined over his subsequent two games. Bourne appears to be well behind WR Michael Wilson and TE Trey McBride, and at least marginally behind WR Marvin Harrison, in the passing-game pecking order at the moment. There could be an opportunity to make some noise against a Giants defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendrick Bourne is looking to re-involve himself in Arizona's offense in Week 5 against the Lions. Bourne logged a healthy 42 of 66 offensive snaps against the Giants in Week 4, but he didn't draw a single target from QB Jacoby Brissett. In fact, Bourne has logged just six total targets across his past three games after posting an 8-75-0 line on eight targets in the Cardinals' season opener. Detroit could provide an opportunity for Bourne to get going, as the Lions have given up a league-high 61 total catches to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kendrick Bourne seems set for a major role in Arizona's offense ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. With Marvin Harrison now officially traded to the Texans, Bourne figures to slot in behind Michael Wilson as the Cardinals' No. 2 wideout. That positioning led to a nice game for Bourne this past Sunday against Detroit, as he outproduced Wilson with a 5-70-0 line on eight targets. The Rams could present a challenge, however, as they've yielded the fewest catches per game (8.0) to wideouts through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kendrick Bourne has established himself as a regular contributor in Arizona's passing attack, catching 22 passes for 225 yards through six games, though he hasn't found the end zone. The veteran wideout is averaging a career-low 10.2 yards per catch in 2026, but that's also due to the struggles the Cardinals' passing attack has had with Jacoby Brissett under center. To make things even more complicated, he'll face the Broncos' secondary in Week 7, and Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026. That makes Bourne a difficult player to trust outside deeper PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Holani looks to be locked in as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. That role didn't yield much fruit for Holani in Week 4, however, as he recorded just 18 yards on seven carries and two yards on one reception. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson recorded 120 total yards and two TDs on 24 touches, so he looks to be in full control of the backfield for the time being. San Francisco has given up just two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) to running backs this season, so they aren't a great draw for a player like Holani who probably needs to get into the end zone to put up meaningful fantasy points.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Holani will likely need to better protect the ball in Week 6 against the Broncos if he wants to continue getting opportunities in Seattle's ground game. Holani fumbled twice this past Sunday against the 49ers, and the fumble that was recovered by San Francisco was a game-changer, as it resulted in a touchdown just before halftime. With that said, Seattle is depleted at running back with Zach Charbonnet (knee - ACL) out at least another week and Jadrian Price (chest) on IR until at least early November, so Holani should get an opportunity to redeem himself against Denver. The Broncos are giving up 21.1 fantasy points per game to RBs, eighth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Holani and the Seahawks host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown during Seattle's 17-14 loss in overtime in Week 6. Holani made the most of his touches by scoring his first rushing TD of the season, but he's expected to have his opportunities reduced with the likely return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) off the reserve/PUP list. It would be wise to steer clear of the Seahawks backfield against a Kansas City defense allowing 19.0 fantasy points allowed per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

player.seasonOutlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price and Emanuel Wilson for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colby Parkinson will aim to be more productive when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Parkinson led Los Angeles tight ends with 47 offensive snaps in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he caught just one pass for six yards. The Rams had three other tight ends log at least 12 offensive snaps in the contest, so the week-to-week individual production among that group could vary widely throughout the season. The Giants held Dallas' starting tight end, Jake Ferguson, to just two catches for six yards in Week 1, so Los Angeles' tight-end corps could have trouble as a whole.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colby Parkinson has had a quiet start to the season heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. Parkinson logged just one catch Week 1 and followed that with a 2-15-0 receiving line on Monday Night Football. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson put up a 6-54-1 line, proving that there's room for players at the position to thrive with QB Matthew Stafford -- though who that tight end is could vary on a week-to-week basis. Denver was burned by Travis Kelce for 71 yards in Week 1 but held Jaguars TEs to just 24 receiving yards in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Colby Parkinson is uncertain to be able to play in the Rams' Week 4 clash against the Eagles due to a shoulder injury. Parkinson suffered the injury in Week 3 against Denver and finished the game with no catches on one target. Meanwhile, veteran Tyler Higbee put up a strong 8-62-1 line and could be poised for more opportunities even if Parkinson does end up playing. Philadelphia has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 3.0 fantasy points per game to the position, second-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colby Parkinson didn't play in Week 4 and isn't certain to suit up in Week 5 for the Rams' matchup against Buffalo. Parkinson is dealing with a shoulder and a knee injury, and his practice participation level this week should help determine if he'll be able to suit up against the Bills. Tyler Higbee has had consecutive big games for Los Angeles and could work as the team's top TE even if Parkinson is able to play in Week 5. The Rams' offense often provides opportunities for multiple tight ends to thrive, though Buffalo has given up just 6.3 fantasy points per game to the position so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colby Parkinson may have officially fallen behind Tyler Higbee in Los Angeles' tight-end pecking order heading into a matchup versus the Cardinals in Week 6. Parkinson logged just one catch on two targets for three yards Monday against Buffalo while Higbee went off again with a 5-83-0 receiving line on six targets. The good news for Parkinson is that he was able to suit up following a one-week absence, but he's yet to register more than two catches in a game so far this season. With that in mind, he could struggle to produce in Week 6 despite facing an Arizona defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points per game (13.3) to tight ends through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colby Parkinson operates as the Rams' main blocking tight end, and while he's going to have a few catches here and there, he's behind Tyler Higbee in terms of the pecking order in the passing game. The matchup is favorable against the Raiders, who have allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, but Parkinson's lack of involvement will limit his upside overall. He has just nine catches for 55 yards and a touchdown in five games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Elliott was perfect on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Eagles. Elliott connected on a 33-yard field goal as well as three extra points in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. In Week 2, Elliott will face a Titans squad that allowed a plethora of points last season. Tennessee gave up an average of 28.1 points per clash in 2025, which was 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Elliott nailed a 58-yard field goal in Philadelphia's last game. Elliott has not missed a kick through two games for the Eagles, connecting on two field goals and six PATs. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears squad allowing 23 points per contest, which is in the middle of the pack thus far this NFL season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Elliott did not attempt a field goal last game for the Eagles, as the offense was stymied in the 27-7 loss to the Bears. Elliott did hit his lone extra point, though has now made just two field goals in three contests thus far this season. In Week 4, Philadelphia will face a Rams squad allowing 21 points per tilt, which is tied for 13th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Elliott still managed two field goals and two extra points last game for Philadelphia, despite massive struggles on offense for the Eagles. Elliott has just four field goals through four contests, as the Philadelphia offense has sputtered in part due to a bevy of injuries to skill players. With DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and potentially Saquon Barkley sidelined for Week 5 versus the Jags, points may be at a premium. The Jags have also been extremely stingy in terms of points allowed this season. Jacksonville is giving up only 13.3 points per tilt, which is second in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jake Elliott connected on his lone field goal attempt last game for the Eagles. Elliott made a 48-yarder that initially looked like the game-winner, only for Philadelphia to somehow squander away the victory. Elliott has hit one field goal or fewer in all but one game in 2026, as the Eagles offense has struggled due to injury and inconsistency. However, in Week 6, the Eagles will face a Panthers squad allowing 27.3 points per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Elliott managed just two extra points last game for the Eagles, as the Philadelphia offense sputtered without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee lined up under center, and should continue to be the quarterback as Hurts will be sidelined for the season. Even with Hurts at the helm, the Eagles offense had failed to score more than 20 points in each of the previous three contests. Saquon Barkley continues to be sidelined as well. In sum, Elliott's prospects for a plethora of points does not look hopeful, even against a Dallas squad in Week 7 allowing 26.5 points per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley wasn't targeted in Tennessee's season opener and is off the fantasy radar completely heading into a Week 2 home game against the elite Eagles secondary. The veteran WR may be as low as fifth in the Titans' WR pecking order behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike. Second-year QB Cam Ward has struggled to keep any of his pass catchers consistently fantasy-relevant, let alone depth options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.
outlooksByWeek.5: Calvin Ridley has just three catches for 48 yards on five targets through four games. He's barely contributing as the No. 4 WR in a Titans offense that's averaging just 13.8 points per game, which is the second-fewest in the NFL. Even in a Week 5 matchup against a Texans defense that has struggled to defend wide receivers, Ridley remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.6: Calvin Ridley hasn't exceeded 35 yards in a game this season and has been blanked twice. The 31-year-old wide receiver appears to have lost a step after fracturing his fibula last season and has fallen to No. 4 on Tennessee's wide receiver depth chart behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, and Elic Ayomanor. With QB Cam Ward averaging a meager 179 passing yards per game, Ridley is unlikely to post his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season in Week 6, even against the Colts' subpar secondary.
outlooksByWeek.7: Calvin Ridley finished without a catch in three of six games this season for the Titans and has just five receptions for 81 yards overall. The veteran WR has been relegated to a depth role at this stage of his career and can continue to be ignored in fantasy. After improving to 1-5 with a Week 6 win over the Colts, the Titans will host the 4-2 Browns in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance. The lost season comes after Ridley delivered consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, finishing both as a top-30 fantasy receiver. Ridley is now 31 years old and has added target competition with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson in the mix. A Year 2 leap from Cam Ward could get Ridley back into the flex discussion, but it's more likely that he's headed for a reduced role. Ridley is worth no more than a middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Willis looks to rebound from a shaky debut when the Dolphins again travel west to face the 49ers in Week 2. Willis was held without a touchdown pass in his first start for his new team, and while the rushing volume was lower than expected, he scampered for a touchdown. It's a challenging road spot against a defense that allowed just 168 yards passing and no scores in their opener, but game flow should remain positive for Willis to flirt with fantasy-worthy production. Miami will likely play from behind, necessitating throws, and dropbacks will continue to lead to rushing yards when pressured.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Willis figures to labor again in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has yet to top 220 yards or complete more than 15 passes through two games, and his rushing attempts haven't been as plentiful as anticipated. Any potential late production while playing from behind has also failed to manifest, and that game script figures to repeat in Week 3 against Kansas City, a defense that's allowed only 341 passing yards, two touchdown passes, and 12 rushing yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Willis will be under heavy pressure when the Dolphins face the Vikings in Week 4. Willis has just one touchdown pass through three weeks and has surprisingly topped 40 yards with his legs just once. Minnesota is the heaviest blitzing team in the league, so Willis will likely need his mobility often in Week 4. Without De'Von Achane (knee) and no emerging receivers, scrambling appears his only path to production against a defense that's allowing 7.0 yards per attempt while also allowing three touchdowns with four interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Willis will seek a breakthrough outing in Week 5 when the Dolphins face the Bengals. He has accounted for just two total touchdowns through four games and completed a mere nine passes for 85 yards in Week 4, both season-lows. An improved Cincinnati defense has allowed only four touchdown passes, but all of them have come over the last two weeks. With Miami's defense likely to give up points, Willis will at least have the opportunity to produce at a higher level than he's shown thus far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Willis hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week with answers to get their offense in gear during a Week 7 matchup with the Jets. He has been held under 200 yards passing in three of his five games and has only two touchdown passes but has shown signs of his dual-threat capability, averaging 47.0 rushing yards over his last three contests. The Jets have allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks thus far, surrendering only nine touchdown passes and 92 rushing yards in six games, boding poorly for Willis's chances to shine.

player.seasonOutlook: Willis signed with Miami during the offseason and is set to start after two successful seasons backing up Jordan Love in Green Bay. Willis, a 2022 third-round pick, has very little experience (155 career pass attempts), but he was outstanding in limited work the past two seasons, completing 70 of 89 passes for 972 yards, six TDs and zero INTs (12.1 yards per attempt, 86% completion rate), while also adding major value with his legs (42-261-3) during the span. Willis played at least 80% of the snaps in three games with Green Bay and averaged 23.3 fantasy points in those outings. Willis' inexperience makes him risky and the Miami supporting cast is perhaps the worst in the NFL, but his dual-threat ability makes him a very fascinating late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.6: Pierre Strong could serve as Green Bay's secondary option at running back once again in Week 6 against the Cowboys. With Chris Brooks on IR with an ankle injury, Strong was brought up for Week 5 versus the Bears. The fourth-year ball carrier ended up serving as the Packers' No. 2 option instead of Kaleb Johnson, with MarShawn Lloyd leading the ground attack. Strong recorded five carries for seven yards and three catches for 11 yards off four targets. If the hierarchy stays the same, he could be in for another game of solid usage facing a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pierre Strong will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Strong led Green Bay's backfield in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, rushing the ball 11 times for 28 yards and catching five of six targets for 39 yards. The fourth-year running back looks to be a more dynamic option than MarShawn Lloyd moving forward, but both players could see a diminished role with Josh Jacobs set to return from the Commissioner's Exempt list. Detroit has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: AJ Barner is coming off a quiet season opener as Seattle heads to Arizona in Week 2. Barner logged just two catches on two targets for 13 yards against the Patriots last Wednesday, though those two receptions were tied for second-most on the squad. Drew Lock played most of that game at QB for Seattle, and he's expected to start in Week 2 with Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury. The Cardinals gave up seven catches for 90  yards to Chargers tight ends in a win Sunday, so Barner could be a key target for Lock.
outlooksByWeek.3: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: AJ Barner will look to build upon a big Week 3 performance when Seattle hosts the Chargers in Week 4. Against the Commanders this past Sunday, Barner registered season-high marks with five catches, nine targets and 69 yards. That production was particularly notable after the third-year tight end compiled just three catches on three targets for 21 yards over the first two weeks of the campaign. Barner could find additional success against the Chargers, who rank in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: AJ Barner will look to amp up his production for Seattle in a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. Barner caught just one of three targets for 12 yards against the Chargers this past Sunday after posting a promising 5-69-0 receiving line the previous week. Barner logged nine targets in that Week 3 win over Washington, but he's drawn three or fewer targets in each of his other three contests. San Francisco has been tough against tight ends this season, giving up just 4.0 points per game to the position (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.6: AJ Barner will look to get more involved as a pass catcher for Seattle in Week 6 against the Broncos. Barner caught three of five targets for 20 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, with each of the catch, target and yardage totals representing his second-highest mark this season. Barner logged six receiving touchdowns across 17 regular-season games last year, but his only score this season has been on his lone rush attempt. Denver has struggled a bit against tight ends this season, giving up 9.9 fantasy points per game, ninth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: AJ Barner and the Seahawks return home for an interconference tilt against the Chiefs in Week 7. He caught three of four targets for 16 yards during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. Outside of his five-catch, 69-yard performance (9 targets) in Week 3, Barner has a 10-69-0 receiving line on 15 targets in his other five games combined. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba commanding most of QB Sam Darnold's attention, it's hard to trust Barner as anything more than a backup TE. However, he could be a solid streaming option versus Kansas City's 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.0) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season.
