The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

outlooksByWeek.2: Tank Bigsby managed just one carry for the Eagles in Week 1. Bigsby rushed once for three yards in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. Meanwhile, fellow backup Will Shipley garnered three total touches for 12 yards. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans.  Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tank Bigsby returned to his backup role last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley recovered from his stinger, Bigsby did not receive a carry in the dismal loss to the Bears. Barring injury, Bigsby will get little run in Week 4 versus the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Will Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Bigsby was acquired by the Eagles early in the 2025 season and progressively worked his way up to primary backup duties, a role he's expected to play again in 2026. Granted, it's a small sample, but Bigsby has been extremely efficient over the last two seasons. Among 48 backs with 200-plus carries during the span, Bigsby ranks first in yards after contact per attempt (2.75) and eighth in yards per carry (4.86). In fact, Bigsby has led qualified RBs in YAC each of the last two seasons. On the other hand, he hasn't been used much as a receiver (20 career targets). With overworked Saquon Barkley entering his age-29 season, Bigsby certainly has some insurance appeal, even if he defers passing-down work to Will Shipley. Bigsby, 25, is worth consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.7: Tanner McKee started last game at quarterback for the Eagles, and he could potentially find himself under center for the foreseeable future. Starter Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for the remainder of the season due to blood clots, leaving McKee as next in line under center. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown last game versus the Panthers. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nick Folk will look to bounce back from a tough performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. The 41-year-old went made just three of the five kicks he attempted in the Week 1 loss, missing field-goals from 54 and 45 yards. He could be in line to continue receiving scoring opportunities, with Atlanta's offense struggling to find the end zone last week. Additionally, Folk is in for a great matchup, with Carolina allowing 11 kicking points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nick Folk's early-season struggled could continue in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers, who have allowed just 6.0 kicking points per game this season. Through two games in 2026, Folk has made just three of six field-goal tries, which is the worst mark in the NFL. He could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix, however, who is expected to drive improvement after Atlanta's offense averaged just 8.0 points per game prior to his return.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Folk has struggled through three weeks this season, converting on just five of eight field-goal tries while making all four point-after attempts. He had his best game of the year in the Week 3 win over the Packers, making all five of his kicks (two field goals and three extra points). With Michael Penix back at the helm, Folk could see more scoring opportunities going forward. Additionally, Folk is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 7.7 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nick Folk is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, Folk has converted all 12 of his kicks (three field goals and nine extra points), averaging 9.0 kicking points per game. With Atlanta's recent offensive success (40.0 points per game over the last two weeks) and Baltimore's defense having allowed 24.0 points and 7.5 kicking points per game, Folk is expected to have a favorable Week 5 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nick Folk will likely continue having scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Folk was perfect in the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, making three field goals and two extra points. On the season, he's converted on nine of 12 field-goal tries but all 12 of his point-after attempts. He could have plenty of scoring chance in Week 6, as Chicago's defense just allowed 31 points while Packers' kicker Trey Smack attempted six kicks (three field goals and three extra points).
outlooksByWeek.7: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities when the Falcons take on the 49ers in Week  7. Folk converted on his lone point-after attempt in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, with the Falcons converting on two two-point conversions in the second half. On the season, Folk has made nine of 12 field-goal tries and all 13 of his point-after attempts. The veteran kicker is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup as well, with San Francisco's defense giving up 8.6 kicking points per game through five contests this year.

player.seasonOutlook: So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 showdown against the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for 18 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 win over the Falcons. Washington and Pat Freiermuth were co-starters at TE, but the latter tallied five catches for 46 yards and a TD. New England's defense is very stingy against the position, as they rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (3.3) to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darnell Washington and the Steelers host the Colts in a matchup between 2-2 teams in Week 5. In Week 4, he played 70% of offensive snaps and caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown. Fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth (3-17-1) was also productive, playing 75% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like they'll have a nearly even snap split as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel to square off against the 1-4 Buccaneers in Week 6. He played 34 snaps on offense (63%) en route to catching two of three targets for 12 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Fellow starting tight end Pat Freiermuth was on the field for 38 offensive snaps (70%) and was the more productive of the two, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two TDs. The playing time will continue to be relatively similar, making Washington a boom-or-bust fantasy option against Tampa Bay's 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.7) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darnell Washington and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference tilt against the Saints in Week 7. He brought in four of six targets for 25 yards and a touchdown during Pittsburgh's thrilling comeback victory in overtime in Week 6. Washington and fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth each played 71% of the offensive snaps, lending more credibility to the "your turn, my turn" trend that's developing in 2026. He'll look to exploit New Orleans' 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.6) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

outlooksByWeek.5: Kimani Vidal is coming off his most productive game of 2026, taking five carries for 25 yards and turning three targets into a 2-11-1 line during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. While the seven touches represented a season high for Vidal, they still trailed Keaton Mitchell's 15 and Omarion Hampton's 11. Mitchell led the trio with 63 scrimmage yards, while Hampton scored a rushing TD. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is drifting toward a full-blown committee as he searches for a spark, but it would likely take an injury ahead of him for Vidal to gain significant volume on a consistent basis. He'll try to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kimani Vidal posted a season-high nine touches in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, turning eight carries into 57 yards and his first rushing touchdown of the season while also catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. The third-year back has gotten into the end zone in back-to-back games, but Vidal remains firmly in a committee with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, and none of the three would seem to have a significant ceiling while working behind a patchwork offensive line. Vidal will try to keep his TD streak going in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Returning for his third year with the Chargers, Vidal is set to compete with newcomer Keaton Mitchell for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. Vidal had some big moments in 2025, clearing 17 fantasy points in four games, but the notable disclaimer here is that Hampton was sidelined for all of those outings. In fact, Vidal scored only 4.1 fantasy PPG in his other nine games. The 2024 sixth-round pick is a fine depth player who showed he can handle big workloads when needed, but he'll be worth rostering only should Hampton miss time and, even then, Mitchell figures to play a role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Shipley managed just three touches for the Eagles in Week 1.  Meanwhile, fellow backup Tank Bigsby had just one carry for three yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Shipley managed nine touches for 29 yards in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Shipley and Tank Bigsby would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge, as the latter had 15 touches and a touchdown to outpace Shipley. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears run defense allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Shipley may be the only healthy running back left for the Eagles. Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags, as is Barkley's due to a hamstring ailment. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. Shipley did have six rushes for 23 yards following the injury to Bigsby. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Will Shipley found the end zone last game for the Eagles but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo had a rough debut Week 1 for the Commanders. On only three targets, the former Titan caught a mere two passes for 16 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. He subsequently injured his hamstring and did not return. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. John Bates and Ben Sinnott would step in at tight end if Chig misses Week 2 versus Dallas. If he suits up, Okonkwo would have a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that allowed two touchdowns to Giants tight end Isaiah Likely in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chig Okonkwo is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4. John Bates has handled the tight end slot amid limited fanfare without Okonkwo, as Bates caught a nine-yard pass last game in Okonkwo's absence. If Okonkwo can suit up in Week 4, he may have an intriguing matchup versus the Colts, even with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chig Okonkwo returned to the lineup for the Commanders following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment. Okonkwo was targeted four times, but managed two catches for a mere five yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, though, which would certainly be a boost for the passing game. However, New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chig Okonkwo made his presence felt for Washington in his return to the lineup. Following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment, Okonkwo led the team with six targets en route to four catches for 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career). As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malachi Fields scored his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. The rookie flashed his big-play ability, snagging a 40-yarder from quarterback Jameis Winston along with the 12-yard score. He finished with two catches for a career-best 52 yards and the touchdown. In Week 5, Fields and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malachi Fields saw just two targets last game for the Giants. Meanwhile, star teammate Malik Nabers had a staggering 20 looks in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders. The production for the rookie Fields has been rather consistent through five contests, as he has two catches in every outing. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malachi Fields finished third on the Giants in targets last game. Fields was targeted eight times, though managed two catches for just 18 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Fields has emerged as the No. 2 wideout behind Malik Nabers, though Isaiah Likely at tight end has also been extremely busy as a pass catcher. Fields has at least two catches in every game he's played, though has just 12 catches on the season. In Week 7, the Giants will face a porous Texans secondary allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wil Lutz's opportunities were minimal in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, converting his only extra point and his sole field-goal attempt from 31 yards. The veteran kicker had been productive in his first three years with Denver, averaging just under 30 FGs and 38 extra points per season while going 12-for-18 on field-goal attempts of 50-plus yards. In Week 2, Lutz will take on a Jaguars team that ranked eighth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wil Lutz has been perfect to begin the season for the Broncos, and in a Week 2 win over the Jaguars, he converted both his field-goal attempts and both his PATs. The veteran kicker has been consistent since following Sean Payton northwest from New Orleans, and kicking at altitude has allowed him to be reliable from long range, but the Denver offense doesn't provide him with enough opportunities to be among the elite at his position. Lutz will face a Rams team in Week 3 that just kept the Giants out of the end zone but which has allowed five FG attempts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wil Lutz missed his first kick of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, hitting the left upright on a 43-yard field goal attempt but connecting on both his extra points. Game flow cost him opportunities, as Denver headed into halftime down 16-0 and attempted two-point conversions multiple times as part of their comeback. Lutz has converted three FGs and five extra points through three games, and his volume may not improve substantially until his offense develops some consistency. He'll take on a 49ers team in Week 4 that's allowed just 16.7 points a game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wil Lutz continues to get little volume thanks to the struggles of the Broncos' offense. Through four games, the veteran kicker has attempted only five extra points, converting all, while going just 5-for-7 on FG attempts, with one of his misses coming from 58 yards out. Lutz is reliable, especially with most of his games coming either at altitude or indoors, but without more opportunities, he won't be able to make much of a contribution. He could get more chances in Week 5 against a Chargers team that has allowed 26.5 points per game, 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wil Lutz has missed field goal attempts in the Broncos' last two games, but he's also benefited from increased volume, going 5-for-7 on FGs and 2-for-2 on PATs. The veteran kicker has had his production dragged down by the struggles of the offense, but with Sean Payton calling plays again, Lutz's outlook has brightened a little. He'll face a Seahawks team in Week 6 that's allowed 21.0 points per game this season, eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wil Lutz played hero for the Broncos in Week 6, with his only field goal coming in overtime during a win over the Seahawks. The veteran kicker's volume is inconsistent thanks to Denver's struggling offense, and through six games, he's gone 9-for-12 on FG attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra points. Lutz could be busier than usual in Week 7 against a Cardinals team that's allowed 29.7 points per game, tied with the Saints for the worst mark in the league.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens travel to take on the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. He filled in well for Lamar Jackson (ankle) after the star quarterback missed the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, completing eight of nine passes for 63 yards while rushing four times for 16 yards. The Ravens wanted to manage their lead with Jackson on the sidelines, and although it doesn't sound like his ankle issue is long-term, there's a decent chance Huntley could be thrust into the Week 5 starting role at Atlanta.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a Week 6 AFC North showdown. In place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle) in Week 5, Huntley threw for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score, helping Baltimore escape with a 30-23 overtime victory. Jackson's availability against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to QBs is still in question, so keep an eye on his practice participation leading up to Week 6. If the Ravens opt to play it safe with their superstar quarterback, Huntley could again be tasked with leading the offense as they look to improve to 5-1 on the season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens return home for a divisional clash against the Bengals in Week 7. He completed 19 of 31 pass attempts for 165 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing five times for 28 yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. It was an underwhelming day for the Ravens' offense, which accumulated just 252 total yards and scored all 10 of their points in the opening quarter. Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status for Week 7 is still murky at best, meaning Huntley could earn a second straight start against a Cincinnati defense allowing 21.5 fantasy points per game (19th) to QBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Ward dropped to 3-19 as a starter for the Titans with a 26-3 loss to the Texans in Week 5, throwing an interception that dropped his season TD:INT to 3:3. He has declined in his second season after posting a 15:7 TD:INT as a rookie, while his passing yards per game have dropped from 186 in 2025 to 179 this year. Even against a Colts defense that's giving up the fifth-most passing yards per game, Ward can't be trusted in Week 6 fantasy lineups outside of deep superflex or multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Ward and the Titans finally earned their first win of the season in Week 6 against the Colts, though the second-year QB certainly wasn't the primary driving force in the victory, as he threw for just 102 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. Ward has mustered just four touchdown passes through six starts in his sophomore season while averaging 166 passing yards per game. He'll face a franchise that's all too familiar with subpar QB play in Week 7, taking on a Browns team that's off to a surprisingly strong 4-2 start this season while boasting one of the league's 10 stingiest defenses in terms of both passing yards and points allowed per game. Between Ward's own shortcomings and the tricky matchup, it's best to avoid him in fantasy for Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Wright's role in the Dolphins' offense is limited entering a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. Despite being their No. 2 back, Wright played just 6% of their offensive snaps to De'Von Achane's 88%. With Miami likely falling behind early and being forced to pass, Wright is far more insurance for Achane managers than a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Wright hasn't emerged from the Dolphins' backfield ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Bengals. After missing Week 3, Wright was thought to have an ascending role following De'Von Achane's season-ending knee injury but received only five carries in Week 4 while Ollie Gordon shined with 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. It doesn't appear Wright was limited by the foot issue that cost him a game, as he remained the team's primary kick returner. Facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry should afford Wright additional running lanes, but the role uncertainty puts Wright in wait-and-see territory rather than as a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Wright hopes to come out of the Dolphins' bye with a larger role in Week 7 against the Jets. Wright has only amassed 11 carries over his last two outings, finishing with 18 yards while not being targeted in the passing game. Ollie Gordon has dominated backfield work since De'Von Achane (knee) went down for the season, leaving managers in a wait-and-see mode with regards to Wright against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, ranking near the middle of the pack league-wide.

player.seasonOutlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

outlooksByWeek.2: Seth McGowan had the only touch by a Colts RB other than Jonathan Taylor in the season opener. McGowan and fellow backup DJ Giddens are irrelevant for fantasy purposes as long as Taylor is available. Taylor handled 22 touches in Week 1 and is expected to maintain a workhorse role in Week 2 at Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.3: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Seth McGowan has seven career touches heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London, four of which came in the Week 3 win over Houston. With star RB Jonathan Taylor healthy, McGowan's workload is expected to remain limited in Week 4 against Washington's stout run defense. McGowan's fantasy value is purely as a bench insurance policy in case of a Taylor injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Seth McGowan got seven touches in the Week 4 win over the Commanders, as the Colts built a big enough lead to give Jonathan Taylor some late-game rest for the first time this season. Those seven touches equaled McGowan's touch total from his first three games combined. The rookie seventh-round pick remains a distant second behind Taylor on the Colts' RB depth chart heading into a Week 5 road game against the Steelers. McGowan has minimal standalone fantasy value as long as Taylor is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.6: Seth McGowan has 20 touches for 71 yards through five NFL games with the Colts. The rookie seventh-round pick is a distant second on Indianapolis' RB depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor. There is a greater chance than usual of the Colts pulling away and resting Taylor in a Week 6 home game against the 0-5 Titans, but banking on a lopsided game is an unreliable strategy, so McGowan is best left out of fantasy lineups in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Seth McGowan has turned 21 carries and four targets into 98 scrimmage yards through six NFL appearances with the Colts. With starter Jonathan Taylor healthy heading into a Week 7 trip to Minnesota, McGowan projects to remain in a low-volume, change-of-pace role. The rookie seventh-round pick has minimal standalone fantasy potential and isn't a recommended option against the Vikings, who boast the league's stingiest scoring defense at 12.8 points allowed per game.

player.seasonOutlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kayshon Boutte was held to one catch in his Texans debut, so he doesn't profile as a viable fantasy option for Week 2 against the Bengals. Boutte may still be learning the playbook after being acquired in an Aug. 24 trade from New England, and facing a tough Buffalo secondary didn't help things in Week 1, but he will need to demonstrate greater involvement in the game plan to warrant lineup consideration outside the deepest of formats. Cincinnati's secondary played well in Week 1, as no Buccaneers WR exceeded 63 yards against them.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kayshon Boutte had three catches in his second game with the Texans in Week 2 after going without a catch in his team debut. He's probably the best downfield option in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), who looks likely to sit out again in Week 3 against the Colts after missing the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. The Colts have talent in their secondary, led by CB Sauce Gardner, but they are vulnerable to big plays through the air since they often leave their cornerbacks in one-on-one coverage with receivers. Indianapolis has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL this season, so Boutte has starter-level upside in deep leagues for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kayshon Boutte has 79 yards on nine targets through three games with the Texans heading into a Week 4 home game against the vulnerable Dallas secondary. Boutte's 8.8 yards per target (YPT) trails only Jaylin Noel's 11.2 YPT among Houston's wideouts, while Xavier Hutchinson (21 targets; 5.7 YPT) and Jared Wayne (12 targets; 5.4 YPT) haven't done much with their chances. The Texans traded for Boutte in late August, so it's possible he's being brought along slowly and could start to see his role increase, especially if Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game in Week 4. Until Boutte starts getting more opportunities, the former Patriots WR will be difficult to trust in any format.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 29 receiving yards per game and has yet to score this season for the Texans. The former Patriots wide receiver hasn't shown enough with his new team to warrant lineup consideration in most fantasy formats in Week 5 against a Titans defense that has allowed three TDs to WRs through four games. Three other Texans wideouts have more yards than Boutte this season, as does TE Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 31 receiving yards per game and has yet to score as a member of the Texans. Houston doesn't seem happy with the August trade acquisition from New England, considering the Texans dipped back into the trade market at wide receiver after their Week 5 win over the Titans and acquired Marvin Harrison from Arizona. Even if Harrison isn't ready to assume a prominent role in Week 6, Boutte hasn't shown enough to warrant fantasy consideration outside the deepest of formats, even in a favorable matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing the most yards per game to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Boutte was traded to the Texans in August. Reportedly a cut/trade candidate throughout most of the 2025 offseason, Boutte went on to lead the AFC champion Patriots' wide receiver room in routes and touchdowns while playing 67% of the offensive snaps when active. Despite the generous usage in a good offense, Boutte wasn't a reliable fantasy option, averaging 8.9 fantasy PPG. After seeing a career-high nine targets in Week 1, Boutte didn't clear five in a game the rest of the regular season. The 2023 sixth-round pick has finished in the range of 500-600 yards each of the last two seasons and has yet to produce a top-50 fantasy campaign. Now with Houston, Boutte will compete with Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for Houston's No. 2 receiver role behind Nico Collins. Even if he wins that job, he doesn't figure to see enough work to find his way into the weekly flex discussion.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cade Otton will likely operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Otton caught just three of five targets for 26 yards in the Week 1 loss, but he was on the field for 56 of 57 offensive snaps, solidifying his role as Tampa Bay's top tight end. Additionally, Otton received the third-most targets on the Buccaneers, suggesting there's more production on the way. He's in for a favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 34 total points and 12.2 PPR fantasy points to TEs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Through two weeks, Otton is tied for the most targets (11) and second-most receptions (eight) on the Buccaneers, which is a good sign for his outlook moving forward. He's currently on pace to finish with career highs in targets (93) and receptions (68), though is role could diminish once Jalen McMillan returns to full speed. Otton is in for a difficult matchup in Week 3, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 PPR fantasy points per game to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cade Otton is expected to remain a crucial part of Tampa Bay's offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Otton had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, catching three of six targets for 56 yards. Through three weeks, Otton is the only Buccaneers tight end to record a reception, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton could struggle in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) set to miss time, but the matchup remains favorable, as Green Bay has allowed 11.5 PPR points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cade Otton will operate as the Buccaneers' top tight end in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Otton led Tampa Bay in receiving yards during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, hauling in four of six targets for 37 yards. He appears to have a connection with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and could be a solid spot-start in Week 5, especially while facing a Dallas defense that's given up 15.3 fantasy points per game and three receiving touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Otton had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching three of four targets for 25 yards. However, he ranks second on the Buccaneers in targets (27) and receiving yards (182) through five games, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Pittsburgh defense that's given up 13.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top pass catchers in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Otton struggled during the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, hauling in one of two targets for four yards. Despite this, he played 100% of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting more fantasy production is coming in the near future. Otton is also in for a favorable matchup in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has given up 16.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2026. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Nailor didn't make much of a splash in his Raiders debut, catching three of five targets for 27 yards in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Tre Tucker and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Nailor has yet to earn much of a role as a pass catcher through his first three weeks as a Raider. While the fifth-year wide receiver does the kind of grunt work as a blocker that keeps him on the field, he's seen only 11 targets from Kirk Cousins and caught just five of them for 52 yards and zero touchdowns. With Brock Bowers making his season debut in Week 3 and immediately reclaiming his spot as the team's top target, Nailor's path to meaningful volume got even narrower. He faces a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Nailor's tough start to his Raiders tenure continued in Week 4, as he failed to get a target before leaving the game early due to a concussion. The former Viking has a meager 5-52-0 line on just 11 targets through four weeks, and while his spot in the lineup seems secure when he's healthy due to his blocking ability, he hasn't established much chemistry with Kirk Cousins despite the fact that the duo played together in Minnesota. If Nailor does clear the concussion protocol in time, he'll be little more than a dart throw in Week 5, even against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and which could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Nailor sat out the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots with a concussion, but his absence may not last much longer. Whether he finds a bigger role in the game plan is another question. The former Viking has caught just five of 11 targets for 52 yards through four games, and his primary value in Klint Kubiak's offensive scheme seems to be as a blocker. Las Vegas doesn't have a true No. 1 wide receiver, with tight end Brock Bowers serving as Kirk Cousins' top option, so the door is still open for Nailor to work his way up in the pecking order. Assuming he's cleared to return, he'll get a great opportunity in Week 6 against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Nailor returned in Week 6 from a one-game absence due to a concussion, but he was able to turn four targets into just one nine-yard catch. The former Viking remains an afterthought in the Raiders' passing game, and through five contests, he's managed just a 6-61-0 line on 15 targets. Nailor's prospects could improve if Fernando Mendoza replaces Kirk Cousins under center at some point, but he'd likely need injuries to the likes of Brock Bowers or Tre Tucker to be anything more than the No. 4 option for either QB. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nailor signed with the Raiders and will battle the likes of Tre Tucker and second-year receivers Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in Las Vegas' new-look offense. Nailor was a rarely used commodity during his first four NFL seasons, all with the Vikings. The 2022 sixth-round pick totaled a 69-1,066-11 receiving line and never reached 30 catches or 450 yards in a single season. In fact, he's yet to clear six targets in a game. The 27-year-old very well could lock down a starting job in Las Vegas, but he's a long shot to make the big leap to consistent fantasy output in his fifth professional season. He's no more than a late-round wild card in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mack Hollins' availability for Week 5 against the Raiders is in doubt due to a calf injury. Hollins has been a steady but unspectacular piece for the Patriots' receiving corps, going for 51 or more yards three times despite topping five targets just once with A.J. Brown sidelined by an ankle injury. Las Vegas can be vulnerable to opposing receivers, surrendering 70 or more yards four times. Efton Chism filled in after Hollins' early Week 4 exit and would likely do so again if Hollins does not suit up.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahan Dotson is in for a great Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers, whose defense just allowed 12.4 yards per completion last week. Dotson played 38 offensive snaps during Atlanta's Week 1 loss, out-snapping Olamide Zaccheaus and rookie Zachariah Branch, who each logged 18 snaps. Additionally, he trailed only Bijan Robinson and Drake London in targets, despite only receiving three. Regardless, Dotson should be in for a phenomenal Week 2 matchup after Carolina's defense gave up 59 points and eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as Atlanta's No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has allowed just 8.3 yards per completion this season. Despite Dotson clearly operating as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout this season, he's had little fantasy value, in large part due to the problems at quarterback. With Michal Penix set to return in the Week 3 matchup, Dotson could be more relevant but will likely remain overshadowed by Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson. Dotson could find the end zone, however, as the Packers' defense has already allowed three touchdowns to wideouts in two games, which is tied for the fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite playing the second-most snaps amongst Atlanta wide receivers this season (137), Dotson has managed to catch just four of 11 targets for 41 yards. He's clearly behind Bijan Robinson and Drake London in the Falcons' offensive game plan and will likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Additionally, Dotson is in for a difficult Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's allowed just 6.5 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top wideouts in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Dotson had his best game of the 2026 campaign in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching two of three targets for 54 yards and a touchdown. Despite this, Dotson has logged just 14 targets through four contests and will likely struggle remaining fantasy relevant without finding the end zone on a weekly basis. He is in for a favorable matchup, however, as Baltimore's defense has allowed 215.3 passing yards per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jahan Dotson will likely play a depth role on Atlanta's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Dotson has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching four of seven targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. However, he remains firmly behind Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson as pass catchers, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Even so, Dotson could have plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 6, as Chicago's defense has already allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Dotson had his most productive outing of the 2026 season in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, catching three of five targets for 87 yards and a touchdown. On the season, he's caught 11 of 23 targets for 236 yards and two touchdowns, benefitting from the return of quarterback Michael Penix. However, Dotson could struggle against the 49ers in Week 7, as they have allowed just 5.7 yards per pass attempt through five games this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1 for the Giants, but that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, third-string running back Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly.  Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Harris does suit up in Week 2, he will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.4: Najee Harris turned back the clock in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Harris rushed nine times for 52 yards, and may have seized the backup running back job away from both Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely heavily on the running game in Week 4 versus Arizona, though Cam Skattebo remains atop the depth chart. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Najee Harris has received nine carries in each of the last two games for the Giants. However, he is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, and remains behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. In Week 5, the G-Men will face a rather stingy Washington run defense. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Najee Harris had five carries for just nine yards last game for the Giants. The running game as a whole was fairly contained, as starter Cam Skattebo rushed for just 58 yards in the 27-27 tie with Washington. Interestingly, Tyrone Tracy also had five touches in this contest, perhaps showing that the backup role remains up for grabs. In Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new home in order to have any shot at 2026 fantasy relevance. He'll begin the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.6: Jaleel McLaughlin and the Browns return home to host the Ravens in Week 6. He did not record a carry and failed to bring in his lone target during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. McLaughlin has rushed twice for 31 yards and one touchdown across four outings so far in 2026. However, he could see an increase in playing time as the only healthy Cleveland running back against Baltimore's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.8). Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) are both dealing with injuries, and Dylan Sampson (knee) remains on injured reserve. It's probably best to avoid everyone outside of Judkins in fantasy, assuming he's active, in what could be a murky backfield rotation.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaleel McLaughlin and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference tilt in Week 7. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all four targets for another 14 yards during Cleveland's Week 6 win. With Quinshon Judkins (ankle) inactive, McLaughlin and Audric Estime each tallied nine carries to lead the backfield. McLaughlin paced the team in yardage and tied for the lead in receptions. If Judkins can't play against the Titans' 13th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.3) to RBs, McLaughlin could find himself busy again.

outlooksByWeek.6: Fernando Mendoza saw his first NFL action late in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, completing six of eight passes for 48 yards. His lone drive stalled in the red zone after he came up just short on a fourth-and-4 scramble. Kirk Cousins has led the team to a 3-2 record and remains the starter, but after Las Vegas used the first overall pick in the 2026 draft on Mendoza, it's only a matter of time before he gets a proper look under center. Another loss or two, something that seems very possible given the Raiders' upcoming schedule, could prompt coach Klint Kubiak to make the switch. If Mendoza does see action again in Week 6, he could pop for some intriguing numbers against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he will not start in Week 1 (Kirk Cousins will get the call), so there's not much sense in drafting him in most formats. He'll be worth a speculative add only when he's named Las Vegas' starter.

While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ray Davis remains largely uninvolved in the Bills' offense entering a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. He played more snaps on special teams (six) than on offense (five) in Week 1, and as long as James Cook remains healthy, Davis is an insurance policy more than a viable flex consideration. Davis' snaps would be further limited if RB Ty Johnson is able to suit up after missing Opening Week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ray Davis hasn't recorded a carry in consecutive weeks or a reception all season as the Bills get set to face the Patriots in Week 4. Davis logged a total of 16 offensive snaps all season, with Ty Johnson's return as a passing-down back further hindering Davis's hope for work. He remains solely an insurance policy for James Cook against a defense allowing 4.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ray Davis has not been a part of the Bills' game plan entering a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. He has only two carries through four weeks, adding one catch while factoring in on kickoff returns. Seemingly losing snaps to Ty Johnson on passing downs in what was already a limited role, Davis's only fantasy appeal would be to James Cook managers in the event of an injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Davis is back as the primary insurance option behind Bills' feature back James Cook III. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the most valuable backups in fantasy, but flies a bit under the radar due to a very small game-day role when Cook and passing-down specialist Ty Johnson are both healthy. That's been the scenario most of the last two seasons, but we've seen Davis play more than half of Buffalo's snaps in three games. During those outings, Davis averaged 21.0 touches, 130.3 yards and 19.4 fantasy points per game. The 26-year-old has no standalone value, but he'll leap into the RB2 mix should Cook miss time, which makes him worth stashing on the end of your bench.

outlooksByWeek.5: Efton Chism's role could expand in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. He drew four targets in Week 4, turning them into two catches for 42 yards and a touchdown, getting additional snaps due to Mack Hollins' (calf) early exit. Seemingly ascending over Kyle Williams on the depth chart and with Hollins' availability uncertain, Chism could again produce against a vulnerable secondary that's allowed four opposing receivers to gain 70 or more yards in as many weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Efton Chism aims to continue ascending the Patriots receiver depth chart Week 6 against the Jets. Chism has 10 targets over the last two weeks with both Mack Hollins and A.J. Brown sidelined, compiling 97 yards and a touchdown. Drake Maye is spreading targets, making Chism a touch volatile, but facing a Jets defense that's allowed four opposing receivers to go for 63 yards or more in two weeks offers Chism the potential to keep it going.
outlooksByWeek.7: Efton Chism's role in the Patriots passing game is in doubt ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury in Week 6, Chism only had one target after compiling 10 looks over the past two weeks. That low volume came with Romeo Doubs missing three quarters of action as well, so even if Doubs misses Week 7, Chism will still have limited opportunities to best a secondary that's allowing 9.8 yards per target, the third-highest mark in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre' Harris is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but he's been Justin Herbert's most reliable option, topping 50 receiving yards in each of the Chargers' last three games. Harris has put together a 13-209-0 line on 21 targets over four weeks, and he could make a push for the top spot on the WR depth chart with Ladd McConkey now dealing with both rib and foot injuries and Quentin Johnston failing to do much with his opportunities. Harris will aim for his first trip to the end zone in 2026 in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre' Harris wasn't able to take advantage of the absences of Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He played 30 snaps, catching two of four targets for 16 yards before also getting hurt. Harris is viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, but he was already struggling to make an impression in a Mike McDaniel scheme that is performing well below expectations in all areas. If Harris does get cleared to play in Week 6, he'll be facing a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jauan Jennings will aim to make more of his opportunities as the Vikings take on the Bears in Week 2. Jennings garnered just one target against the Packers in Week 1, and he was unable to convert it into a reception. The veteran was still on the field for almost half of the offensive plays, which keeps him as the WR3 moving forward. He'll look to get his first catch of the season against a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but he played almost 50 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers so far this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jauan Jennings will look to expand on his first catch of the year as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jennings brought in one of two targets for one yard against the Buccaneers in Week 3, which is promising given that he was out due to personal reasons the previous week. The veteran should continue to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver moving forward, but Justin Jefferson's injury does have a bearing on Jennings' usage. Miami has allowed a top-five 24.2 fantasy points per game to WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jauan Jennings remains a secondary option in the passing game ahead of Minnesota's Week 5 matchup at New Orleans. Jennings was projected to benefit from Justin Jefferson sitting out Week 4 with an ankle injury, but the veteran wideout logged just one catch for eight yards. He's now recorded two catches for nine yards in two weeks mostly without Jefferson, which especially doesn't bode well for his value when the star pass catcher returns to the field. He'll face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jauan Jennings is a depth option ahead of Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Jennings has been unable to get things going so far this season, with just two catches for nine yards across his four appearances. The only positive outlook moving forward for the veteran is that he's been on the field for a favorable number of offensive snaps, but that hasn't translated into output. Indianapolis has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jennings signed with the Vikings in May. The 2020 seventh-round pick was a situational player during his first three pro campaigns in San Francisco prior to breaking out with a 77-975-6 receiving line and 27th-place finish in fantasy PPG in 2024. He dipped quite a bit statistically in 2025 and failed to produce a single top-10 fantasy week, but did score nine touchdowns (sixth among WRs) in a good Niners offense. The 29-year-old will now file in third on the Minnesota depth chart behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He's headed for a big dip in targets and, especially with Kyler Murray under center, won't be a consistent fantasy option. He's barely worth late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Brooks will remain in the backfield mix for Green Bay against the Jets in Week 2. While Brooks took an ancillary role to Marshawn Lloyd in Week 1, Brooks still finished the game with seven rushes for 29 yards to Lloyd's 13 for 37. Brooks is also an excellent pass blocker, so he'll still get time on the field even if it doesn't convert to rushing attempts. New York dominated Tennessee in the trenches in Week 1, but they should be a lot less daunting than a staunch Minnesota front.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Brooks should continue to stay involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Brooks was a non-factor on the ground against the Jets in Week 2 (four carries for 11 yards), but he did reel in his first catch of the season for 15 yards. The fourth-year running back should remain on the field for passing-situation plays moving forward, especially since he served that role last season even with Josh Jacobs on the field. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's been tough on RBs so far this season, allowing a top-10 16.3 PPR points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield against the Buccaneers in Week 4. Brooks failed to register a carry and caught his sole target for four yards in a Week 3 loss to Atlanta, but he did log his third straight game with a 40-plus percent snap share on offense. The fourth-year running back's consistent usage on late downs as a pass catcher and a blocker makes him a valuable asset to the Packers, but not to fantasy managers at this point in the year. Tampa Bay has allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) but the sixth-highest receiving yards (165) to RBs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield if he's healthy in Week 5 against the Bears. Brooks rushed a solid four times for 30 yards and caught one ball for five yards in the first quarter of Week 4, but he then injured his ankle and did not record a stat after. The fourth-year running back will need to log some healthy practices this week if he hopes to play against the Packers' big rival. If he's able to suit up, Brooks will face a Bears defense that's allowed bottom-10 (4.73) yards per carry for RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Mason will remain sidelined for Week 6 as the Packers take on the Cowboys. Brooks is currently on IR due to an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next three weeks. His absence from the field sets up MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong as Green Bay's running back options in the near future.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Brooks will be out again in Week 7 when the Packers play the Lions. Brooks is currently on IR with an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next two weeks. His absence from the field should continue to give Pierre Strong more opportunities in the run game.

outlooksByWeek.4: Despite not recording a touch to date, Isaiah Davis could have meaningful touches in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. Breece Hall (thigh) seems unlikely to play, elevating Braelon Allen to the lead back role with Davis as a secondary option. Allen hasn't shouldered a heavy load his entire career, having double-digit carries just three times, all during his rookie 2024 season. The Bears are allowing a generous 4.9 yards per carry, so even a handful of rushes for Davis could yield positive results.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Davis hasn't factored into the Jets' offensive plans ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. Despite Breece Hall's (quad) Week 4 absence, Davis didn't receive a rushing opportunity and has no official offensive touches to date. Braelon Allen would again lead the Jets' backfield should Hall sit out again in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Davis hasn't factored into the Jets' running plans despite Breece Hall's absence entering a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Davis has played a mere 11 offensive snaps in two games, rushing for eight yards on two carries while adding a nine-yard catch. Even if Hall doesn't return in Week 6, Davis would need further injury to Braelon Allen to collect enough touches to succeed against a run defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2.
