The 25-year-old rookie and former CFL receiver played nine snaps on offense and six on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 1 win. Meyers flashed with his limited opportunities, catching his lone target for 18 yards while rushing once for 10 yards. There's a chance he could leapfrog Colbie Young on the depth chart, but we'll have to see what he does against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the Jaguars in Week 4. The rookie receiver caught three of five targets for 29 yards during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss, stepping up with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) out due to injuries. Meyers tied Mike Gesicki for third on the team in receptions, though he garnered two more targets than the tight end. He's still firmly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the passing game, but he's showing signs of being a reliable option in a banged-up WR room. Meyers will look to contribute against Jacksonville, whose defense ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed (527) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals visit the division-rival Ravens in Week 7. He caught both of his targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both healthy, Meyers returned to a supporting role, supplying 91 yards on three kick returns and another 13 yards on two punt returns. Rookie Colbie Young (knee) could also return from a two-game absence, so both receivers could struggle to make much of a contribution against the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan Engram was on the receiving end of Bo Nix's only touchdown pass in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. The veteran tight end also led the team in receiving yards with a 4-43-1 line on five targets, as top wideouts Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were neutralized. Engram's first season in Denver was a disappointment, as his 461 receiving yards last year were his lowest total for a full season since 2021, but more experience in Sean Payton's scheme and a new play-caller in Davis Webb could lead to better numbers. Engram is set for a potential revenge game in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 23rd in points per game allowed to TEs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan Engram had a minimal role in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, catching his only target for 17 yards. The veteran tight end has notched just six targets through two games, and while he did get into the end zone in the season opener, the reduced volume he saw in 2025, his first year in Denver, doesn't look like it will improve in 2026. Engram will take on a Rams defense in Week 3 that's allowed just 64 receiving yards to TEs so far, sixth in the league, and has yet to allow one to score a touchdown.
outlooksByWeek.4: Evan Engram failed to catch a pass in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, as he remains stuck in a peripheral role in the passing game. The veteran TE has notched just eight targets through three games, catching five for 60 yards and a touchdown. His workload is unlikely to significantly increase if Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are dominating looks from Bo Nix. Engram will face a 49ers defense in Week 4 that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Evan Engram tied his season high with five targets in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but the additional volume didn't lead to much production as he caught only one of them for six yards. Over the last three games, the veteran tight end has a meager 2-23-0 line on eight targets, remaining an afterthought in the offense. No. 3 wide receiver Pat Bryant left the loss to San Francisco with an ankle sprain, which could result in more volume for Engram, but that may not be enough to make him relevant again. Engram will try to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Evan Engram is coming off his most productive game of the season in terms of receiving yards in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers. With Sean Payton calling plays again, the veteran tight end caught all four of his targets for 55 yards. Engram remains a secondary option in the passing game behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, but he could get more consistent volume with Payton at the helm. Engram will face a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Evan Engram continues to see little usage in the Broncos' offense. Despite quarterback Bo Nix's struggles to attack downfield, Engram isn't getting much volume as a check-down option, failing to see more than five targets in any game this season and amassing a 12-134-1 line on 19 targets through six contests. Even if Nix picks up the pace, Engram likely won't be much of a factor. The veteran tight end does get a favorable matchup in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Engram returns for his second season in Denver after an underwhelming debut campaign with the team. The veteran tight end was limited to a career-low 13% target share and finished 15th or lower among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage, despite appearing in 16 games. Engram worked as a short-area target but still struggled to a poor 68% catch rate and was, as usual, a nonfactor near the goal line (one TD, two end zone targets). Engram hasn't cleared four touchdowns in a season since he scored six as a rookie in 2017. He finished 32nd among tight ends in fantasy PPG and isn't a good bet for a larger role this season, especially with Jaylen Waddle added to the offense. The 32-year-old Engram is a fantasy TE3, at best.

Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

outlooksByWeek.4: Ty Johnson looks to remain a passing-down option in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. In Week 3's season debut, Johnson caught all four targets for 50 yards against the Chargers-heavy volume for playing just 15 snaps. In 28 snaps last season against New England, Johnson failed to record a reception. The Patriots have allowed eight catches to opposing running backs, rendering Johnson an unappealing, low-ceiling, low-floor option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ty Johnson continues to factor in the Bills' passing game out of the backfield ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. After missing Weeks 1 and 2, Johnson has amassed six catches in Weeks 3 and 4, adding one three-yard carry. The Rams have allowed only 19 catches and 103 yards to opposing backs as receivers, and James Cook will likely continue to dominate backfield touches, rendering Johnson's fantasy potential minimal.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ty Johnson will look to again create chunk plays in the passing game when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Johnson has only one carry in three games, but for the second time this season, he snagged four passes, finishing with 72 yards in Week 5. Johnson's role appears clear, and he's unlikely to have the chance to exploit a Las Vegas defense that's allowing 5.2 yards per carry but has been stingy to running backs in the passing game, surrendering just 29 receiving yards per game.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson has settled in as a productive change-of-pace and receiving option in the Buffalo backfield behind James Cook. Johnson enters his eighth NFL season having yet to clear 63 carries or 34 catches in a season, but his role allows for him to hit for the occasional big game (15-plus fantasy points four times over the last two seasons). Of course, those games have come at random, making Johnson an unusable fantasy commodity. Even if Cook misses time this season, it's likely that Johnson would remain in his role, with Ray Davis instead stepping into lead back duties. Johnson plays a valuable role for Buffalo, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option as the Lions take on the Bills in Week 2. TeSlaa was unable to convert on his one target in Week 1 against the Saints, which only made season hopes lower for him after a subpar training camp. He also remains the fifth option in the Detroit passing game behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. Luckily, Buffalo gave up a whopping 40.0 PPR points to Houston wide receivers in Week 1, so this upcoming week could be TeSlaa's chance to return to relevance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaac TeSlaa will look to replicate a solid performance as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. TeSlaa started the season quietly with just two catches for 26 yards across the first two games, but he reeled in all three targets for 66 yards against the Jets in Week 3. While this output isn't enough to warrant a start and is more translatable to a stash move, TeSlaa could be in store for more looks. The Panthers have also allowed a second-least 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaac TeSlaa could continue to have a big role as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. TeSlaa finished Week 4 against the Panthers with season-high targets, catches and yards, reeling in four of eight looks for four catches and 95 yards. After a slow start to the season, the second-year pass catcher has now posted a 7-161-0 receiving line in the last two games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaac TeSlaa will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. After it appeared the second-year pass catcher was starting to carve out a role for himself again, TeSlaa recorded zero catches against the Cardinals before Detroit's bye. Hopefully the second game this year with zero catches was another anomaly, as there is plenty of love to spread with the Lions' high-volume offense. Green Bay has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: TeSlaa is a candidate for a Year 2 leap as the favorite for No. 3 WR duties in Detroit behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. TeSlaa barely played as a rookie (27 total targets), but he had a very specific role and, believe it or not, tied for 11th in the entire NFL with 11 end zone targets. That helped lead to six touchdowns, four of which came when his snaps increased during Detroit's final six games. The 2025 third-round pick has a big size edge on both St. Brown and Williams, so while consistent targets are a long shot, he's still likely to remain busy near the goal line. TeSlaa won't be more than a boom/bust situational target most weeks, but if one of the starters misses time, he'll be on the flex radar. Consider him with a late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Hutchinson set season highs with four catches and 65 yards in Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, but he has yet to score this season and has just three touchdowns in 54 career regular-season games. He's likely to slide down a spot on the WR depth chart once trade acquisition Marvin Harrison is up to speed, but that may not happen in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Hutchinson should get enough opportunities against a Jaguars defense that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers to warrant Week 6 flex consideration in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Hutchinson had season-low totals across the board with two catches for 10 yards on three targets in Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars, and he won't be a recommended Week 7 fantasy play against the Giants, even in deeper formats. He was earning decent volume while Houston's WR room was banged up, but the return of Nico Collins from a hamstring injury, coupled with the trade for Marvin Harrison and emergence of Jaylin Noel, have relegated Hutchinson to a depth role. Hutchinson doesn't have the talent to find consistent success with limited usage, as he has just three TDs in 55 career regular-season games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Oronde Gadsden didn't have a big role in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, sitting third in snap share at tight end behind Charlie Kolar and David Njoku while catching both his targets for 32 yards. Njoku was the more productive receiver and Kolar by far the best blocker of the group, making it tough for Gadsden to find a niche in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme despite his impressive numbers as a rookie. Gadsden faces an additional challenge in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR points per game allowed to TEs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Oronde Gadsden hasn't logged much volume to begin the season, with just four targets through two games, but he's caught all four for 50 yards and scored his first touchdown of 2026 in the Chargers' loss last week to the Raiders. The second-year tight end's usage could increase significantly in the coming games. Both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar left the Week 2 loss to Las Vegas with injuries that are expected to land them on injured reserve, leaving Gadsden as the only healthy TE on the roster. He doesn't have the blocking skills of his veteran teammates, which could limit how much OC Mike McDaniel is willing to put him on the field, but Gadsden's workload will still increase almost by default unless the team is able to find immediate help from outside the organization. He'll face a Bills defense in Week 3 that ranks in the bottom 10 in catches and receiving yards allowed to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Oronde Gadsden didn't get a significant increase in his pass-catching assignments in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, despite injuries to Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers to have his tight ends block, which is not Gadsden's forte. While he saw a season-high 36 offensive snaps in Week 3, he only got three targets from Justin Herbert and failed to catch any of them. There still isn't any real competition for Gadsden on the roster at tight end, but fullback Alec Ingold ended up being the player who benefited most from the absences of Njoku and Kolar. Gadsden will try to prove to his new OC that he has more to offer in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Oronde Gadsden garnered his first significant target volume of the season in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, catching five of eight targets for 36 yards. The second-year tight end doesn't have the blocking chops offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers, but with Charlie Kolar and David Njoku both injured and the team's wide receiver room also banged up, Gadsden is one of Justin Herbert's best remaining pass catchers. He'll try to build on this performance in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed to TEs through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Oronde Gadsden may need a trade to reclaim the fantasy value he displayed as a rookie in 2025. Even with the Chargers' wide receiver room depleted by injuries in Week 5, the second-year tight end notched just one target in a loss to the Broncos, while veteran Charlie Kolar turned four looks from Justin Herbert into three catches for a team-high 37 yards. Gadsden is the more dangerous pass catcher, but coordinator Mike McDaniel doesn't trust him with blocking assignments and apparently doesn't see much in him as a downfield option either. If Gadsden can work his way into a larger role, he could produce in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Gadsden's rookie season was quite the roller coaster. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't get much early run prior to exploding for 29.4 fantasy points in Week 7 and 18.7 points in Week 8. He went on to score one touchdown and average 6.2 fantasy PPG the rest of the season, never clearing 12.2 points in a single outing. Gadsden finished the season eighth or better at the position in end zone targets, aDOT, YPR, YPT and YPRR. The 23-year-old's second-half fall is concerning, and he now enters Year 2 set to compete for work with newcomer David Njoku and Charlie Kolar. It's still possible Gadsden emerges as a featured target in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, but consistent fantasy output may be tough in an offense that figures to spread the ball around. Gadsden is only worth stashing in dynasty.

Pearsall (knee) is out for the 2026 season after battling injuries during his first two NFL campaigns. The 2024 first-round pick's rookie season ended on a strong note (18-plus fantasy points in Weeks 17 and 18) and that momentum carried over early in 2025 (14.6 fantasy PPG during Weeks 1-3). Pearsall then suffered a knee injury and went on to average 7.5 PPG in six games the rest of the season. Pearsall holds the unfortunate distinction of having the most targets among all players who failed to score a single TD last season. Pearsall will enter 2027 - his age-27 campaign - eyeing his first fully healthy campaign and will battle for a starting job in San Francisco. He's no longer a must hold in dynasty, but he's a fine enough hold in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Gunnar Helm finished third on the Titans with 28 receiving yards on six targets in the season-opening loss to the Jets. He's locked in as Tennessee's top TE heading into Week 2 against the Eagles, but Helm isn't a recommended fantasy option outside of super-deep fantasy formats given the struggles of the Titans' entire offense. Helm has recorded at least four catches in five of his last eight games, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has just two games with more than 36 receiving yards in his career and two TDs in 17 NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Gunnar Helm is tied for second on the Titans with seven targets through two games, but he has just 41 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick is locked in as the team's starting TE heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, who just allowed six catches for 54 yards and a TD to Rams TE Terrance Ferguson. Helm is unlikely to match that production considering he has yet to exceed 51 receiving yards in a game while scoring just twice through 18 NFL appearances. Unless second-year Titans QB Cam Ward starts to pick up his passing production, Helm can continue to be ignored in the vast majority of fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.4: Gunnar Helm is third on the Titans through three weeks with eight catches and 11 targets, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has mustered a meager 55 receiving yards. His fantasy appeal is minimal for Week 4 against the Ravens, even though Baltimore's defense has allowed a TD to a TE in two of three games this season. Helm has reached 40 receiving yards in just two of 19 NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.5: Gunnar Helm is averaging just 15 receiving yards per game heading into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans. The second-year TE has exceeded 70% of offensive snaps in every game this season, but Helm is being used more as a blocker than a pass catcher in Tennessee's struggling offense. Houston is allowing 56 yards per game to TEs but hasn't given up a TD to the position, while Helm has scored just twice in 20 career NFL games. Helm hasn't done enough to warrant fantasy consideration.
outlooksByWeek.6: Gunnar Helm remains a fantasy non-factor heading into Week 6 against the Colts, as Tennessee's starting TE is averaging just 12 receiving yards per game. Helm has played over 70% of offensive snaps in every game this season, but he's used primarily as a blocker. The Colts are tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to TEs with four, but Helm has scored only twice through 21 career NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.7: Gunnar Helm has been trending in the wrong direction, with consecutive zero-catch performances coming into a Week 7 home game against the Browns and just nine catches for 60 yards all season. He continues to lead Tennessee's TEs in playing time, but Helm has been used almost exclusively as a blocker in recent weeks. Helm remains a non-factor for fantasy purposes in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Helm quietly caught 44 passes during his rookie season, which -- believe it or not -- ranks 11th among rookie tight ends over the past decade. Impressively, the 2025 fourth-round pick hit that mark despite playing second fiddle to starter Chig Okonkwo. Helm, who caught a healthy 79% of his 56 targets, wasn't much of a fantasy option as a rookie (5.7 PPG), but with Okonkwo out of the picture, he's positioned for a much larger role in his second season. Helm will need a leap from QB Cam Ward, but if that happens, a breakout season is possible. The 24-year-old is worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

Higgins is out for the 2026 season after tearing his ACL in mid August. As a rookie, the 2025 second-round pick played 58% of Houston's offensive snaps and handled a 12% target share en route to clearing 500 yards and scoring six touchdowns. Higgins averaged a lowly 7.6 fantasy PPG, but the 6-foot-4 perimeter receiver is a good bet for a larger role opposite Nico Collins once healthy in 2027. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.7: Los Angeles placed Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and they're expected to work out multiple kickers over the next few days before deciding on a new option prior to Sunday's game against the Raiders in Week 7. Regardless of who gets the nod in Week 7, this might not be a favorable matchup for Rams kickers since the Raiders have given up the 11th-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing kickers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.5: Brandin Cooks will look to log his first reception for the 49ers in a Week 5 clash against Seattle. Cooks made his San Francisco debut this past Sunday against Denver but didn't catch his only target. The veteran wideout could work his way up to more opportunities, however, with all of Demarcus Robinson (ankle), Christian Kirk (calf) and De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) on IR. Even if Cooks gets more looks in Week 5, he could struggle to produce against a Seahawks defense that has given up the fewest receiving yards per game (98.8) to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandin Cooks could have an elevated role for San Francisco in Week 6 against the Commanders. Cooks made his first catch for the 49ers this past Sunday against Seattle, hauling in a seven-yard touchdown from QB Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout ended up logging a 38 percent offensive snap share, largely as a result of Deebo Samuel exiting with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. Should Samuel be sidelined in Week 6, Cooks could start at WR alongside Mike Evans. The 49ers' wideout corps could thrive against a Washington defense that has given up seven receiving TDs to the position -- tied for third-most in the NFL -- through six weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandin Cooks and the 49ers are back on the road for a meeting with the Falcons in Week 7. He brought in one of two targets for 13 yards during San Francisco's Week 6 win. With Mike Evans expected to miss time after aggravating his Achilles injury in the victory and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) in jeopardy of missing a second straight game, Cooks could see an uptick in opportunities. However, there's a possibility of Christian Kirk (calf/IR) making his debut for the 49ers, which would hinder some of Cooks' value versus an Atlanta defense allowing 37.0 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Carlson will look to remain productive in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Carlson converted his first four kicks (two field goals and two extra points) before missing a 62-yard field-goal attempt on the last play of regulation. He's expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities moving forward but may struggle against the Ravens in Week 2, as they allowed just 5.0 kicking points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Carlson is expected to have few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Carlson, who spent the previous eight seasons with the Raiders, converted on all three of his field-goal tries during the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He could continue to receive scoring opportunities due to New Orleans' offensive success. However, Carlson is likely in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, as Las Vegas has allowed just 4.5 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Daniel Carlson could see few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Carlson has been relatively accurate in his first three games with New Orleans, converting on seven of eight extra-point attempts and four of five field-goal tries. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high-powered offense, which is currently averaging 27.0 points per game. However, Carlson is in for a tough Week 4 matchup, as the Falcons' defense has allowed just 6.7 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Daniel Carlson could get few scoring chances in the Saints' Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Carlson missed another field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons and is now just one of three on tries from 50-or-more yards. On the season, he's converted five of seven field-goal tries and 10 of 11 point-after attempts. Carlson likely won't have many scoring opportunities in the Week 5 matchup as well, with Minnesota's defense allowing just 12.8 points and 6.8 kicking points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Daniel Carlson could see few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Carlson struggled in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, converting on just one of two point-after attempts. On the season, Carlson had made five of seven field-goal tries and 11 of 13 extra-point attempts. He could continue to struggle in Week 6 against a Giants team that's allowed just 4.0 kicking points per game this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Daniel Carlson could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Carlson's struggles continued in the Week 6 win over the Giants, missing a kick for the fourth consecutive week. On the season, he's made seven of 10 field-goal tries and 15 of 17 point-after attempts. Despite the inconsistency, he's in for a very favorable Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's allowed 10.3 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devin Singletary acted as the No. 2 back for the Giants in their season-opening win in Week 1 over Dallas. He received the second-most carries out of the backfield behind starter Cam Skattebo, while also catching four passes for 22 yards and a touchdown in the 28-20 triumph. Fellow rusher Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in this game as well, which could further solidify Singletary's role, though veteran Najee Harris also looms. In Week 2, the Giants will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men to give the defensive line a boost.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devin Singletary managed just three carries for nine yards last game for the Giants. He remains firmly behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury, so teams will likely gameplan to stop the run. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.

Marcus Mariota will likely start for the Commanders in Week 3, as starter Jayden Daniels dislocated the same elbow that he previously injured last season. Mariota relieved Daniels in the second half in Week 2 versus the Cowboys, throwing for 111 yards and a touchdown. He will have his work cut out for him versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 scrimmage yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marcus Mariota led an improbable Washington victory over the defending Super Bowl champions last game. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4, though he is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow.  Whoever lines up under center will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Bell hopes for additional volume in the Dolphins Week 2 matchup at San Francisco. Coming off an ACL tear in November, the rookie logged a 52.7% snap share in his NFL debut, ending with a 25-yard catch on two targets. Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas dominated the targets in Miami's limited passing game, as expected given their availability throughout training camp. The 49ers' secondary doesn't appear to be one where Bell can break out, allowing just 6.4 yards per target in Week 1. Bell is worth monitoring, but he's currently off the fantasy radar.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Bell will hope to build on his best game of his rookie season in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. Bell posted seven targets in Week 3 after just three in the first two weeks, playing 72% of offensive snaps with Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined. Bell is the Dolphins' highest-ceiling option, but the passing game hasn't thrived under Malik Willis. Likely playing from behind, Bell could excel against a secondary that has misleading stats thanks to a Week 2 monsoon in Chicago that shut down the passing game, but Bell needs to turn potential into production before earning fantasy trust.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Bell is failing to gain traction in the Dolphins' limited passing attack ahead of a Week 5 tilt with the Bengals. Bell failed to record a catch on three targets in Week 4 in a game where Miami threw only 17 times, completing nine of them. Bell remains long on potential, but he's garnered three or fewer looks in three of Miami's first four games, and a breakout against a middling Bengals defense that hasn't allowed more than 63 yards to an opposing receiver seems unlikely.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Bell will look for a bigger role in the Dolphins' passing game coming out of a bye in Week 7 against the Jets. He has failed to record a catch in three of his first five games to start his career, with Miami's production failing to reach 200 yards. With the Jets allowing just 202 passing yards per game and Bell logging a limited workload, he's unlikely to garner Week 7 fantasy attention.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik Willis plays well, but there are enough concerns that he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andy Borregales hopes his scoring chances will elevate with a bounce-back offensive performance from the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Borregales had only two opportunities as the team struggled to move the ball in Seattle, and unfortunately, Week 2's game doesn't profile as high-scoring. Perhaps that increases Borregales' three-point opportunities, and he's a reliable option from all over the field. Pittsburgh allowed four field-goal attempts last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andy Borregales' opportunities could again be limited when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. Borregales missed his first kick of the season in Week 2, and through two games, has just four field-goal attempts and three extra points as New England's offense has struggled to sustain drives. Jacksonville has allowed just three field goals and three extra points through two games, so there are likely more reliable Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Andy Borregales is one of many Patriots hindered by the team's struggling offense heading into a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. New England has scored just 39 points in three weeks, marginally suppressed by two missed field goals, though Borregales' opportunities have been sparse. Buffalo has allowed nine extra points and six field goal attempts through three weeks, so Borregales could be busier in Week 4. Even so, there are safer options until the Patriots offense gets in gear.
outlooksByWeek.5: Andy Borregales' opportunities have been scant for the Patriots ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. After not attempting an extra point in Week 3, Borregales drilled three extra points but did not attempt a field goal for the first time this season in Week 4. Las Vegas has allowed the second-fewest points to opposing kickers, surrendering 10 PATs but only five field goal tries through four games, and though the Patriots' offense may be righting its early-season struggles, Borregales has yet to regain fantasy trust.
outlooksByWeek.6: Andy Borregales will look to remain busy when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. With New England's offense coming to life over the last two weeks, Borregales has nailed nine PATs over that span, but their efficiency has yielded only one field goal. The Jets have allowed nine field goals and nine PATs through five games, ranking in the middle, and if those averages hold, Borregales can be an adequate streamer.
outlooksByWeek.7: Andy Borregales hasn't been a huge scorer despite the Patriots' offensive uptick over the last three weeks as they get set to face the Bears in Week 7. While he's garnered 12 PATs in this stretch, the offensive efficiency has resulted in just three field goal tries, all from inside 40 yards. Chicago has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers, so until the Patriots' offense slows down and Borregales gets more field goal attempts, his fantasy viability appears minimal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving room during the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 9.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the NFL. Despite not receiving a target in his NFL debut, Branch tied Olamide Zaccheaus for the third-most snaps (18) amongst Falcons receivers. Additionally, he could be more involved in the Week 2 gameplan after Atlanta's offensive struggles last week. Even so, Branch is in for a great matchup against a Panthers defense that gave up eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zachariah Branch is expected to remain a minimal portion of the Falcons' offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints, Through three weeks, Branch has caught three of four targets while playing 45 offensive snaps. Despite not having much competition in Atlanta's WR room, the rookie wideout likely won't have fantasy value without finding the end zone in Week 4. Additionally, Branch could struggle against a good New Orleans secondary that's allowed just 6.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Branch has received two targets in each of his last three games, even out-targeting Olamide Zaccheaus over the last two weeks (four to three). Additionally, Branch played a career-high 23% of the Falcons' offensive snaps in the Week 4 win over the Saints, suggesting his offensive role may be growing. He's also in for a favorable Week 5 matchup against a Ravens secondary that's given up 734 receiving yards to wideouts through four contests this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zachariah Branch will likely play a complimentary role in Atlanta's receiving corps during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Branch has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching all four of his targets for 25 yards. He appears to have overtaken Olamide Zaccheaus in the wide-receiver room but likely won't have much fantasy value without scoring a touchdown. That being said, Branch could succeed against a Bears defense that's giving up 10.4 yards per target to opposing WRs this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow as the Falcons' face the 49ers in Week 7. Branch has caught all six of his targets over the last three weeks, accumulating 34 receiving yards. He appears to have emerged as Atlanta's No. 3 wideout, as Olamide Zaccheaus hasn't caught a pass since the Week 3 win over the Packers. Regardless, Branch will likely struggle in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has given up just 8.9 yards per completion through five games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Njoku led the Chargers' tight end group in receiving during a season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. That far overshadowed Oronde Gadsden's two catches for 32 yards, while Charlie Kolar was predictably limited to blocking duties in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Top wideout Ladd McConkey did get knocked out of the game with a rib injury, however, and if he misses additional time, there could be more looks available for Njoku. He gets a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR points per game allowed to TEs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Njoku signed with the Chargers after spending his first nine NFL seasons in Cleveland. The 2017 first-round pick was a late bloomer and has struggled with durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2018), but he has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years. Prior to a lost 2025 campaign, Njoku finished in the top eight among tight ends in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row. A force near the goal line, Njoku paced the position in end zone targets in both 2023 and 2024. At 30 years old, Njoku likely still has something left in the tank, but he has a tough path to fantasy relevance in a Los Angeles tight end room that also includes ascending Oronde Gadsden II and Charlie Kolar. Njoku will only be worth an add if he quickly takes control as the team's clear starter at the position.

outlooksByWeek.3: Kaleb Johnson could continue to carve out a role as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Johnson saw a huge uptick in usage against the Jets in Week 2, logging eight carries for 32 yards. The second-year ball carrier was the most efficient of Green Bay's RBs, and he could continue to see an early-down role if MarShawn Lloyd remains inefficient. Still, Atlanta has allowed 127 rushing yards to running backs through two weeks, a top-10 mark, which could make Johnson's job tough even if he's the Packers' go-to on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaleb Johnson will seek to earn more touches as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Johnson struggled to stay involved with Green Bay playing from behind in Week 3, logging just four carries for six yards and catching one of three passes for 10 yards. The former Steeler still saw his offensive snap share increase from 27 percent in Week 2 to 36 percent in Week 3, while Lloyd's share fell in the same stretch. This could open up more opportunities in the coming weeks, but not enough to start Johnson against a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaleb Johnson will seek to stay involved as the Packers take on the Bears in Week 5. Johnson finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a solid eight carries for 42 yards, but he also lost a critical fumble in the fourth quarter. This makes it unclear what the backfield split will look like moving forward, not that there's been much of a clear breakdown so far. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed to RBs this season, which could carve a path for Johnson to stay productive if he can hold onto the ball.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kaleb Johnson is likely to be a depth option once again as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. After committing a costly goal-line fumble against the Buccaneers in Week 4, Johnson operated as the No. 3 running back for Green Bay in Week 5. The second-year ball carrier was on the field for just nine offensive snaps, and his seven carries for 26 yards came in garbage time. He'll look to make the most of what could be limited opportunities versus a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was traded to Green Bay in August after his rookie season in Pittsburgh didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start and very well could get some early-season run with Josh Jacobs facing a suspension. Johnson will compete for reps with unproven Marshawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andre Szmyt and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. He finished Cleveland's 34-10 loss a perfect two-for-two on kicks, making a 26-yard field goal and connecting on his lone PAT. Tampa Bay gave up 33 points last week, but that was to an elite Bengals offense that isn't even in the same realm as the Browns. Szmyt should be left on waiver wires as long as Cleveland continues to struggle to create scoring opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3. He remained perfect through two games by connecting on all three of his field-goal attempts and both PATs to help Cleveland upset the Buccaneers 23-19 in Week 2. Szmyt drilled field goals of 34 yards (twice) and 50 yards, his first score from 50 or more in limited opportunities. He's proven to be reliable, but more is needed from the Browns' offense to say he's an every-week starter. After giving up a whopping 59 points in their season opener, Carolina's defense allowed just three points to the Falcons in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host the Steelers for a divisional tilt between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Szmyt improved to 6-for-6 on FGAs and 4-for-4 on PATs across three contests in 2026. The Browns rank 24th in scoring at 18.0 points per game, but despite his perfect mark thus far, Szmyt should be considered a risky start in fantasy with other options available.
outlooksByWeek.5: Andre Szmyt and the Browns hope to improve to 4-1 on the season when they travel to take on the Jets in Week 5. He made both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winner with 10 seconds remaining, and connected on all three PATs during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Szmyt set a new career high in distance and appears to be establishing himself as one of the best kickers in the league, as he's made 22 straight field goals dating back to last season. He'll face a tough Jets defense outdoors that allows 21.0 points per game, tied for 11th in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host Baltimore for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He went 2-for-2 on field goals but missed his only extra-point try in Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. The PAT miss was Szmyt's first of the season, and he's now a perfect 10-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-8 on extra points. The Browns' offense took a step back after a three-game winning streak, but some of that can be attributed to the rainy conditions all afternoon. Either way, Szmyt will aim to contribute at home against a Ravens defense allowing 23.8 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Andre Szmyt and the Browns visit the Titans for a Week 7 showdown. He made two of his three field-goal attempts, including the 48-yard game-winner, and his lone PAT during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 5. It was Szmyt's first field goal miss this season, as he's now 12-for-13 (92.3%) through six games. The Browns' offense has taken a step back in recent weeks, scoring a combined 22 points in their last two outings, leaving Szmyt a difficult kicker to rely on in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.6: Savion Williams could be vying for a return as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Williams has yet to make his season debut, with a high-ankle sprain keeping him on IR, but he did appear in practice ahead of Week 5 before his eventual inactive status. If the second-year pass catcher can get more involved in Green Bay's preparation in the coming days, there's a good chance he'll face Dallas. Williams would be in line for WR3 duties behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson if he does return to the field.
outlooksByWeek.7: Savion Williams will aim to stay involved as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Williams got plenty of usage in his season debut versus the Cowboys in Week 6, catching all four of his targets for 32 yards and rushing the ball twice for nine yards. The second year looks to be the WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, especially given that Skyy Moore is on IR with an ankle injury. Williams will face a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams is primed for a larger role in his second NFL season. The 2025 third-round pick had a unique rookie campaign, handling more carries (11) than he did targets (10). Williams' gadget role allowed him only 90 snaps (12%) and he was utilized only near the line of scrimmage (1.4 aDOT). The Green Bay WR rotation no longer includes Romeo Doubs or Dontayvion Wicks, but Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and fellow second-year wideout Matthew Golden remain in the mix. Williams will need to beat out one (or perhaps two) of them and start to see more downfield targets in order to land on the fantasy radar. The 24-year-old is only worth late-round consideration in deeper formats, especially since he'll open the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kavontae Turpin managed just one catch for eight yards in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Turpin remains mostly utilized as a kick returner at this stage, though the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: KaVontae Turpin continues to flash his versatility for the Cowboys. In addition to his standard role as the primary returner for Dallas, Turpin also rushed for a nine-yard touchdown and even caught a nine-yard pass. Despite this, Turpin remains a boom-or-bust candidate in an offense with so much firepower ahead of him on the depth chart. In Week 4, the Cowboys face a Texans defense allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt through the air, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: KaVontae Turpin remains buried on the depth chart for the Cowboys, at least in terms of receiving. Turpin is the primary returner but has just two catches for 17 yards through four contests. Barring injury, Turpin's impact will mostly be felt on special teams. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KaVontae Turpin saw a season-high four targets last game for the Cowboys.  CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to the additional looks for Turpin. However, Turpin managed just two catches for 22 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Turpin back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: KaVontae Turpin left the last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury, leaving his status in question for Week 7 versus the Eagles. Tyler Goodson handled kick return duties, while Jonathan Mingo caught punts in Turpin's absence. His targets on offense appear to have been gobbled up by No. 3 wideout Ryan Flournoy. If Turpin can return in Week 7, he would face an Eagles defense allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Odell Beckham earned a spot on the roster for the Giants, completing a remarkable comeback from injury. Though the nostalgia was high, Beckham did not even record a target in the season-opening win over the Cowboys in Week 1. With Malik Nabers now healthy, new additions Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields ahead of him on the depth chart, and Isaiah Likely looking like a blossoming star at tight end, it will be difficult for Beckham to have much of an impact on the stat sheet this season. In Week 2, Odell and company will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in its first game. Los Angeles gave up 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in a dismal loss in Australia to the 49ers, and also lost star pass rusher Myles Garrett to knee surgery.
outlooksByWeek.3: Odell Beckham has yet to catch a pass through two games for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Beckham will likely see his stock further take a hit. In Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league, though Beckham looks more like depth than anything else at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Odell Beckham and Braxton Berrios have been vying for the No. 4 wideout role on the Giants, though neither has a catch to date on the young season. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for both players. Winston should remain under center in Week 3 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Bryant was the Broncos' surprise target leader in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching four of six targets for 42 yards. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were both taken out of the equation by the Chiefs secondary, forcing Bo Nix to look underneath for options like Bryant and tight end Evan Engram. Bryant had a solid finish to his rookie season in 2025, posting a 26-332-1 line on 39 targets over his final eight regular-season games, and his snap count and production suggest he's moved past Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin to take over the No. 3 wideout role for Denver. Bryant will look to stay involved in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Bryant scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, connecting with Bo Nix for a five-yard strike in the third quarter. It was one of just two catches on the night for the second-year wide receiver. Through three games, he's produced a 6-86-1 line on nine targets while adding a 16-yard gain on one carry. Bryant is well behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the pecking order, but he seems to have secured the No. 3 role ahead of Troy Franklin. Bryant will look to build some momentum in Week 4 against a 49ers secondary that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Bryant caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but an ankle sprain knocked him out of the contest early. The second-year wide receiver is expected to miss multiple weeks, but Denver hasn't placed him on IR yet. In Bryant's absence, Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin will get more work behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, beginning with a Week 5 matchup against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 third-round pick, Bryant played a situational role throughout his rookie season and is likely to do the same in 2026 after Denver added Jaylen Waddle as a running mate for Courtland Sutton. Bryant will battle the likes of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. During his rookie campaign, Bryant barely saw the field early on, but eventually passed Franklin on the depth chart and earned more work down the stretch. That led to more snaps but not much fantasy production, as he failed to clear 13.2 fantasy points in a single game and found the end zone once. The 23-year-old isn't on the fantasy radar right now, but he makes for a fine dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Sanders hopes to maintain his job when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Sanders secured the team's opportunities in Week 1 over Blake Grupe, finishing with eight points, more where distance matters as he made two field goals from beyond 50 yards. Assuming he's again active, a higher-scoring game could be on tap against a defense that allowed 39 points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Sanders appears on track to serve as the Jets' kicker again in Week 3 at Detroit. Despite Blake Grupe being on the roster, Sanders has been the active option through two games, hitting four extra points and four of five field goals. Volume is questionable as the Jets' offense isn't highly efficient, and Detroit's defense has allowed just two field goal attempts while surrendering nine touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Sanders appears in line to handle kicking duties for the Jets again in Week 4 against the Bears. Sanders has routinely been activated from the practice squad in advance of game day and has made all five of his PATs and 5-of-6 field goals. Chicago has allowed just 17 points to opposing kickers through three weeks, and with the Jets not offering a high-powered offense, Sanders seems unlikely to provide a top-end fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Sanders hasn't notched many scoring chances in the Jets' limited offense entering Week 5 against the Browns. Through four games, Sanders has eight field goal attempts and only five PATs, keeping his floor and ceiling low. Cleveland has allowed the second-most field goal attempts (12) through four games, so perhaps there's a chance at a productive Week 5 if the Jets continue to be held out of the end zone, but Sanders' overall body of work doesn't suggest fantasy relevance.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jason Sanders hasn't collected ample attempts to create a floor or ceiling ahead of the Jets' Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Sanders has just seven PATs through five games, while only attempting multiple field goals in two of five outings. New England is the fourth-stingiest team to opposing kickers, allowing just six made field goals, likely again keeping Sanders out of the Week 6 fantasy mix.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jason Sanders could offer bye-week replacement production for the Jets in a Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. Sanders drilled a season-high four field goals in Week 6, his third game in six appearances with multiple 3-point connections, and he's added multiple PATs at the same 50% clip. Miami's defense has allowed plenty of points to opposing kickers, surrendering three extra point attempts and two field goals per game, setting Sanders up for a potentially busy, high-scoring Week 7.

outlooksByWeek.4: Jalon Daniels is set to start in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Tampa Bay's Week 4 matchup against the Packers. In three preseason games, the undrafted rookie from Kansas accounted for 276 total yards and two touchdowns while turning the ball over just once. In college, Daniels showed incredible arm talent and scrambling ability, though he struggled with accuracy at times. He's in for a tough matchup in his first NFL start, as the Packers' defense has allowed just 18.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalon Daniels is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Daniels struggled during his first NFL start in Week 4, throwing for 148 yards, two interceptions and a touchdown while adding 55 yards on the ground. However, he showed flashes of potential and could take advantage of a Cowboys defense that's allowing 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Daniels could really thrive getting out of the pocket, as Dallas' defense has given up the most rushing yards to quarterbacks (188) in the NFL through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalon Daniels is expected to start at quarterback as the Buccaneers' take on the Steelers in Week 6. Daniels has impressed while filling in for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) over the last two weeks, totaling 424 yards and two touchdowns. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Friday that he plans to start Daniels in Week 6, as Tampa Bay continues to be cautious with Mayfield's injury. If Daniels starts as expected, he could struggle against a good Steelers defense that's given up just 16.8 points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalon Daniels is expected to start at quarterback if Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined for the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Daniels struggled against the Steelers defense in a Week 6 overtime loss, throwing for 164 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while adding 39 yards on nine carries. Over his first three NFL starts, Daniels has accounted for just three touchdowns and five turnovers, suggesting he'll carry minimal fantasy value going forward. Despite this, Daniels could be in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Carolina defense that's given up 146 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets and a few carries, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Williams' snaps could increase for the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Despite not drawing a target to open the season, Williams will likely ascend the depth chart following A.J. Brown's ankle injury that will sideline him for at least a month. Williams has shown big-play potential, so he may not require heavy volume to contribute, but until New England reveals its new receiving rotation, Williams can only be considered in the deepest of formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Williams hopes for more opportunities in Week 3 as the Patriots face the Jaguars. Rising up the depth chart with A.J. Brown on IR, Williams still only recorded a 21% snap share, registering two targets and a 10-yard catch in Week 2 where New England completed only 14 passes. Williams has big-play potential, but the passing game isn't operating at a high enough level to sustain a No. 4 WR despite facing a defense that's allowing 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Williams remains a low-volume, big-play option for the Patriots entering Week 4 against the Bills. Serving as the No. 4 WR following the ankle injury to A.J. Brown, Williams caught one of three targets for 34 yards in Week 3. He's logged five targets in the two games since Brown went down and has a favorable matchup against a Bills' secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target. With Drake Maye struggling, Williams likely won't have enough opportunities to be a Week 4 option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Williams hasn't been heavily involved in the Patriots passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. Williams amassed a mere two targets in Week 4 while Efton Chism appeared to overtake him as the team's No. 4 receiver. Williams likely won't garner enough attention to be a reliable Week 5 option, despite facing a Raiders secondary that's allowing a generous 8.2 yards per target to receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Williams hopes to maintain his big-play ability in Week 6 when the Patriots host the Jets. Williams hauled in three passes for 91 yards in Week 5, despite a 32% snap share even with Mack Hollins's absence, making Williams reliant on chunk plays for fantasy production. The Jets have allowed just 644 yards to opposing wideouts over five games (128.8 per game), and with New England spreading targets, Williams won't have volume on his side in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Williams could factor into the Patriots' receiving rotation in Week 7 against the Bears if Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is unable to play. Williams has three or fewer targets in every game to date, but averaging 24.5 yards per catch, he's proven capable of doing more with less. While more volume can be anticipated, Williams will have a chance to stretch the field against a defense that's allowing 9.8 yards per target, the third-highest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams showed some flashes as a rookie, but he has a tough path to a Year 2 breakout. The 2025 third-round pick didn't see the field much (31% snap share), but he scored three touchdowns on 21 targets, all of which came from Week 10 on. He was utilized as a situational deep threat (17.6 aDOT), which led to a low catch rate (48%) but plenty of big plays (20.9 YPR). That role may not change much in 2026, as Williams will now compete with newcomers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, as well as incumbents DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for targets in a good New England offense led by Drake Maye. Unfortunately, he doesn't have a path to fantasy consistency and is best stashed only in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Greg Dulcich will look for increased target share in Week 2 when the Dolphins face the 49ers. Entering the season opener, Miami had minimal proven pass catchers, creating optimism around Dulcich, but despite a 74% snap rate, Dulcich was targeted just twice. San Francisco allowed just four catches and 31 yards to tight ends in their opener, so even if Miami is forced to throw from behind, it doesn't yet appear Dulcich has Malik Willis' eye, suggesting there are better fantasy options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Greg Dulcich's opportunities have been limited in Miami's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. Dulcich has four total catches on five targets to open the year, tallying 35 yards. Kansas City has allowed volume to the position through two weeks, surrendering 12 catches and two touchdowns, but just 74 total yards and 4.6 yards per target. Better fantasy options are available.
outlooksByWeek.4: Greg Dulcich will look to build on Week 3's momentum in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. After just five targets in his first two weeks, Dulcich recorded seven in Week 3, logging five receptions for 55 yards. Miami's receiving room is thin, and Malik Willis will be under constant pressure from Brian Flores' heavy-blitz scheme, allowing Dulcich to work underneath. Minnesota hasn't allowed a tight end to score, but three opposing tight ends have recorded at least 50 yards, giving Dulcich moderate Week 4 potential.
outlooksByWeek.5: Greg Dulcich hasn't played a meaningful role for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. After amassing seven targets in Week 3, Dulcich didn't get a look in Week 4 in a game where Miami completed only nine passes, giving him three or fewer targets in three of Miami's first four outings. While Cincinnati remains a defense that struggles against the position, allowing 67 or more yards to an opposing tight end in three straight weeks, Dulcich hasn't factored heavily enough to benefit.
outlooksByWeek.7: Greg Dulcich is facing an uphill battle for meaningful production when the Dolphins face the Jets in Week 7. Dulcich's usage has been sporadic, notching 12 targets in two games and five total in Miami's other three tilts, and he's topped 37 yards just once in five games. The Jets have been stingy against the position, allowing just one touchdown, though they have allowed 44 or more yards in three straight weeks. Miami's limited passing game further adds doubt to Dulcich's viability.

player.seasonOutlook: Dulcich is back on the fantasy radar as the top tight end on the Miami depth chart. The 2022 third-round pick for the Denver Broncos made some noise as a rookie with a 33-411-2 receiving line in 10 games, but he went on to total 16 targets during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before landing in Miami last season. Dulcich didn't see his first target until Week 9 but went on to post a 26-335-1 receiving line the rest of the way. He wasn't a regular fantasy option (one top-15 week among TEs), but he certainly has a path to a substantial target share in 2026 with minimal competition at tight end and with Miami so short-handed at wide receiver. The 26-year-old is a long shot for consistent fantasy value in an offense expected to struggle, but there's some deep-league sleeper appeal.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Royals scored his first career NFL touchdown in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the third quarter-the third of three TD passes for the superstar QB on the night. Royals, a fourth-round pick in 2025, has only four career catches in nine regular-season games, and he's firmly behind Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Tyquan Thornton on the WR depth chart. With Mahomes spreading the ball around early in the season, Royals could begin to establish a small but consistent role in the passing game. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Royals is beginning to establish a depth role in the Kansas City passing game. After being used only on special teams in the season opener, the second-year wide receiver has had double-digit snaps on offense the last two weeks, getting three targets from Patrick Mahomes and catching all three for 17 yards and his first NFL touchdown. If injuries were to hit, Royals could move into a more significant role. Unless that happens, he's unlikely to contribute in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Royals could be headed for a big opportunity coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. With Tyquan Thornton likely out for the season due to an ankle injury in a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Royals could emerge as Patrick Mahomes' preferred deep option while Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Travis Kelce handle underneath routes. That role allowed Thornton to erupt for a 5-111-2 line prior to getting hurt against Las Vegas, and Royals showed similar big-play ability in college. The 2025 fourth-round pick will be a very intriguing dart throw in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Royals recorded a career-high four targets in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching two for 24 yards. The second-year wideout's role has slightly increased with Rashee Rice sidelined, but Royals still has yet to prove himself as a trusted option for Patrick Mahomes. Even if Rice remains on the shelf in Week 7, Royals isn't likely to break out against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Mooney caught both of his passes in Week 1 for the Giants. Mooney had two catches for 27 yards in the shocking 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Mooney had fewer targets than rookie Malachi Fields, an intriguing development. Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely already look like the favorite targets for quarterback Jaxson Dart, though, so it could be slim pickings for Mooney and the rest of the pass-catching corps. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in its opener, allowing 205 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Darnell Mooney led the Giants in receiving last game.  Unfortunately, Mooney managed just 48 yards on two catches in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The bigger news is that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Mooney will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darnell Mooney has two catches in each of his first three games with the Giants. Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 50 yards in any single contest. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Mooney as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darnell Mooney did not manage a reception last game for the Giants. Mooney was targeted twice, but could not get into the scorebook. He has still not scored through four contests, and has just six catches over that span.  In Week 5, Mooney and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darnell Mooney saw seven targets for the Giants last game. Unfortunately, Mooney dropped a couple of passes and failed to connect with quarterback Jameis Winston on some others.  Mooney finished with two catches for just 14 yards, and has just eight receptions on the season. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darnell Mooney sustained a neck injury in the second half of the last game for the Giants. Mooney did not record a catch prior to his exit, though did manage a 20-yard rush. Mooney has struggled in his first season with the Giants, recording just eight catches for 109 yards on the season. It remains to be seen if he will be able to suit up in Week 7 versus the Texans. If he can play, Mooney would face a Texans defense allowing 246 passing yards per clash, which is 27th in the NFL.
