player.seasonOutlook: Mooney signed with the Giants to help replace Wan'Dale Robinson as the team's No. 2 receiver behind Malik Nabers. Mooney's production has been all over the map throughout his career, having posted strong 81-1,055-4 and 64-992-5 receiving lines over the past five seasons, while also finishing in the 400-to-500-yard range the other three campaigns during the span. The 28-year-old has proven to be a serviceable starting receiver and could easily settle in second or third in line for targets in the Giants' ascending, Jaxson Dart-led offense. Mooney's ceiling isn't very high, so he's barely worth late round consideration in deep leagues.

The rebuilding Dolphins are woefully lacking in talent on both sides of the football, and they're coming off a season in which they tied for 21st in fantasy points from the D/ST. An opening-week matchup against the Raiders could make them a viable streaming choice -- though that's directed more at you 12-, 14-team and Knockout managers ? but there's little else to like here, especially with one of the toughest overall schedules in the league ahead.

outlooksByWeek.2: Demarcus Robinson should again have a key role for San Francisco in Week 2 against the Dolphins. After rookie De'Zhaun Stribling hurt his ankle in a season-opening win over the Rams, Robinson stepped up as the team's No. 3 wideout and produced two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown. Stribling is expected to miss at least a month, so Robinson will likely continue to work as the 49ers third wideout behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. Miami presents a good matchup after falling to the Raiders 27-13 and yielding three passing touchdowns Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in San Francisco's win over the Dolphins on Sunday, and his status is very much in doubt for a Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Before getting hurt, Robinson caught all three of his targets for 34 yards against Miami as the 49ers' No. 3 wideout. In the likely scenario that he can't play in Week 3, Jacob Cowing would stand to step into Robinson's place in the pecking order. Arizona has given up four receiving TDs to wide receivers through two weeks, tied for the most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: The seeds are here for the Cardinals to have a respectable pass defense -- Budda Baker, Josh Sweat and Will Johnson all return -- but a lot would need to go right for Nick Rallis' defense to become a fantasy force. As is, the Cardinals have one of the league's toughest D/ST schedules, largely due to their playing in last year's winningest division -- their three division rivals combined to go 38-13. But hey, they do have what could be a great fantasy-playoff schedule (NYJ, @NO, LV, from Weeks 15-17), if they show us anything early.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tommy Tremble is expected to operate as Carolina's top tight end in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. The Notre Dame product led the Panthers' tight end corps in targets (five) and receptions (three) in the Week 1 loss, though he was outgained by Darren Waller (2-28-0). Tremble could very well operate as Carolina's No. 3 receiving option going forward, as Xavier Legette saw just two targets in Week 1. Additionally, Tremble is in for a great Week 2 matchup, as Atlanta's defense allowed 19.4 PPR fantasy points to tight ends last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tommy Tremble is expected to remain the Panthers' top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Tremble was overshadowed by Darren Waller in the Week 2 win, as Waller paced Carolina's tight end corps in targets (three), receptions (three), yards (33) and touchdowns (two) Despite this, Tremble played six more Darren Waller (32 to 26), suggesting he's still operating as the Panthers' top TE. Regardless, Tremble could struggle in Week 3 against a Browns defense that's allowed just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tommy Tremble is expected to remain one of Carolina's top tight ends in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Tremble has had a solid start to the season, catching seven of 11 targets for 70 yards. Despite this, he's been overtaken by Darren Waller for the Panthers' top receiving TE, as Waller has tallied 10 receptions on 14 targets for 112 yards and two touchdowns. Regardless, Tremble should be in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 33.4 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tommy Tremble is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top tight ends in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Tremble tallied a season-high four receptions during the Week 4 win over the Lions, even though it led to just 12 receiving yards. He ranks second amongst Carolina's tight end corps in yards (82), targets (14) and receptions (11) through four games this season, being primarily used as a blocker. Tremble could struggle in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's allowed no touchdowns to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tommy Tremble will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Tremble had his most productive outing of the 2026 season in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, catching all four targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns. Despite this performance, Tremble ranks second amongst Carolina tight ends in targets (18) and yards (128) through six weeks, trailing Darren Waller (21 targets and 148 yards). Tremble could stay productive in Week 7 against a Buccaneers defense that's given up 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Sanders enters his second NFL season set to back up Deshaun Watson in Cleveland. Sanders made eight appearances during his rookie season and wasn't overly productive, scoring eight all-purpose touchdowns, throwing 10 interceptions and completing 57% of his passes. The fifth-round pick produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 18th, though it was an impressive 364-yard passing game with four total touchdowns (33.5 points). Sanders added some value with his legs, including 20-plus yards in five straight games to end the season. The 24-year-old remains a wild card and is likely to earn some starts this season, so that's enough to make him worthy off a stash in superflex/dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Watkins heads into San Francisco's Week 4 matchup versus Denver with momentum on his side. Watkins played for the first time this season Sunday versus Arizona and caught both of his targets for 60 yards. That production came with No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) missing the entire second half of the contest, and Watkins' opportunities in Week 4 could logically depend upon Evans' ability to suit up. With that said, the Broncos could be a challenge for the 49ers' wideout corps as a whole given the 50.9% catch rate they've yielded to WRs so far (second-best in the NFL), though Rams star WR Davante Adams did just a 7-137-0 line on them in Week 3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Legette appears to be an afterthought in Carolina's offensive game plan, as he received just two targets despite the team scoring 37 points in the Week 1 loss. He's clearly behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (ankle) in the WR room, so it's unlikely Legette will see much volume going forward. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 2 matchup, as Atlanta's defense allowed just 8.6 yards per completion in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in Carolina's receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Legette had a solid Week 2 performance after putting up a goose egg in Week 1, catching two of four targets for 64 yards. The third-year pro remains firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker in Carolina's receiving corps, as the two have combined for 26 receptions, 380 yards and a touchdown through two weeks. However, Legette could take advantage of a Cleveland secondary that's allowed 10.0 yards per target to opposing WRs heading into Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Legette (knee) is expected to operate as one of Carolina's top deep threats if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Legette was sidelined for the Week 3 loss to the Browns but showcased some big-play ability the week prior, catching a 55-yard bomb from Bryce Young. Even if Legette suits up for the Week 4 contest, he'll likely play a depth role behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (quadriceps), if active. Legette could really take advantage of a struggling Lions secondary that's allowed 10.4 yards per completion this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Legette is eyeing a Year 3 leap after a boom/bust start to his NFL career. The 2024 first-round pick flashed with 521 yards and four touchdowns on 55 touches as a rookie, but fell to 363 yards and three scores on 36 touches in 2025. Legette did post a pair of big games (24.2 points in Week 7 and 18.3 points in Week 11), but was otherwise held in check (3.6 PPG in the other 13 games). Legette has struggled with the ball in his hands (woeful 2.1 RAC in his career) and is behind Tetairoa McMillan and likely Jalen Coker on the Carolina WR depth chart. The 25-year-old will see some situational targets and carries, but he'll need a big Year 3 leap to find his way to fantasy relevance. He's no more than a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Williams' role could be elevated for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers with WR Omar Cooper (ankle) questionable. Williams logged just one Week 1 target despite playing 62% of the snaps in a game where the Jets led early and throughout-a script unlikely to materialize again in Week 2. With potential double-coverage on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell running vertically, Williams could find ample space underneath without Cooper's presence, making him someone to consider in very deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Williams will look to build on an expanding role in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. Elevated to No. 3 on the depth chart with Omar Cooper landing on IR, Williams recorded six targets last week, catching them all for just 34 yards. The Jets' offense is unlikely to score enough to sustain a third viable receiver, but if there were such a matchup, it would be Week 3 against a secondary that's already allowed 437 yards to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets' offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 tilt against the Bears. Despite the absence of Adonai Mitchell in Week 3, Williams logged only two targets in a game where the Jets threw 37 times. While the Bears are allowing 8.5 yards per target to receivers, Williams doesn't seem likely to garner enough looks to exploit a potentially favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Williams continues to amass minimal volume for the Jets as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. Williams flashed in Week 4, finishing with 73 yards and a touchdown, but it came on just three targets. While Cleveland has allowed three receivers to top 70 yards over the last two weeks, Williams' lack of opportunities makes for a boom-or-bust play in Week 5, and that assumes Adonai Mitchell doesn't return from a two-week absence.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets offense may be declining ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Despite Adonai Mitchell's three-week absence, Williams has not logged more than three targets, and his snap share fell to a season-low 59% in Week 5 with the return of Tim Patrick. The Jets aren't throwing the ball enough to sustain secondary pass-catching options, and New England is allowing just 7.5 yards per target, the ninth-lowest in the league, leaving Williams with minimal appeal.

outlooksByWeek.3: Tyson Bagent is set to get the start for Chicago in Week 3 versus the Eagles. With Caleb Williams currently week-to-week with a hamstring injury and doubtful against Philly, Bagent is primed to get his first start since the 2023 season. The D2 product completed five of nine passes for 54 yards in the fourth quarter against the Vikings this past week after filling in for Williams, but he was unable to deliver a win for the Bears in the end. Bagent's most notable stats trail back to 2023, when he completed 94 of 143 passing attempts for 859 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions across five games while filling in for Justin Fields. He'll face an Eagles offense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyson Bagent will likely be Chicago's backup quarterback again in Week 4 against the Jets. Bagent didn't get the start in Week 3 after getting next-to-no practice reps with a concussion, and Case Keenum throwing for 247 yards and two touchdowns should keep it that way. The D2 product will now only face New York's defense if something were to happen to the veteran.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyson Bagent is primed to get the starting nod once again as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Bagent completed 25 of 34 passes for 268 yards and an interception in a win over the Jets during Week 4, which was enough for Ben Johnson to announce him as the starter once again. The D2 product will now have to face a Packers defense on their home turf, which has ranked top ten against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyson Bagent's role is up in the air for Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Bagent got the start in Week 5 against the Packers, but a 57 percent completion rate for 87 yards and a 0:2 TD:INT eventually got him benched for veteran Case Keenum, who didn't fare much better. If Caleb Williams sits out another game with his hamstring injury, it's unknown if the Bears will roll with Bagent or Keenum. If Bagent does see the field, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Stevens missed a field goal and an extra point in Week 1 for Washington. The Commanders lost by two points, making the misses all the more glaring. Stevens will have a chance to rebound in Week 2, though, as Washington faces a Dallas squad that allowed the most points in the NFL last season, and looked no better in their season opener versus the Giants. Dallas lost an ugly 28-20 affair to the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Stevens missed his second field goal of the season last game for Washington. Stevens did make two other field goals as well as both of his PATs, but the Commanders offense is not a pretty option for a fairly shaky kicker heading into a brutal Week 3 matchup versus Seattle. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per contest thus far this season, which is second in the NFL. In addition, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels is unlikely to play for the Commanders after dislocating his elbow.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drew Stevens connected on an impressive 57-yard field goal in Washington's 33-31 win over the Seahawks last game. However, Stevens also missed an extra point, and has now missed four kicks through three outings. Stevens has a big leg but could be on thin ice with a few more misses. He should have ample opportunities in Week 4 versus the Colts, though. Indianapolis is allowing 30.3 points per tilt, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in three-straight games for the Commanders. Stevens connected on two field goals, as well as an extra point, in Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London. In Week 5, Washington will face the first-place New York Giants. New York's defense has been much-improved in 2026, allowing just 19.8 points per tilt, which is eighth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drew Stevens missed an extra point last game for Washington. With the contest resulting in a 27-27 tie, Stevens could have been viewed as the goat. However, late-game clock mismanagement by the offense failed to allow Stevens a chance at redemption, as the Commanders could not get off a game-winning field goal attempt as time expired in overtime. Stevens did hit two other field goals as well as another extra point in the contest. His job should still be safe heading into Week 6 versus the 49ers. However, his opportunities could be limited, as San Fran is yielding just 18.6 points per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cole Kmet will aim to stay involved as the Bears take on the Vikings in Week 2. Kmet brought in two of three targets for 35 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 1, and he was the only tight end to record a catch. While the veteran is set to be a secondary option behind Colston Loveland this season, the high-scoring ability of Chicago could allow plenty of targets for the pair. They'll face a Minnesota defense that gave up five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cole Kmet remains a depth option as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Even though Kmet played more offensive snaps in Week 2 (69 percent) than in Week 1 (57 percent), he garnered just one target and was unable to catch it. Still, young tight end Colston Loveland has yet to do much this year, which could keep a veteran presence like Kmet relevant. He'll face a Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Kmet started off the season hot with two catches for 35 yards and a touchdown, but he's been unable to catch his sole target in each of the last two games. The veteran tight end is still a big part of Chicago's offense, but it's to be seen if this goes beyond blocking work. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cole Kmet remains a depth option in Chicago's passing game in Week 5 at Green Bay. Kmet hasn't replicated his two catches for 35 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 against Carolina, but he caught two for 13 yards this past Sunday against the Jets. While the veteran tight end is still a big part of Chicago's offense, his role is currently centered around blocking work. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option in Chicago's passing game during Week 6 at Atlanta. Kmet recorded another catch in Week 5 against the Packers, bringing in one of two targets for eight yards. The veteran tight end has now logged five catches for 56 yards and a touchdown across five games this season. He'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option in Chicago's passing game during Week 7 against New Engand. Kmet recorded two catches for three yards in Week 6 against the Falcons, with one of them being a near trip to the end zone. The veteran tight end has now logged seven catches for 59 yards and a touchdown across six games this season. He'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy TEs this year.

Myles Price will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Price mostly contributed on special teams to start the season, but he's seen an uptick in usage, with five catches for 45 yards in his last two outings. While more targets will be needed to make him an attractive target beyond his return abilities, he's worth keeping an eye on, especially against an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs.

outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Mims has yet to get significant work as a pass catcher this season for the Broncos, but that could soon change. The speedster missed two games with a foot injury, and in the two games in which he's been healthy, he sat behind Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, and Pat Bryant on the depth chart. Bryant left a Week 4 loss to the 49ers with an ankle sprain, however, and Mims garnered his first targets of the season, catching one of three for 10 yards. He's always capable of producing in the return game, but Mims could contribute on offense in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marvin Mims' role in the Broncos' offense has increased with Pat Bryant sidelined. Over the last two weeks, Mims has caught three of five targets for 16 yards while adding three rushing yards on one carry. Those numbers are modest at best, but the fourth-year speedster is a big-play candidate every time he gets the ball in his hands, whether as a pass catcher or as a kick returner. Mims isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Marvin Mims continues to fill a secondary role in a lackluster Broncos offense. The fourth-year speedster has logged nine targets over the last three games while Pat Bryant has been injured, turning that volume into a 5-29-0 line while also taking one carry for three yards. Mims has also handled kick return duties during that time, but it would likely take an injury to Jaylen Waddle or Courtland Sutton for him to move into a significant role in the passing game. Mims could get a chance to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 in a Week 7 clash with a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers, 31st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: James is an intriguing insurance stash as a candidate to work as 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't record a single touch on three snaps during a rookie campaign spent buried behind McCaffrey and a host of veterans. James wasn't utilized much as a receiver at the collegiate level and underwhelmed at last year's combine, so it's unclear what his upside will be in the pros. However, if the 22-year-old wins the No. 2 gig over rookie Kaelon Black and McCaffrey misses action, he'll be a priority add. Consider him in the final few rounds in deep leagues.

Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sione Vaki is poised to serve as Detroit's supplementary running back once again in Week 2 at Buffalo. While the Lions were planning to use a committee approach at RB2 this season, Vaki was the only other player at the position who saw the field behind star Jahmyr Gibbs. The third-year ball carrier recorded two rushes for seven yards and brought in his sole target for 11 yards. This makes it likely he'll be the main option behind Gibbs at least in the short term. Vaki will face a Bills defense that allowed 33.9 PPR fantasy points to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sione Vaki should remain Detroit's low-usage RB2 in Week 3 against the Jets. Vaki logged one carry for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards against the Bills in Week 2, showcasing that the secondary running back for the Lions is a graveyard role this year. The third-year ball carrier is still on pace to log career-high numbers given his small role so far in his career, but he's nothing more than a depth option with Jahmyr Gibbs healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sione Vaki will remain Detroit's secondary running back option in Week 4 at Carolina. Vaki hasn't been able to carve out much of a role behind phenom Jahmyr Gibbs so far this season, but he did register a season-high six carries for 26 yards, along with another catch for 11 yards in Week 3. The third-year running back remains a depth option given the usage of Gibbs so far this season, so it won't matter much that the Panthers defense has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sione Vaki will remain Detroit's second running back option in Week 5 at Arizona. Vaki hasn't been able to produce much behind phenom Jahmyr Gibbs so far this season, but he did record his fourth straight game with a catch against the Panthers in Week 4. The third-year running back remains a depth option given the usage of Gibbs so far this season, and he'll face a Cardinals defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sione Vaki will look to do the most with his opportunities as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Vaki's ceiling is relatively low with Jahmyr Gibbs ahead of him, but blowout wins have allowed the third-year rusher to stay involved this season. Vaki has now totaled 15 carries for 51 yards and four catches for 52 yards across five games this season. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

Tutu Atwell was a healthy scratch in Week 6, but the wideout could be back in the mix in Week 7 against the Raiders, as the Rams need depth in the receiving corps after Davante Adams' hamstring injury. Atwell has three catches for 31 yards on four targets this season, so even if he's part of the active roster in Week 7 against a subpar Raiders defense, he's not expected to have a prominent role on offense. At least the matchup is favorable on paper since Las Vegas ranks in the bottom 10 in receiving yards allowed, touchdowns allowed and fantasy points per game allowed to opposing wideouts in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Goodson is the third backup running back already for the Cowboys this season. With Malik Davis injured and Emari Demercado deemed ineffective, Goodson had six carries for 22 yards in his season-debut versus the Ravens. However, Javonte Williams remains the undisputed starter, leaving Goodson and company picking up the scraps. In Week 4, the Cowboys will also face a rather stingy Texans run defense allowing 86.7 yards per game on the ground, which is fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Goodson managed three carries for 12 yards last game for the Cowboys. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams had 24 touches and three touchdowns in the comeback win over the Texans. In other words, Goodson's utility is extremely low barring injury. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Goodson did not receive a touch out of the backfield last game for the Cowboys. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams had 14 touches and a touchdown and continues to be the workhorse for the offense on the ground. If Goodson sees any touches in Week 6, he could find some room, though, as Green Bay's defense has been extremely suspect in defending the run. The Packers are allowing 127.6 rushing yards per contest, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Goodson had just three offensive touches last game for Dallas. Goodson gained only nine yards, as he continues to be the primary, albeit little-used backup to Javonte Williams. Interestingly, though, Goodson returned five kicks for 122 yards after Kavontae Turpin went down with a rib injury. Goodson could reprise that role in Week 7 versus the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth piece in Tampa Bay's wide-receiver room in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Johnson has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 campaign, catching four of nine targets for 74 yards through four games. Additionally, the Buccaneers will likely continue relying on the running game more, as it favors rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels while Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains out. Despite this, Johnson should be in for a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that's allowed 8.3 yards per pass attempt this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Although Johnson was targeted just once in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, he made the most of his opportunity, totaling 64 receiving yards. He's appears firmly behind Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Cade Otton in Tampa Bay's passing attack, and likely won't be fantasy relevant without a touchdown going forward. Johnson is in for a tougher Week 6 matchup against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed 7.9 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth option in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson played just 34% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, catching two of three targets for seven yards. He could find more fantasy value if Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to return for the Week 7 contest, but Johnson will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown. Additionally, Johnson is in for a difficult matchup against a Panthers defense that's given up just two touchdowns to wideouts all season.

outlooksByWeek.4: Zach Ertz made his return to the Eagles last game, but it was not exactly triumphant. Signed during the week due to the injury to Dallas Goedert, Ertz managed just one catch for nine yards in the dismal 27-7 loss to the Bears.  Goedert's status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. Johnny Mundt also had a four-yard grab and would also see some run without Goedert. Even Goedert cannot suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.3 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zach Ertz caught two passes last game for the Eagles, as he continues to fill in for his injured former understudy, Dallas Goedert. It appears that Goedert is unlikely to suit up in  Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. Ertz had four targets last game and could prove a useful safety valve with an otherwise young, inexperienced pass-catching corps. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joshua Palmer's role within the Bills' offense is minimal at best entering a Week 2 matchup against the Lions. Palmer's snap share was 29% to open the season, and while his lone catch went for a big 34-yard gain, he drew just two targets. The passing game appears to flow through newly acquired DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, and tight end Dalton Kincaid, keeping Palmer on the fringe for production despite a terrific matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joshua Palmer will look to make another chunk play for the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. Palmer has just two catches on the year, but they've gone for 34- and 43-yard touchdowns. The Chargers are allowing 10.8 yards per target to wideouts, the third highest through two weeks, so while volume isn't likely, Palmer could still contribute.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joshua Palmer remains a low-volume option in the Bills' run-first offense ahead of Week 4's matchup with the Patriots. Palmer failed to record a target in Week 3 and has only two on the season. He's been a deep-ball specialist on those rare looks, but facing a New England secondary that is allowing just 6.6 yards per target, Palmer isn't likely to break off a big play in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Joshua Palmer was not a factor in the Bills' passing game in Weeks 3 and 4, and now Buffalo travels to face the Rams in Week 5. Palmer has totaled three catches all season, and over the last two weeks has only one grab for three yards. He's primarily a deep option and as such, not much of a fantasy option against a defense that's allowing a stingy 6.5 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Joshua Palmer will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he's to reprise his big-play, low-volume role in the Bills passing game in a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Palmer missed the team's Week 5 tilt with the Rams and has just three catches on the year. Averaging 26.7 yards per catch, Palmer has shown he can do more with less, but the lack of consistent targets in a run-first offense makes for a high-risk, medium-reward option.

outlooksByWeek.5: Treylon Burks snagged a 47-yard touchdown last game for the Commanders. Burks has scored in consecutive games for the Commanders. However, Terry McLaurin is likely to return from a hamstring injury in Week 5 versus the Giants, which could negatively affect Burks. New York has also been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Treylon Burks was second on the team in targets last game. Burks had a season-high five looks in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Unfortunately, he corralled just two of those balls for 26 yards, and had a two-game scoring streak snapped. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Lock is expected to serve as Seattle's starting quarterback in Week 2 versus Arizona due to Sam Darnold's glute injury. Lock took over in the first quarter of the Seahawks' season opener and guided the team to a win, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. Lock's TD was a 45-yard connection with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who again figures to be his top target against the Cardinals. Arizona is coming off a surprising win against the Chargers, during which they limited Justin Herbert to 209 yards and an interception.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Lock could have another opportunity to lead Seattle's offense in Week 3 versus Washington. Lock started for the injured Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday versus Arizona and threw for 235 yards with three touchdowns. Darnold is reportedly making good progress in his recovery, so it's not yet clear who will helm the team's offense in Week 3. Whichever QB gets the opportunity could be in for a big game against the Commanders, who have allowed a league-high seven passing touchdowns and have no interceptions through two weeks.

Jacob Cowing stands to take on a bigger role in San Francisco's offense if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can't suit up versus Arizona in Week 3. Cowing hasn't seen much opportunity on offense yet, playing just 27 offensive snaps without drawing a target through two games. However, Robinson seems likely to miss Week 3 due to his injury, and if that's the case Cowing would likely be called upon to step into a larger amount of work in the passing game. The Cardinals haven't been good against the pass this season and just allowed star Seattle WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to rack up 155 receiving yards and three TDs in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacob Cowing could be in for a bigger role in the 49ers' wideout corps Week 4 against Denver depending on the status of No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (ribs/oblique). If Evans can't play against the Broncos, both Cowing and Jordan Watkins figure to see a rise in their offensive snap counts. However, Cowing was held without a catch (on two targets) this past Sunday against Arizona even with Evans exiting in the second quarter, so fantasy managers may not be able to count on Cowing for increased production even with more opportunity. Adding to that context is the fact that the Broncos have a tough pass defense that has limited WRs to 18.4 fantasy points per game this season, 10th-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacob Cowing may be in for a bigger role on offense for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Deebo Samuel suffered an injured hamstring versus Seattle this past Sunday, and if he's out versus the Commanders, Cowing should be slated for a key role in the team's passing game. He's yet to make much of an impact so far with just one catch on five targets for nine yards, but there could be room for him to succeed against Washington. The Commanders are surrendering 14.6 receptions per game to wideouts, tied for second-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jacob Cowing and the 49ers travel to square off against the Falcons in Week 7. He did not record a target during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6, marking his third such outing through six games. Cowing tallied 24 yards on one kickoff return and two yards on one punt return, fumbling once while making the recovery. Even with Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to miss the road tilt with Atlanta, Cowing should not be considered in any fantasy format until he's able to prove otherwise.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyquan Thornton saw only one target in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, failing to bring in a deep ball from Patrick Mahomes, and that sums up his role in the passing game. The former Patriot will hit for big plays on occasion, as 11 of his 19 receptions in 2025 went for 20 yards or more, but he won't see enough volume to be a reliable contributor unless injuries open up more volume for him. Thornton gets a more exploitable matchup in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyquan Thornton produced strong numbers in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, hauling in all four of his targets for 86 yards. The fifth-year speedster is at best fifth in the pecking order for looks from Patrick Mahomes, but his role as a deep option gives Thornton some big-play potential in the right matchup, even on limited volume. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyquan Thornton is settling in as a deep option for Patrick Mahomes. After getting blanked in Kansas City's opener, Thornton has caught six passes over the last two games on seven targets, and two of those receptions have gone for 20 yards or more. He's collected 108 yards in total, and while he's still looking for his first touchdown of 2026, it would take just one defensive breakdown to free him up for a long score. Thornton's low volume will make him a risky option in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

Case Keenum is in line to get the start again as the Bears play the Jets. Keenum amazed in his first start since 2023, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions, while rushing four times for six yards and another score. The veteran quarterback most definitely guaranteed another opportunity if starter Caleb Williams remains out with a hamstring injury, which is currently the likely scenario. Keenum will face a Mean Green defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Case Keenum is set to serve as the backup quarterback as the Bears travel to play the Packers in Week 5. Keenum started on the field at quarterback with Tyson Bagent lined up as a receiver in Week 5 against the Jets, but Bagent ultimately played the game, and Keenum served as his backup. Keenum's role should remain minimal, if not null, so long as Bagent stays healthy in Green Bay. The Green and Gold defense gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Case Keenum usage is up in the air for Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Keenum entered Week 5 versus the Packers as the backup quarterback, but he ended up coming in and completing 11 of 19 passes for 108 yards and one interception after Tyson Bagent's struggles. While Keenum didn't fair that much better than Bagent, the Bears might want to rely on a veteran play caller if Caleb Williams misses another week with a hamstring injury. If Keenum does draw the start, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

Zavion Thomas will seek to stay involved as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Thomas was on the field for a season-high 22 percent of offensive snaps in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, and he was able to bring in his sole target for 11 yards. The rookie remains a return specialist first at this point in the season, but he could continue to see opportunities in the passing game. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zavion Thomas will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Thomas logged a season-best performance in Week 6 against the Falcons, bringing in all three of his targets for 25 yards. The rookie wide receiver had just two catches to his name in the first five games of the season, so his output could continue to grow with Caleb Williams situated in the pass-heavy offense. New England has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. The LSU product is small (5'10/190), but extremely fast (4.28 40-yard dash) and figures to make his hay as a situational rusher, receiver and returner in the pros. He was limited to a 13% target share across his final three collegiate seasons (one at Mississippi State and two at LSU), having failed to clear 41 catches, 536 receiving yards or five touchdowns in any of the three campaigns. He'll battle Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker for work behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Thomas is unlikely to emerge into a reliable fantasy option.

Singleton was selected by the Titans in the fifth round of April's draft. He is a big, versatile back with terrific speed who can contribute as a rusher, receiver, blocker and returner. While working in a committee with fellow rookie Kaytron Allen at Penn State the past four years, Singleton was effective after contact (3.46 YAC is sixth best in this RB rookie class) but struggled with elusiveness (8.0 forced missed tackle rate is worst). He was solid as receiver (102-987-9) and returner (class-high 1,138 kick return yards) during his 53-game tenure. Singleton will open his career behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, but would make for an interesting waiver add in the event of a Pollard injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) could start if active for the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed eight total touchdowns to the Bears in Week 1. Tagovailoa was unable to suit up last week after sustaining an oblique injury in practice, which is likely a factor in why Atlanta's offense struggled so much. He struggled in 2025, throwing for 2,660 yards and 20 touchdowns while turning it over 16 times in just 14 contests. The Falcons' offense is in for a very favorable matchup, however, as Carolina gave up 334 total yards and five touchdowns to Caleb Williams last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta during the offseason after spending his first six seasons in Miami. The 2020 first-round pick showed signs of life a few years ago, which included a 4,624-yard, 29-TD season in 2023, but his production and efficiency have declined since. The final straw was a rough 2025 in which he threw 15 INTs (second most in the league) in just 14 games and was benched. Tagovailoa is a nonfactor with his legs (fewer than 75 yards in four straight seasons, with zero TDs during the span) and has, in turn, never finished better than 10th in fantasy points per game (he was 33rd in 2025). Even if Tagovailoa starts in Week 1, he's unlikely to be anything more than a fringe QB2 in fantasy and figures to eventually lose work to Michael Penix Jr. (recovering from a torn ACL). Tagovailoa is way off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carson Wentz could be in line to start again as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Wentz came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion) against the Packers in Week 1, and he ended up delivering a come-from-behind win. The veteran completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns, and he did not commit a turnover during the matchup. If Murray is unable to clear concussion protocol ahead of Sunday, Wentz will be in position to get his first start since 2025 against a Bears defense that gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carson Wentz will return to Minnesota's backup role in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. Wentz performed well while leading the Vikings to a 2-0 record, completing 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in that stretch. The veteran quarterback will remain a solid backup behind Kyler Murray, although anything can happen as the season progresses.

outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Juszczyk is unlikely to play for San Francisco in Week 5 against Seattle. Juszczyk suffered a knee injury in Week 4 versus Denver and is slated to miss multiple weeks of action as a result. The veteran fullback doesn't typically log gaudy statistics, but his role as a blocker has been a critical component of the 49ers' offense. As such, Juszczyk's absence could impact the team's running and passing games versus a tough Seahawks defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Heidenreich was selected by the Steelers in the seventh round of April's draft. Heidenreich is an intriguing prospect, as he's a tweener who could play running back or receiver in the pros. The Navy product never cleared 77 carries in a single season, but did post a 51-941-6 receiving line in 2025. For his career, he averaged 6.85 yards per carry and evaded one tackle for every 5.9 touches, both of which are best in this RB rookie class. He'll likely max out as a gadget player behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joey Slye is unlikely to get many kicking opportunities in Week 2, when Tennessee's underwhelming offense faces the ferocious Eagles defense. The Titans generated just 195 yards of total offense in their 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, and Tennessee was a bottom-three team in both yards and points per game last season, while Philadelphia gave up the fifth-fewest points in 2025. Slye isn't known for his accuracy, either, so he isn't worth using in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joey Slye has been limited to two or fewer field-goal attempts in 12 of his last 13 outings for the Titans, who continue to have one of the league's worst offenses. After averaging 16.7 points per game last season, Tennessee is scoring 15.0 PPG heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants. It's a favorable matchup on paper since the Giants are banged up on both sides of the ball, but MetLife Stadium tends to have some of the least-favorable weather conditions for kickers, and Slye's upside will continue to be capped by the Titans' inability to consistently move the ball on offense. There are better kicking options available for fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joey Slye missed his only field-goal attempt in tough conditions against the Giants in Week 3, and his opportunities figure to remain limited in Week 4 at Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing 26.0 points per game, but Tennessee's underwhelming offense rarely gets into scoring range, which is why Slye has attempted at least three field goals in only one of his last 14 games. Slye also has accuracy issues, as the last time he exceeded an 80% success rate on field-goal attempts was 2022.
outlooksByWeek.5: Joey Slye has made just four field goals through four games, and he's unlikely to get many chances in Week 5 against the Texans while kicking behind a Titans offense that's generating a league-low 261.3 yards per game. Houston has allowed 11 made field goals, which is tied for the most in the NFL, but Slye has attempted more than two field goals just once in his last 15 games. Despite the favorable matchup, Slye is best left on waivers in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Joey Slye continues to be limited by a league-worst Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards (246.4) and points (11.6) per game heading into a Week 6 trip to Indianapolis. Slye has made just five field goals in as many games and has logged more than two field-goal attempts in only one of his last 16 appearances. The Colts have given up 11 made field goals in five games and 24.8 points per game, but a relatively favorable Week 6 matchup isn't enough to propel Slye out of the bottom tier of fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Joey Slye converted all four of his field-goal attempts in Week 6 against the Colts as the Titans notched their first win of the season. That performance marked only the second time in Slye's last 17 games that he has made more than two field goals. Slye is likely to revert in Week 7 against a Browns team that's allowing just 20.3 points per game, as a Titans offense that's tied for last in the league with 14.0 points per game is unlikely to provide many scoring opportunities for Tennessee's kicker. There are likely better kicking options available on the waiver wire in most fantasy leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Troy Franklin had a small role in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, failing to catch his only target and gaining five rushing yards on one jet sweep. By contrast, Pat Bryant led the team with six targets and seems to be emerging as Bo Nix's most comfortable security blanket and the No. 3 receiver behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. Better days will be ahead for the Denver passing game, but Franklin has some work to do to earn meaningful production. He'll face a Jaguars defense in Week 2 that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Troy Franklin has seen his snap count increase in the Broncos' last two games due to an injury to Pat Bryant, but as yet the workload hasn't translated into significant target volume. In a Week 5 win over the Chargers, Franklin caught both his targets for just 16 yards. Denver's offense as a whole has struggled, and while having Sean Payton call plays again should pay dividends in the long run, Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton still figure to dominate looks from Bo Nix. Franklin faces a tough test in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Troy Franklin has played more than 30 snaps on offense in each of the last three weeks with Pat Bryant injured, but so far the increased role hasn't translated into much usage as a pass catcher. Franklin has caught all three of his targets for just 18 yards during that stretch, as he remains well behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the pecking order at wide receiver. Marvin Mims has also seen six touches during that stretch despite being on the field less often, giving Franklin little upside. He'll try to take advantage of what opportunities he does get in Week 7 as the Broncos face a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to WRs this season, 31st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Midway through the 2025 season, Franklin appeared well on his way to a Year 2 breakout. The 2024 fourth-round pick entered Denver's Week 12 bye with five touchdowns and a team-high 81 targets (22% share). He was demoted during the week off, however, and ended up with just 24 total targets (a 9% share) over his final seven games, including the playoffs. In total, Franklin finished a respectable 41st among receivers in fantasy PPG, but the 23-year-old's demotion, coupled with Denver's offseason acquisition of Jaylen Waddle, means he's nowhere close to the fantasy radar. Franklin will battle Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. Ignore him on draft day.

Allen was selected by the Commanders in the sixth round of April's draft. Allen has a good size and a solid efficiency profile, having ranked seventh in this rookie class in YAC (3.35) and 10th in forced missed tackle rate (4.5) during his four seasons at Penn State. Though he out-carried fellow draft prospect Nicholas Singleton in all four seasons at PSU, Allen was less involved as a receiver (career 70-490-4 line, including a weak 5.1 YPT) and doesn't figure to get much run as a receiver in the pros. Allen is a long shot as a sixth-rounder, but he's a name to monitor considering the state of the Washington backfield (Rachaad White, Jacory Croskey-Merritt). If Allen impresses during the offseason, he could sneak onto the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Raheim Sanders and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. After Dylan Sampson (knee) was ruled out in the first half, Sanders filled in as the No. 2 RB behind Quinshon Judkins. He notched one carry for one yard and caught all three targets for 25 yards while playing 16 snaps on offense. With Cleveland expected to play from behind often, Sanders could have a fairly sizable role in the passing game, no matter who the quarterback is. Tampa Bay allowed eight catches on nine targets for 52 yards to RBs in their Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3. He tallied two carries for four yards and caught his only target for seven yards during Cleveland's first win of the season in Week 2. Quinshon Judkins handled 12 of 15 carries by running backs, and as long as he remains healthy, the workload split should remain similar. Sanders does have some upside as a receiver out of the backfield, but his role is still too limited to be relied upon in fantasy. Carolina's defense has been susceptible on the ground, allowing 36.3 fantasy points to RBs (31st), but they rank 14th in receiving yards surrendered to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the rival Steelers for a divisional clash in Week 4. He took his lone carry for 17 yards and caught four of five targets for 34 yards during Cleveland's upset win in Week 3. Sanders was highly efficient with his five touches, finishing second on the team in receptions and third in targets. He should continue operating as the third-down back and in most passing situations, but his overall involvement is difficult to trust while Quinshon Judkins remains healthy. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points (22.1) and 25th in receiving yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Raheim Sanders and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5. He rushed twice for nine yards and caught both targets for seven yards during Cleveland's Week 4 win. Quinshon Judkins remains the unquestioned leader in the backfield, as he compiled 23 touches for 96 yards and one score. Sanders' workload will be similar in a favorable matchup against the Jets' 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.3) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the Ravens for an AFC North showdown in Week 6. He rushed three times for 12 yards and caught his only target for one yard during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Sanders was forced to exit the contest in the fourth quarter due to a hip injury, and there's no word yet on the severity of the issue. If he's unable to suit up in Week 6, Jaleel McLaughlin would be in line for more opportunities versus a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game (T-9th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith heads into his second NFL season set to compete with rookie Emmett Johnson for No. 2 duties behind new Chiefs' lead back Kenneth Walker III. Smith played just 17% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps as a rookie and had nearly as many targets (35) as he did carries (44). The seventh-round pick wasn't overly effective (3.43 yards per carry, 4.9 yards per target) and was able to reach double-digit fantasy points only once (13.1 in a Week 7 blowout win). The undersized 23-year-old would likely share the backfield even if Walker were to miss time, and he has minimal fantasy appeal.

outlooksByWeek.3: Noah Fant is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' tight end corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Fant had a surprisingly productive Week 1 outing, catching four of eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown. However, he didn't see a target in Week 2 while playing on 45 percent of the team's offensive snaps, suggesting he remains firmly behind Juwan Johnson. Additionally, Fant is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's given up just eight receptions to TEs through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Noah Fant is expected to operate as one of the Saints' top red-zone options in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Despite playing behind Juwan Johnson, Fant has produced in two of three contests this season, catching eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three touchdowns. He definitely benefits from the Saints averaging 44 pass attempts per game but could struggle remaining fantasy relevant if the touchdowns dry up. However, Fant is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's given up three touchdowns to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Noah Fant (abdomen) is expected to operate as one of the Saints' top tight ends if active for the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Fant was inactive for the Week 4 loss to the Falcons but has been productive when healthy, catching eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three touchdowns in just three appearances. The veteran from Iowa remains behind Juwan Johnson in the Saints' tight end corps, but Fant appears to be one of the team's top red zone options, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Fant will likely struggle if active for the Week 5 matchup, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 11 receptions and no touchdowns to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Noah Fant is expected to remain one of the Saints' top tight ends in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Fant was ineffective in his return from an abdomen injury during the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching his lone target for seven yards. Through four appearances this season, Fant is tied for the most receiving touchdowns (three) on the Saints and ranks fourth in receiving yards (73). He likely won't be fantasy relevant in the Week 6 unless finding the end zone, which is unlikely against a Giants defense that's allowed just two touchdowns to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Noah Fant is expected to continue operating as the Saints' No. 2 tight end in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Fant has underwhelmed over the last two weeks, catching just one of two targets for seven yards. Despite competing with Juwan Johnson for snaps, Fant has played on 67% and 59% of the Saints' offensive plays over the last two games, respectively. He caught three touchdowns in the team's first three games and will likely need to continue finding the end zone to stay fantasy relevant. Fant is in for a tough Week 7 matchup though, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just two receiving touchdowns to TEs this year.

outlooksByWeek.4: Laquon Treadwell has caught all four of his targets for 81 yards over the Colts' last two games, and the 31-year-old journeyman could continue to be used as a field stretcher in Week 4 against Washington's beatable secondary in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Indianapolis signed Darius Slayton after Pierce was placed on IR, but Slayton was inactive for the Week 3 win over Houston. Slayton could take over the role currently occupied by Treadwell, and even if Treadwell maintains that role, the latter lacks fantasy appeal considering Treadwell has just five touchdown catches in 96 games, with his last score coming in 2021.
outlooksByWeek.5: Laquon Treadwell led the Colts with 42 receiving yards on six targets in the Week 4 win over Washington. He's averaging 41 yards over the last three games heading into a Week 5 road game against the Steelers. The journeyman wideout has stepped up in a WR room depleted by injuries to Alec Pierce (heel; IR) and Keenan Allen (groin). Treadwell should maintain an expanded role in Week 5, which makes him a viable deep-league dart throw against a Steelers secondary that's still adjusting to the departure of starting CB Joey Porter, who was traded away prior to Week 4. Keep in mind that Treadwell has just five touchdown catches in 97 games and hasn't scored since 2021.
outlooksByWeek.6: Laquon Treadwell has been targeted 14 times in the last two games and remains the Colts' No. 3 healthy WR heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans, who rank among the 10 weakest units at preventing catches and yards for wideouts. Treadwell's recent usage and the favorable matchup make him a viable deep-league dart throw, but expectations should be tempered considering the 31-year-old veteran hasn't scored a TD since 2021 and has just five touchdowns in 98 career regular-season appearances. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are likely to continue outperforming Treadwell while the Colts remain without their leading 2025 receiver Alec Pierce (heel).
outlooksByWeek.7: Laquon Treadwell has operated as the Colts' No. 3 WR in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel), drawing 19 targets over the past three games. Treadwell has caught just nine of those targets for 97 yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since the 2022 season. He's earning enough volume to be worth a dart throw for desperate fantasy managers in deeper formats in Week 7 against the Vikings, but most leagues should have more enticing fantasy options floating around the waiver wire. Minnesota's allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game.

outlooksByWeek.5: Sean Tucker is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Tucker logged his first three carries of the 2026 season in the Week 4 loss to the Packers, rushing for 10 yards and a touchdown. Following offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's comments about getting Tucker more involved in the offense early in October, he appears to have established himself as the team's top goal-line option at running back. Despite this, Tucker will likely struggle remaining fantasy relevant without another touchdown in the Week 5 matchup against a Cowboys defense that's given up five total touchdowns to RBs this year.

outlooksByWeek.3: Demond Claiborne is set to be a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Claiborne did not log a carry as one of Aaron Jones' backups against the Bears in Week 2, but he did reel in his single target for two yards. Still, the rookie running back will remain a depth pick against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Demond Claiborne will remain a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Claiborne saw his first carries of the year in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, totaling three for just one yard. The rookie looks to be in a role opposite of DeeJay Dallas as Minnesota's secondary RB option, with veteran Aaron Jones holding full control while Jordan Mason is out. Claiborne will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Demond Claiborne will remain a secondary option in the backfield as the Vikings play the Saints in Week 5. Claiborne logged three carries for 12 yards against the Dolphins in Week 4, and he was the only other running back to record a carry besides veteran Aaron Jones. The rookie running back has appeared to be the secondary rushing option for Minnesota with Jordan Mason (thumb) out, while Deejay Dallas has handled some receiving work. Claiborne will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Demond Claiborne remains a depth option ahead of Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Claiborne saw an elevated role with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, but Mason's return to practice this week could diminish Claiborne's usage. The rookie running back will take his eight touches for 21 yards into a home matchup versus an Indy defense that's ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Claiborne was selected by the Vikings in the sixth round of April's draft. Claiborne is an undersized back who struggled badly with efficiency during his four seasons at Wake Forest. On 558 career carries, Claiborne averaged 4.66 yards per attempt (second worst in this RB rookie class), 2.68 yards after contact and produced 5-plus yards on a class-low 32% of his carries. Also not much of a factor in the passing game, Claiborne may be limited to change-of-pace/return work in the pros. He'll open his career as a depth player behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jack Bech was the only Raiders wide receiver to make much of a difference in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching three of four targets for 23 yards and a touchdown. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker, produced very similar numbers in terms of receptions and receiving yards. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Bech will look to continue building chemistry with Cousins in Week 2 against a Chargers secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jack Bech has been unable to escape a supporting role in the Raiders' offense to begin his second NFL season. Through two games, the 2025 second-round pick has a 5-48-1 line on just six targets, volume that will make it very difficult to make a consistent impact. Bech had to watch journeyman Cody White come off the practice squad and catch two red-zone TDs in a Week 2 win over the Chargers, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Bech seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Bech is a candidate for a Year 2 leap after an underwhelming rookie campaign. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 36% of Las Vegas' offensive snaps and cleared three targets in a game only twice. He failed to find the end zone while predominantly working as a short-range target. Bech will now compete with the likes of Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in a new-look offense led by coach Klint Kubiak and, at some point, No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is likely headed for a larger role in his second season and is worth a late-round flier.

Tolbert signed with Miami after spending his first four NFL seasons in Dallas. The 2022 third-round pick has a path to a substantial offensive role, with Malik Washington and rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas as his top competition for snaps and targets. We have seen Tolbert as a near-full-time player in a much better offense and he wasn't much of a fantasy option. That came in 2024 when he played 76% of the Cowboys' offensive snaps. He found the end zone seven times, but was held to 610 yards and finished 54th among receivers in fantasy PPG. Tolbert played a reduced role last season and his 203 yards were the fewest since his rookie season. The 27-year-old has very limited upside and isn't worth much late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emari Demercado filled in for the injured Malik Davis as the backup in Week 1, but barely had an impact for the Cowboys. Sitting behind starter Javonte Williams, Demercado had just two rushes for seven yards. Demercado should continue to occupy the backup role in the short term, though his opportunities should remain limited.  In Week 2, Demercado will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emari Demercado continues to play backup to Javonte Williams following the Malik Davis injury, but Demercado has had a marginal role through the first two games for Dallas. Demercado has five carries for a combined 15 yards behind Williams. Even if he receives a few extra touches, Demercado will have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Raridon was selected by the Patriots in the third round of April's draft. Raridon is a tall, blocking tight end who was barely targeted (5% share) and totaled a 48-623-3 receiving line during four seasons at Notre Dame. Most of the receiving work came in 2025, so perhaps there's some hope in that area, but he's a long shot for fantasy value any time soon, especially with Hunter Henry ahead of him on the depth chart this season.

outlooksByWeek.7: Will Mallory was targeted six times in the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans. He was the team's top pass-catching TE in the absence of Tyler Warren (groin), though Mallory corralled only two of those six looks from Daniel Jones for 20 yards. Mallory would be a viable deep-league dart throw in Week 7 against the Vikings if Warren remains sidelined, but Warren's return would push Mallory out of fantasy consideration in pretty much all formats.

outlooksByWeek.6: Skyler Bell remains without a catch in his rookie season with the Bills, who are set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Bell made his season debut in Week 5 with DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer both sidelined by shoulder injuries, drawing two unsuccessful targets. Buffalo wants to run as often as possible, which doesn't allow for a third or fourth pass-catching option to be relevant against a secondary that's allowing 9.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Bills in the fourth round of April's draft. Bell is an undersized, but versatile, receiver who finished 2025 second in the nation (first in this WR rookie class) in receiving yards (1,278) and, while he had a class-high 25 drops across 52 collegiate games, he was better in this area last season (five drops on 146 targets). Bell showed well at the combine, running a solid 4.40 40-yard dash and posting terrific marks in the vertical and broad jump. With DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir locked in atop Buffalo's WR depth chart, Bell will compete with Keon Coleman and Josh Palmer for work. He's only worth drafting in dynasty formats.

Beck was selected by the Cardinals in the third round of April's draft. Beck is a big, experienced quarterback who started for two seasons at Georgia prior to leading Miami to the national championship game last season. Beck paced this rookie QB class in completion percentage last season (72.4%) and for his career (69.5%), while also leading this group with an 80.9 QBR and 8.4 YPA during his 55-game collegiate career. He's unlikely to offer much with his legs in the pros, however, and will begin his career behind Jacoby Brissett and likely Gardner Minshew. Beck has no short-term fantasy value, though he could very well make some starts during his rookie season. Monitor him in superflex.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tory Horton is coming off his first catches of the season with Seattle set to host the Chargers in Week 4. Horton notched three catches on three targets for 48 yards in Sunday's Week 3 win over Washington, finishing as the Seahawks' third-leading pass catcher. However, his role makes for a limited fantasy ceiling at the moment, as he's logged less than one-third of Seattle's offensive snaps in each of his two games so far. The Chargers haven't done well against the pass this season, ranking 22nd in receiving yards allowed to wideouts through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tory Horton will look to get into the end zone for the second straight game when Seattle hosts San Francisco in Week 5. Horton caught just one pass against the Chargers in Week 4, but it was a six-yard touchdown. The second-year pro has otherwise struggled to make an impact so far in 2026, logging just four catches for 54 yards through three contests. His outlook isn't great against a San Francisco defense that has allowed the seventh-fewest receiving yards to wideouts so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tory Horton and the Seahawks host the undefeated Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 13 yards and returned one punt for 13 yards during Seattle's Week 6 overtime loss. Horton garnered his most looks of the season but wasn't able to make much of anything happen. The second-year wideout owns a 5-67-1 line on nine targets through five games in 2026. Despite the increased opportunities, Horton should remain on fantasy waiver wires versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Horton had the look of a Day 3 find by Seattle early on in 2025 prior to a season-ending shin injury suffered in Week 9. The 2025 fifth-round pick opened his career buried on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, but still found a way to make an impact while being limited to 46% of the offensive snaps. Though his production was volatile and he never cleared five targets in a game, he found the end zone five times on 23 targets. Despite the impressive showing, Horton's short-term outlook is dicey with JSN, Kupp and Rashid Shaheed presumably ahead of him on the depth chart. The 23-year-old's primary value is as a dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Whittington will look to improve upon a quiet season opener when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Whittington had just one catch for eight yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco. Still, he was the only Rams WR outside of stars Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to log a reception. Nacua and Adams stand to command most of QB Matthew Stafford's attention, so Whittington figures to compete for scraps with Los Angeles' tight ends and other depth wideouts each week. The Giants held Dallas' passing game in check in Week 1, as QB Dak Prescott tallied just 175 yards through the air, though he did toss two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Whittington (quadriceps) sat out the Rams' Week 2 win over the Giants and isn't certain to return for a Week 3 matchup against Denver. It was a missed opportunity Monday for Whittington, as top wideout Puka Nacua (hip) was also sidelined, opening the door for other WRs to take on a bigger role. Whittington was quiet in Week 1 against San Francisco with just one catch on one target for eight yards, and when both Nacua and Davante Adams are healthy, he figures to be competing with a variety of other pass catchers for targets. Should Whittington return in Week 3, he'll draw a tough Broncos secondary that has allowed a 51.6 percent catch rate to wideouts -- second best in the league -- so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Whittington will try to make more of an impact in the Rams' Week 5 battle against Buffalo. Whittington caught one of two targets for four yards in Week 4 against Philadelphia and has just two catches for 12 yards over three games this year. It may be hard for any wideout not named Puka Nacua or Davante Adams to log much production for Los Angeles when those star receivers are healthy given the amount of attention they draw from QB Matthew Stafford. However, there could be room for multiple Rams pass catchers to find success against a Buffalo defense that allowed four different Patriots players to log over 40 receiving yards in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Whittington continues to be a non-factor for the Rams heading into a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Whittington didn't log a target this past Monday against Buffalo, marking the second time through four games that he's finished without a single ball thrown his way. There doesn't appear to be many targets for Los Angeles wideouts behind stars Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and it doesn't help Whittington's outlook that QB Matthew Stafford has also frequently looked for his tight ends. With that said, Whittington isn't a desirable fantasy play in Week 6 despite the fact that the Cardinals have struggled to contain wideouts this season and have yielded the league's second-worst yards per target (10.17) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Whittington is one of several players who should be in line for more targets and touches in the Rams' passing attack after it was confirmed that Davante Adams will miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury. However, Whittington has recorded only two receptions for 12 yards through five games, making his projected increase in opportunities more speculative than established. The Raiders have been a below-average defense against pass-catchers in 2026 and have allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to WRs. However, it remains to be seen whether Whittington will handle the volume or even the opportunity to take advantage of that situation.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are established as lead backs, so there's an opportunity for Allen to force his way into a larger role. The 22-year-old is worth no more than a late-round flier.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He's off the fantasy radar.
