He'll face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Demond Claiborne should continue to be a secondary option at running back once again as Minnesota plays the Dolphins in Week 4. Dallas registered one carry for two yards in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. While his usage was low again, the veteran still appears slotted next to rookie Demond Claiborne in the RB totem pole behind Aaron Jones. Both could make the most of their action against a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeeJay Dallas will continue to be a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Dallas recorded zero carries against the Dolphins in Week 4, but he did log one catch for 10 yards. The veteran's role looks to be shrinking slightly even with Jordan Mason (toe) on IR, as rookie Demond Claiborne has now had three carries in back-to-back weeks. Dallas will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeeJay Dallas' status is up as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Dallas has recently served as a passing option out of the backfield with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, with a catch in back-to-back games entering Minnesota's bye week. Mason will return to practice this week, which puts Dallas' role in a weird spot, especially given that he's seen a small workload even with his position mate sidelined. Indianapolis has allowed the second-most receiving yards to RBs this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colbie Young and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 tilt against the Texans. The rookie fourth-round pick played just nine offensive snaps and did not record a target during Cincinnati's season-opening win. As long as Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, and Mike Gesicki are all healthy, Young's time on the field and opportunities will remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colbie Young and the Bengals travel to face the Steelers in Week 3. The rookie fourth-rounder caught his only target for seven yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston, giving him his first career reception in his second game. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, so Young remains firmly off the fantasy radar. In Week 3, he'll face a Steelers defense that ranks second, allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Colbie Young and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. Unfortunately, the rookie fourth-rounder has already been ruled out for that contest after suffering an injury in the first quarter of Cincinnati's Week 3 loss. Young caught his lone target for two yards before leaving the game. It sounds like the injury is not expected to be long-term, but the Bengals will take some time to evaluate the young receiver.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colbie Young and the Bengals are on the road to face the division-rival Ravens in Week 7. He sat out a second consecutive game in Week 5 thanks to a knee injury. There was some optimism about Young's return for Cincinnati's 31-24 victory prior to their bye week, so the hope is that he'll be ready to roll against the Ravens. However, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both healthy, the rookie wideout's role will likely be minimal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dyami Brown saw two targets in Week 1 for the Commanders. Unfortunately, he could not corral either target and went catchless in the opener. Meanwhile, rookie Antonio Williams looks to have cemented himself as the No. 3 wideout behind Scary Terry and Stefon Diggs with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown to lead Washington. That being said, there could be plenty of ball to go around in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that looked dreadful all of last season, as well as Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dyami Brown tied for second on the Commanders last game with six targets. That led to four catches for 21 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Brown and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dyami Brown only had one target for the Commanders last game. He did not record a catch. Brown is vying with Treylon Burks and Jaylin Lane for scraps in an offense currently led by backup quarterback Marcus Mariota.  Still, in Week 4, Washington will face an Indianapolis defense that has been rather poor against the pass in 2026.  The Colts are allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Klubnik was selected by the Jets in the fourth round of April's draft. Klubnik is an undersized, conservative quarterback who ranked last in this rookie class in aDOT (7.4), yards per completion (11.1), yards per attempt (7.1) and QB rating (136) during his collegiate tenure. He peaked with a 36-to-6 TD-to-INT showing in 2024, but fell to 16 TDs and six INTs in 2025. Klubnik does have a lot of experience (three years as a starter at Clemson) and could add value with his legs (totaled a 294-1,429-17 rushing line in his career), though he was extremely inefficient in the latter in 2025. Klubnik will handle No. 2 duties behind Geno Smith, but could handle some starts later in the year.

Benson was selected by the Raiders in the sixth round of April's draft. An accomplished sprinter, the speedy Benson has big play written all over him, though he's a slightly older prospect and his collegiate production was limited by a lot of changes in scenery (two years of community college followed by 2023 at Alabama, 2024 at Florida State and 2025 at Oregon). Benson never cleared a 15% target share in a single season, peaking with a 43-719-6 receiving line in 2025. Benson is a longshot as a sixth rounder, but the Raiders' shaky wide receiver depth chart presents him with an opportunity to quickly earn a role. Still, he's no more than a deep sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.5: Patrick Ricard has yet to see a carry this season for the Giants. The 300-lb fullback has served as the primary blocker for Cam Skattebo in this run-heavy offense. In Week 5, the G-Men will face a rather stingy Washington run defense. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Ricard has yet to see a carry this season for the Giants. The fullback continues to play a crucial role in the run game solely as a blocker. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league. Perhaps even Ricard can get in on the action.

player.seasonOutlook: Klare was selected by the Rams in the second round of April's draft. Klare is a receiving tight end who has experience playing in line and in the slot. He might not offer much as a blocker in the pros, but he showed his receiving ability at two different schools, posting a 51-685-4 line with Purdue in 2024 and a 43-448-2 line with Ohio State in 2025. Klare has the speed and athleticism to eventually emerge as a fantasy option, but hell begin his career in a crowded tight end room that also includes Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson. Klare is nowhere close to fantasy relevance at the moment.

outlooksByWeek.5: Sam Roush will look to keep his catch streak alive as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Roush stayed relevant in Chicago's passing game against the Jets in Week 4, taking his sole target for eight yards. The rookie tight end has now recorded a catch in three straight games, posting a 3-33-0 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Roush was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. Roush is a huge, in-line blocking tight end. Though he did catch 40-plus passes each of his final two seasons at Stanford (including a healthy 22% target share in 2025), his overall receiving efficiency was underwhelming (6.6 YPT, 1.22 YPRR) and he totaled four TDs on 182 career targets. He's unlikely to see enough target volume in the pros to find his way to the fantasy radar and that's especially the case in Chicago, as he's buried behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet.

outlooksByWeek.2: Olamide Zaccheaus is in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers. Carolina is coming off one of the worst defensive performances in recent memory, allowing 59 points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears. Despite Zaccheaus playing just 18 offensive snaps and catching his lone target last week, he could find value in this incredible matchup. Zaccheaus' value could depend on which quarterback starts for Atlanta as well, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) battling injuries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Zaccheaus played 29 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is 11 more than he did in Week 1. However, this didn't lead to an increase in production, as he caught just one of three targets for three yards. Zaccheaus could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix in Week 3, but he'll likely have to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant. Additionally, he could struggle against a Packers defense that's given up just 5.4 yards per pass attempt this season, the fifth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Zaccheaus played just 34 percent of Atlanta's offensive snaps in the Week 3 win over the Packers, catching both of his targets for nine yards. He's made fairly little impact on the Falcons' offense this season, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London accounting for nearly all of the team's production. Zaccheaus is in for a tough Week 4 matchup as well, as the Saints' defense has given up just 9.2 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to continue playing a depth role in Atlanta's wide-receiver room in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Despite the Falcons' offensive success since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, Zaccheaus has been less involved, catching just two of three targets for nine yards in two games. He remains firmly behind the likes of Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Jahan Dotson as a pass-catching option and likely won't fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. Even so, Zaccheaus is in for a favorable Week 5 matchup against a Ravens secondary that's given up 8.4 yards per targets to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to remain a depth piece in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Despite the Falcons' recent offensive success with the return of Michael Penix (ribs), Zaccheaus has been unproductive, catching just two of three targets for nine yards in his last three games. He's unlikely to have much fantasy value moving forward without finding the end zone. However, Zaccheaus is in for a favorable Week 6 matchup against a Bears defense that's given up a whopping 8.3 yards per target this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to remain a depth option in Atlanta's receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging a season-high four targets in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, Zaccheaus went without a reception for the third consecutive week. He's unlikely to have fantasy value without finding the end zone, especially in a tough Week 7 matchup against a 49ers defense that's given up just four touchdowns to WRs through five contests this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Moore and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. On Monday, Baltimore reverted him to their practice squad, despite the receiver finishing second on the team with 53 yards on one catch. However, with Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane doubtful with a fractured wrist, Moore has a solid chance of being elevated to the active roster ahead of their tilt against New Orleans. He could be a name to monitor, with WR Devontez Walker (groin) also considered questionable to play.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Moore and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 road tilt against the Cowboys. He caught one of three targets for six yards and garnered 108 yards on four kick returns during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. Moore enjoyed a slight uptick in playing time with Zay Flowers (hamstring) out, as he was on the field for 31 offensive snaps compared to 25 in the season opener. Flowers is expected to return in Week 3, but even if he remains sidelined, Moore's limited involvement on offense takes him out of any fantasy consideration.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Moore and the Ravens return home from Brazil to host the Titans in Week 4. The 33-year-old brought in his only target for a four-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 34-31 victory in Week 3, his first of the season. Moore has now had one reception in all three outings, earning him a 3-63-1 line on six targets. Tennessee's defense is vulnerable through the air, as it ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs, but Moore's limited involvement in a run-heavy offense should keep him firmly on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Moore and the Ravens are on the road to battle the Falcons in Week 5. After sitting out Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4, he'll look to return to the field against an Atlanta defense allowing 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs. Prior to his absence, Moore had one reception in all three outings and caught a touchdown versus the Cowboys in Week 3. As the fourth or fifth receiver on a run-heavy offense, he should be left on waiver wires despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Moore and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He returned from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury but did not draw a target during Baltimore's Week 5 overtime win. Moore has a 3-63-1 receiving line on six targets across four games so far this season. He should remain on fantasy waiver wires for the Week 6 matchup versus Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.4) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tai Felton will look to get more chances in Minnesota's passing game against Chicago in Week 2. Felton garnered zero targets in a Week 1 win over the Packers, but he was on the field with the offense, which could contribute to some looks in the coming weeks. Veteran Carson Wentz played under center for most of the game, and Vikings receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings both did not record a catch. Given that Wentz could serve as the quarterback again, Felton could fill a niche in the passing game behind Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. The Bears defense also allowed the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game even more.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tai Felton will aim to stay involved as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. After being on the field for five percent or fewer of offensive snaps in Weeks 1 and 2, Felton saw a major boost in Week 3 with 57 percent and garnered two targets. The second-year wide receiver did benefit from the departure of Justin Jefferson, but this uptick in usage could level out even with the return of the Vikings' star. Felton will seek to get his first catch of the year against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers so far.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tai Felton will seek to stay involved as Minnesota travels to play the Saints in Week 5. Felton benefited from star wideout Justin Jefferson being inactive in Week 4, logging his first catch of the season for 14 yards. The second-year pass catcher could be at a disadvantage this week, as Jefferson is aiming for a return. New Orleans has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tai Felton will seek to stay involved as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Felton stayed involved in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye week, bringing in two of three targets for 27 yards. After recording zero catches in the first three games of the season, the second-year wide receiver has now brought in three catches for 41 yards in his last two outings. He'll now face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Delp was selected by the Saints in the third round of April's draft. Delp was busy during his final three seasons at Georgia (1,733 snaps in 42 games), but that didn't lead to much work in the passing game (no more than 24 catches, 284 yards or a 7% target share in a single season). Good speed and hands suggest there's some hope for him as a developmental piece, which is what he'll be in 2026 while playing a situational role behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant.

outlooksByWeek.6: Tim Patrick is unlikely to contribute prominently for the Jets in Week 6 against New England, despite the team's banged-up secondary receivers. Patrick made his season debut in Week 5, catching two of three targets for 26 yards-minimal usage despite a 92% snap share. In a run-centric offense, Patrick is unlikely to garner enough looks to produce against a secondary that's allowing 7.5 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tim Patrick remains in a limited role for the Jets' passing offense entering Week 7 against the Dolphins. Patrick has garnered three targets in each of the last two weeks while Adonai Mitchell remains sidelined, but hasn't emerged as a secondary option behind Garrett Wilson. He now faces further competition for targets with Omar Cooper healthy. Given that Miami is allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts through five games, Patrick's lack of volume does not suggest a fantasy-worthy profile.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenen Thompson was on the field for just 10 offensive snaps in his NFL debut and failed to get a target in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. The fourth-round speedster could still end up being useful in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, but the whole unit is still adjusting. Top wideout Ladd McConkey left the game early with a rib injury, and if he misses additional time, it could open the door for Thompson to take on a bigger role, although he would still likely be behind Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris in the pecking order. In Week 2, Thompson will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenen Thompson began to work into the offense a little more in Week 2, notching his first three targets and catching one of them for 13 yards. That usage may have been due to Ladd McConkey nursing a rib injury, but Thompson's elite speed could earn a consistent spot in OC Mike McDaniel's quick-strike game plan if he shows he can get open against NFL defenders. Thompson will try to keep building chemistry with QB Justin Herbert in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenen Thompson was unable to suit up in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills due to a quadriceps strain, denying him a chance to continue earning a larger role in the passing game. The fourth-round rookie has the speed offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel craves, but Thompson is behind Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris on the depth chart, and even once he's healthy he's unlikely to work his way into significant volume. If he's able to return in Week 4, Thompson will get a daunting matching against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenen Thompson has missed the Chargers' last two games with a quadriceps strain, but if the rookie speedster is cleared to return soon, a big opportunity could be awaiting. Ladd McConkey is dealing with both rib and foot injuries and seems set to miss time, while Quentin Johnston has been disappointing once again. Thompson logged three targets in Week 2, his last healthy game, and he could get even higher volume if he returns in Week 5 to face a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brenen Thompson has missed the Chargers' last three games with a quadriceps injury, but with injuries piling up all over the wide receiver room, the rookie speedster could get thrust into a significant role as soon as he's cleared to return. In his last healthy game back in Week 2, Thompson logged three targets from Justin Herbert, catching one for 13 yards, but with the entire offense struggling under coordinator Mike McDaniel, no one has a particularly enticing ceiling. If Thompson is cleared to return in Week 6, he'll face a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Thompson was selected by the Chargers in the fourth round of April's draft. Thompson is an extremely small and very fast (4.26 40-yard dash) receiver who posted a rookie-class-high 18.5 YPR during his career and handled a massive 43% of Mississippi State's air yards last season. He didn't see much work prior to 2025, however, and figures to operate as a situational deep threat in the pros. He'll battle second-years Tre Harris and KeAndre Lamber-Smith for occasional looks behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston this season.

Cuevas was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. Cuevas wasn't targeted much during three collegiate seasons at Washington and Alabama (57-793-6, 5% target share), but he was effective when called on, averaging 10.4 yards per target. He's a bit of a tweener and underwhelmed athletically at the combine, but can help as a blocker and receiver. He'll battle fellow rookie Matthew Hibner for snaps behind Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe this season.

outlooksByWeek.6: Charlie Kolar returned in Week 5 from a two-game absence due to a forearm injury, and the tight end wound up leading the Chargers with 37 receiving yards while catching three of four targets. His workload as a blocker figures to remain high as the team once again deals with injuries to its offensive line, but a depleted wide receiver room and coordinator Mike McDaniel's apparent unwillingness to deploy Oronde Gadsden could result in increased target volume for Kolar. He is an intriguing dart throw in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Oliver will seek to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game at Chicago in Week 2. Oliver was an unlikely contributor against the Packers in Week 1, logging two catches for 22 yards and ranking third on the team in targets (four). With veteran Carson Wentz also very likely to serve under center once again, the seventh-year tight end could be in line for more targets. He'll face a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Panthers tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Oliver will aim to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game against Tampa Bay in Week 3. Oliver stayed active in a low-scoring Week 2 win against the Bears, reeling in his sole target for a 24-yard gain. The supplementary tight end has now amassed three catches for 46 yards off five targets in his first two outings. He'll take on a New York defense that's allowed a third-lowest 6.0 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Oliver was announced to be out for the season with a torn biceps ahead of Minnesota's Week 4 matchup against Miami. Oliver was looking to be a high-upside option in deeper leagues after three catches for 46 yards across two games and staying involved as a blocker. The veteran tight end will instead focus on rehabbing for the 2027 season, which should open up opportunities for T.J. Hockenson even more.

Braxton Berrios and Odell Beckham have been vying for the No. 4 wideout role on the Giants, though neither has a catch to date on the young season. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for both players. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Braxton Berrios suffered a foot injury last game for the Giants. Primarily a returner, Berrios was targeted once in the passing game, though could not corral the target. Charlie Jones would likely continue to serve as the primary returner if Berrios misses Week 5 versus the Commanders. If Berrios can somehow suit up, he will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.6: Teagan Quitoriano will look to build upon a surprising Week 5 performance when the Cardinals visit the Rams in Week 6. In Quitoriano's 2026 debut this past Sunday versus Detroit, he caught both of his targets for 15 yards and two touchdowns. The pair of catches were his first since the 2023 campaign, and he trails both star TE Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins in the pecking order, so Quitoriano will be hard-pressed to repeat that two-TD performance moving forward. He'll have a particularly tough task against the Rams, who have allowed a meager 19.8 receiving yards per game to tight ends so far, by far the top mark in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Kacmarek was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Kacmarek is a massive, strong blocking tight end who won't see much receiving work in the pros. He's likely to play a lot of snap as a rookie considering Miami's shaky roster, but Greg Dulcich is expected to operate as the team's top pass-catcher at the tight end position. Kacmarek is no more than the deepest of deep sleepers.

Daniels was selected by the Rams in the sixth round of April's draft. It helped that he played in 68 games across six seasons at Liberty, LSU and Miami, but Daniels ranked third in this WR rookie class in receiving yards (2,991) and second in TD receptions (28) for his career. His overall efficiency was good, though he failed to emerge as anything more than a secondary target once he left Liberty. Daniels will battle for a roster spot and is no more than a dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.6: J. Michael Sturdivant could see an elevated role as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Sturdivant has seen volatile usage so far this season, with just three catches for 22 yards, all of which came in a pass-heavy loss to the Falcons in Week 3. Still, the rookie wide receiver may be in line for more opportunities with Skyy Moore dealing with an ankle injury. Sturdivant remains a depth option, but he could record his best game yet against a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Boerkircher was selected by the Jaguars in the second round of April's draft. Boerkircher is a blocking tight end who handled a 3% target share (lowest in this rookie TE class) across 52 collegiate games (five seasons). He aligned in the slot 30% of the time and posted a 1.04 YPRR, both of which are lowest in this TE group. He'll file in as a blocking complement to starter Brenton Strange and is not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.7: Ben Skowronek and the Steelers travel to face the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He missed Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime victory in Week 6 due to a calf injury he suffered in Week 5. Skowronek's practice status will bear monitoring leading up to the contest with New Orleans. However, only two wide receivers, DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard, recorded receptions in the OT win, meaning Skowronek can remain on fantasy waiver wires until further notice.

player.seasonOutlook: Nowakowski was selected by the Steelers in the fifth round of April's draft. Nowakowski is a bit undersized with very small hands, but he's a capable blocker and, after totaling 18 catches in 36 games at Wisconsin, made a little bit of a leap as a pass catcher in 2025 (his lone season at Indiana), posting a 32-387-2 receiving line. He's expected to play fullback and offer some tight end depth behind Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington.

Rudolph is expected to return as the clipboard holder in Pittsburgh, with Aaron Rodgers back as the starter. The veteran quarterback has never appeared in more than 10 games in a single season and made just one start in 2025 (he threw for 171 yards and one TD on 31 attempts). Rudolph has thrown 30 touchdowns and 22 interceptions in his six-year career, and isn't much of a rushing threat (career 75-209-1). The 31-year-old wouldn't even be a QB2 option in superflex if called on to start.

outlooksByWeek.7: Gavin Bartholomew could see elevated usage again as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. After a quiet start to the season, Bartholomew recorded an impressive five catches for 33 yards in Week 5 against the Saints after teammate T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion early. The rookie's opportunities are directly contingent on if Hockenson can suit up this week, but he is worth monitoring given Kyler Murray's affinity towards tight ends in his career. Indianapolis has ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy TEs on the year.

outlooksByWeek.4: Kameron Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. The third-year wideout has played just six offensive snaps through Tampa Bay's first three games this season. However, he's expected to have more opportunities in the near future, with Jalen McMillan (knee) set to miss time. Despite the increased opportunities, Johnson will likely struggle finding fantasy value, as he'll likely operate as the team's WR4 without Baker Mayfield (thumb) at the helm. The matchup is favorable, though, as Green Bay's defense has allowed 8.6 yards per target to wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Shavers tore his ACL in the playoffs and is unlikely to make a fantasy impact once back on the field in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.5: Mitchell Tinsley and the Bengals are on the road to square off against the Dolphins in Week 5. He caught three of seven targets for 49 yards in Cincinnati's Week 4 loss after the team signed him from Houston's practice squad leading up to the contest. Tinsley finished fourth in targets and tied for fourth in receptions while establishing chemistry with Joe Burrow in his debut. There's a real possibility he could operate as the No. 2 or 3 receiver for the Bengals with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) all questionable versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling had his first meaningful action of the season in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, playing 26 offensive snaps but failing to catch his only target. Ladd McConkey is battling both rib and foot injuries and seems set to miss time, while rookie Brenan Thompson has missed the last two weeks with a quadriceps strain. This could open the door for Valdes-Scantling to fill the No. 3 receiver role behind Quentin Johnson and Tre' Harris. If he does, the veteran deep threat might be able to hit a big play or two in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marquez Valdes-Scantling was pressed into a starting role for the Chargers in Week 5 due to the absences of Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, and the veteran wide receiver caught two of three targets for 22 yards. Valdes-Scantling has been a deep-ball specialist during his career, but with Justin Herbert just trying to stay upright behind a patchwork offensive line, the QB doesn't have a lot of time to let downfield routes develop. Even if Valdes-Scantling gets a big workload again in Week 6, it's unlikely to result in much production against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Homer and the Steelers take on the division rival Bengals at home in Week 3. He rushed twice for 16 yards after filling in for Rico Dowdle, who was forced out of the contest with a toe injury. With Dowdle questionable to play against Cincinnati, Homer could be elevated into a backup role once again. He was reverted to the practice squad on Monday, but he's expected to be back on Pittsburgh's roster for Sunday's contest. However, as long as Jaylen Warren is healthy, Homer's role will be limited against the Bengals first-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Homer and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns in Week 4. He recorded one carry for no gain and was not targeted during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3 as Jaylen Warren's backup. With Rico Dowdle (toe) in jeopardy of missing his second straight contest, Homer is in line for the No. 2 RB role once again. However, Warren should handle the bulk of touches out of the backfield versus Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Green was selected by the Browns in the sixth round of April's draft. Green is a huge, aggressive dual-threat quarterback. He's a major threat with his legs (112-999-8 rushing last season) but a work in progress as a passer, as he completed only 61% of his passes and threw 11 INTs on only 326 attempts in 2025. Green's size and athleticism (which included a 4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) supplies him with massive upside, but he'll need to improve as a passer in order to find a starting opportunity. He'll continue to compete for playing time with Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel.

Burks was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. Burks is a small receiver who has experience as both a primary perimeter receiver (under 25% slot in 2023 and 2025) and a primary slot (over 80% slot in 2022 and 2024). He had productive seasons at both Purdue and Oklahoma, though his overall efficiency is fairly poor across the board. That includes an ugly 6.4 YPT and 1.37 YPRR, both of which rank near the basement of this rookie WR class. He showed very well athletically at the combine, including a 4.30 40-yard dash and class-best marks in the vertical (42.5) and bench press (26 reps). Burks is a longshot for 2026 fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.4: Ke'Shawn Williams and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He played no offensive snaps but generated 131 yards on five kick returns on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss and also lost a fumble. Williams remains off the fantasy radar, but with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) set to miss the contest against Jacksonville, he could earn some additional opportunities as a fourth receiver.

player.seasonOutlook: Klein was selected by the Texans in the second round of April's draft. He's an inexperienced, blocking tight end who posted an ugly 5.5 YPT and 57.6% catch rate in his collegiate career. Klein peaked with a 24-248-1 receiving line in 2025 and now joins a Texans' offense that already includes Dalton Schultz, Cade Stover and Foster Moreau at the tight end position. Klein may be Houston's tight end of the future, but he won't be on the fantasy radar as a rookie.

Leonard is expected to operate as the Colts' No. 2 quarterback this season. It's a notable designation, as starter Daniel Jones continues to recover from a torn Achilles suffered in Week 14 last season. Should Jones miss time to begin the 2026 season, Leonard is positioned to start. Leonard made one start as a rookie, throwing for 270 yards and two touchdowns and rushing for 21 yards and an additional score, primarily against Houston's backup defense in Week 18. The 2025 sixth-round pick adds value with his legs, but he'd be no more than a fringe QB2 even if called on to start.

outlooksByWeek.4: Alec Ingold took advantage of a rash of tight end injuries to catch three of four targets for 35 yards in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. The veteran fullback has yet to get a carry this season, but his blocking ability makes him a better fit to handle the kinds of assignments Charlie Kolar and David Njoku were getting in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, rather than receiving TE Oronde Gadsden. Ingold has shown some aptitude as a pass catcher in the past, but his primary role will still be to protect Justin Herbert and open holes for the running game. Ingold will be a TD-dependent dart throw in Week against a Seahawks defense that has given up 14 receptions to RBs this season, tied for 17th in the league, and which has allowed a combined three receiving touchdowns to RBs and TEs through three games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jimmy Horn will likely play a minimal offensive role in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1. Horn had a poor Week 1 performance despite not receiving an offensive touch, as the second-year wideout had a costly fumble on a punt return that helped set up a Bears touchdown. He's not expected to see much volume or be very involved in Carolina's offensive game plan going forward, especially with the emergence of Jalen Coker (ankle). Horn is also in for a tough divisional matchup in Week 2, with the Falcons' defense allowing just 6.5 yards per target to WRs last week.

outlooksByWeek.5: Dareke Young's role in the Raiders' offense could increase as injuries mount in the wide receiver room. The former Seahawk's familiarity with Klint Kubiak hasn't translated into much work as a pass catcher, as he's split his time between special teams and the offense, but he saw multiple targets for the first time in 2026 during a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. With Jack Bech on the shelf due to a fractured forearm and Jalen Nailor now in the concussion protocol, Young could line up as Las Vegas' No. 3 WR in Week 5 against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

player.seasonOutlook: Nussmeier was selected by the Chiefs in the seventh round of April's draft. Nussmeier is an undersized, pocket quarterback and older prospect. He was extremely conservative last season, posting rookie-class-low marks in aDOT (6.4), YPA (6.7) and YPC (9.9). Aside of his ability to avoid sacks (career 3.40% sack rate), Nussmeier's efficiency isn't overly impressive and he's a nonfactor as a rusher (career 33-179-5 line and a class-low 1.4 carries per game). Nussmeier will handle No. 3 duties behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields.

Payton was selected by the Eagles in the fifth round of April's draft. Payton is a big, dual-threat quarterback who started only one season at North Dakota State and totaled more rushing (31) than passing (21) touchdowns during his five collegiate seasons. Lacking arm strength and with little experience, especially at the FCS level, he'll likely require plenty of development. He likely max out as an emergency third quarterback in 2026.

Joly was selected by the Broncos in the fifth round of April's draft, but was later waived and claimed by Miami. Joly is a highly productive receiving tight end who ranked near the top of this rookie TE class in all receiving counting stats (166-1,978-15) and target share (17%) during 50 collegiate games at UConn and NC State. He's not much of a blocker, but he could stretch the seam as a move tight end in the pros. Joly may one day emerge as a receiving option, but it's going to take some time.

outlooksByWeek.7: Reggie Virgil is considered the No. 4 wideout in the Cardinals' rotation, but his contributions haven't been meaningful so far. The former Texas Tech standout has two catches on five targets for 29 yards this season, and he didn't see a single target in Week 6 against the Rams, so it's hard to imagine a scenario in which he has a prominent role in a Week 7 matchup against the Broncos. That's because Denver has been excellent against the pass this season, and its defense has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing WRs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Virgil was selected by the Cardinals in the fifth round of April's draft. Virgil is a tall, thin, perimeter, vertical receiver who ranked near the top of this WR rookie class in aDOT (14.7) and YPR (15.8) but near the basement in RAC (4.5), catch rate (54%) and YPRR (1.79) during his career at Miami Ohio and Texas Tech. A class-high 48% of his targets came on deep routes, though he played a more well-rounded role in 2025 -- his lone season with the Red Raiders. Virgil ran a 4.57 40-yard dash at 187 pounds at the combine, which works out to a poor speed score of 86. Virgil will battle Kendrick Bourne for No. 3 duties behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson. He's off the short-term fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.5: Mark Redman will look to build off a solid outing as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Redman started the season with zero catches across three games, but he brought in both of his two targets for 29 yards in Week 4 at Tampa Bay. It appears Redman could continue to carve out a role in Green Bay's passing game, especially with the lack of production from depth receivers Skyy Moore and Bo Melton. Chicago's defense has ranked top five against fantasy TEs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Law was selected by the Lions in the fifth round of April's draft. Law is a short-area/slot target who played a limited role in three seasons at Alabama (33 catches in 34 games) prior to delivering a 53-540-3 receiving line at Kentucky last season. Law's career 4.2 aDOT is lowest in this WR rookie class, but his 9.1 RAC and 78% catch rate rank first. He'll battle for a returner/depth receiver role and isn't a fantasy option.

Henderson was selected by the Seahawks in the sixth round of April's draft. Henderson is a thin receiver with small hands who has experience playing inside and out (career 38% slot rate). A converted running back, Henderson was limited to five catches in three seasons at Alabama prior to making a leap to a 45-766-5 receiving line (22% target share) in his lone season at Kansas. Henderson was cut in late August and will attempt to work his way back onto an active roster.

Miller was selected by the Patriots in the seventh round of April's draft. Miller has decent size, but he has struggled with effectiveness, posting a 4.57 YPC (worst in this rookie class) during his collegiate career (including an ugly 3.88 in 2025). Poor tackle breaking and YAC numbers give him perhaps the worst efficiency profile in this RB class, and he hasn't shown much in the passing game (career 40-336-2 line). He ran a solid 4.42 40-yard dash at the combine but posted the worst marks in this RB class in the vertical and broad jump. He didn't make the initial 53-man roster, but will look to stick on the practice squad.

Koziol was selected by the Jaguars in the fifth round of April's draft. Across 49 collegiate games at Houston and Ball State, Koziol produced 349 targets, 237 receptions, 2,234 yards, 24 TDs, a 23% target share and a 24% air yard share. All six stats easily top this TE rookie class and that production included a massive 94-839-8 showing in 2024. Koziol has work to do as a blocker, but his size and production suggest there's clear receiving upside. He's worth stashing in dynasty, but doesn't have a path to short-term value behind Brenton Strange and likely fellow rookie Nick Boerkircher.

Carr reportedly considered a return after sitting out the 2025 season, but did not end up signing with a team. He played pretty well during his two-year run with the Saints (including finishing in the top 12 in completion percentage, YPA and QBR in 2024), but injuries cost him seven games in 2024 and he remained an underwhelming fantasy option. Even after a strong start to that 2024 season (21-plus fantasy points in Weeks 1 and 2), Carr ended up contributing 15.1 fantasy PPG in 10 games, which ranked 19th for the season. Incredibly, that matches his best fantasy showing since his career-best 10th in 2016. Carr is a solid passer, but he simply doesn't run enough (below 110 yards in four straight seasons, with one TD during the span) to provide high-end fantasy output.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Wayne drew seven targets in Week 2 as the Texans played without top WR Nico Collins (hamstring). Wayne could be an option for desperate deep-league fantasy managers in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the league. If Collins sits again, Wayne will join Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel as the only healthy options in Houston's WR room. Wayne caught only two of his seven targets in Week 2 against the Bengals, and he has only 65 career receiving yards in six games across three seasons in Houston.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Wayne has caught only four of 12 targets for 65 yards heading into Houston's Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The third-year pro has had opportunities in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), but even if Collins remains sidelined in Week 4, Wayne hasn't shown much to suggest he deserves consideration for fantasy lineups. Wayne has yet to score a TD in his career, and only three of the Cowboys' 10 total TDs allowed this season have been scored by WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Royer was selected by the Browns in the fifth round of April's draft. After barely seeing the field during three seasons at Ohio State, Royer broke out with a 50-522-3 receiving line (21% target share) in 2024, prior to dipping to 29-416-4 (10%) in 2025. He has solid size with big hands and could emerge as a versatile depth option. Once back on the field, he'll compete for reps behind Harold Fannin Jr. this season.

outlooksByWeek.5: Sterling Shepard hasn't factored in the Jets' minimal passing game ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Browns. Shepard has just one target over two weeks since being elevated from the practice squad, seemingly overtaking Malik McClain for the team's fourth receiver role. In an offense that can sustain two receivers at most, Shepard appears unlikely to pop against a defense that's allowing 8.8 yards per target to opposing wide outs.

outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Smith and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference tilt in Week 6. He was elevated from Pittsburgh's practice squad ahead of their Week 5 victory, but he did not record a target during his 15 snaps on offense (28%). With receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) already ruled out against Tampa Bay, Smith could see another increase in playing time. However, with the offense running through Jaylen Warren, Germie Bernard, DK Metcalf, and tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, Smith should remain on fantasy waiver wires.

player.seasonOutlook: Levis is entering his fourth NFL season. Levis, who missed all of 2025 with a shoulder injury, was the Titans' starter for most of his first two seasons, but simply wasn't up to the task. He totaled 21 pass TDs and 16 INTs in 21 games, while not adding much with his legs (240 yards and one TD). In 2024, he appeared in only 12 games (nine full) and still finished in the top seven in INTs and times sacked. Levis is aggressive (he ranked in the top five in average depth of throw both seasons), but the lack of efficiency and rushing contributions keeps him well off the fantasy radar. He'll barely be worth an add in superflex leagues, even if given the chance to start.

outlooksByWeek.3: Arian Smith has an extremely limited role for the Jets heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Lions. He has been bumped up to No. 4 on the team's depth chart following Omar Cooper being placed on IR, but Smith still logged just one offensive snap in Week 2. With wideouts Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, capable tight ends, and solid running backs, the Jets offense can't support much more, even in an inviting matchup with a Detroit secondary that's allowed the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Endries was selected by the Bengals in the seventh round of April's draft. Endries is a pass-catching/move tight end who caught 33-plus passes during each of his three collegiate seasons. He peaked with a 56-623-3 receiving line with Fernando Mendoza under center at Cal in 2024 prior to seeing less work in an in-line role at Texas last season. Endries will compete for the No. 3 gig in Cincinnati and isn't close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.5: Kevin Austin could play a depth role in New Orleans' wide-receiver corps in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Austin played just 12% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, suggesting he's firmly behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance in the WR corps. Austin likely won't be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone, which is a tough task against a Vikings secondary that's given up just three receiving touchdowns to wideouts all season.

outlooksByWeek.3: KhaDarel Hodge may be asked to step into a larger role for the 49ers in Week 3 versus Arizona. Hodge has just one catch (on one target) for 18 yards so far this season, but he logged 17 offensive snaps Sunday versus Miami after playing just one snap in Week 1. San Francisco will likely be without No. 3 wideout Demarcus Robinson (ankle) against the Cardinals, and No. 1 WR Mike Evans picked up a hip injury Week 2, leaving the door open for Hodge to get more opportunities. Through two weeks, Arizona ranks in the bottom half of the league in most categories versus wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Bentley was selected by the Broncos in the seventh round of April's draft. Bentley is a big, in-line tight end who, after catching three passes during his first two seasons (18 games) at Utah, exploded for a 23% target share and 48-620-6 receiving line in 2025 (13 games). Bentley figures to focus primarily on blocking in the pros, but his 2025 pass-catching work suggests there's some hope for fantasy relevance in future seasons.

outlooksByWeek.4: Malik McClain seems to be a non-factor in the Jets' receiving rotation ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bears. Elevated to the active roster following Omar Cooper being placed on injured reserve, McClain didn't record a target in Week 3 while playing 26% of the team's snaps. It seems highly unlikely he'll garner enough looks to exploit a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing wideouts.
